api/dbtools.Core.Failure.FailureReport.h.title: Class FailureReport | dbtools
api/dbtools.Core.Failure.FailureReport.h.summary: Class FailureReport Namespace dbtools.Core.Failure Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Shows each failure once. A handler that shows a failure banner records it with the exception; an outer handler that receives the same exception only logs it. The banner system keeps every request it accepts (see NotificationBannerService), so a request counts as shown when it is made. public static class FailureReport Inheritance object FailureReport Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The outermost SafeExecutor run of an asynchronous flow opens a report scope; nested runs use its records. A run that rethrows to its caller hands its record on to the window error boundary, which takes it once. A later run ignores and removes a record that another run handed on, so a failure its caller cached and throws again is shown again. Tool code that shows its own banner and rethrows records the failure for its next handler. Methods ShowBanner(IWindowErrorBanner, Exception, string, string) Shows a failure banner and records it, for tool code that rethrows the failure afterwards. public static void ShowBanner(IWindowErrorBanner notifier, Exception failure, string title, string message) Parameters notifier IWindowErrorBanner failure Exception title string message string TakeShown(Exception) For a last handler that would show its own banner: returns true, and takes the record, when an earlier handler already showed this failure. public static bool TakeShown(Exception failure) Parameters failure Exception Returns bool

TryWrite(Action write, string context) Parameters write Action The diagnostic write. context string Names the write in the Serilog.Debugging.SelfLog report. Returns Exception null after a successful write. After a failed write, the write's exception when Serilog.Debugging.SelfLog returns, also when it is disabled. api/dbtools.Core.Notifications.Notificat.summary: Class NotificationBannerService Namespace dbtools.Core.Notifications.NotificationBanner Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Shows banner rows in a strip across the top of the supplied owner window. public static class NotificationBannerService Inheritance object NotificationBannerService Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Presentation uses IToolWindowSession. On the owner dispatcher's thread, owner resolution and presentation finish before return. Their exceptions propagate to the caller. Other threads queue delivery and return immediately. Delivery failures are logged without propagating to the caller. Dispatcher selection can throw on any thread. A zero owner HWND, missing anchor position, retired host or host reset suppresses presentation and returns an inert handle. A returned handle therefore does not confirm presentation. Disposing the handle before delivery cancels presentation. Rows use these default deadlines: success 3 s, info 5 s, warning 8 s, error 10 s. Prompts have no automatic deadline. Rows with actions use their kind's deadline too; a successful action can close one early when CloseOnSuccess is true (the default). A running action defers expiry, requested dismissal and last-handle release until it finishes. A request with the same key as an open row updates that row. Without a key, a request updates an open row only when kind, title, message and action presence match. An update restarts its deadline when the kind has one; an exact repeat shows a count. api/dbtools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGat.summary: Interface IRevitCallGate Namespace dbtools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGate Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Unified entry point for executing Revit API callbacks either inline (modal) or queued (modeless). public interface IRevitCallGate Remarks Null work delegates and rejected delegate shapes throw from the call itself. Failures after argument validation, including cancellation, mode or context refusal, callback failure, and erased awaitable-result rejection, are delivered through the returned task. Cancellation completes the task as Canceled. An OperationCanceledException thrown by a gate check or work delegate is rethrown; cancellation observed by the queued host surfaces as a TaskCanceledException. Properties InGate True when currently executing within a call-gate callback on the Revit UI thread. bool InGate { get; } Property Value bool RunsInline True when every accepted callback runs synchronously inside the calling API turn. bool RunsInline { get; } Property Value bool Remarks This is a fixed property of the gate. It grants no Revit API authority and does not describe the current InGate state. Methods RunAsync(Action<UIApplication>, CancellationToken, RevitCallGateMode) Executes the work delegate on the Revit UI thread. Null work and async-state-machine Action delegates throw from the call before execution. Task RunAsync(Action<UIApplication> work, CancellationToken ct = default, RevitCallGateMode mode = RevitCallGateMode.Auto) Parameters work Action<UIApplication> ct CancellationToken mode RevitCallGateMode Returns Task Remarks Queued work that has not started when the owning call-gate task retires is dropped, and its task never completes, even if its cancellation token is canceled later. Callers must not await or block on such a task during shutdown. Failed-startup cleanup cancels pending work instead. RunAsync<T>(Func<UIApplication, T>, CancellationToken, RevitCallGateMode) Executes the work delegate on the Revit UI thread and returns a result. Task<T> RunAsync<T>(Func<UIApplication, T> work, CancellationToken ct = default, RevitCallGateMode mode = RevitCallGateMode.Auto) Parameters work Func<UIApplication, T> ct CancellationToken mode RevitCallGateMode Returns Task<T> Type Parameters T Remarks Task and ValueTask result shapes and reference-typed multicast result delegates throw from the call before execution. An erased Task or boxed ValueTask result (for example, a Task returned as object or an interface) is rejected only after the work runs. Its side effects remain, and any started Task continues running. Other awaitable types (for example, ConfigureAwait results and custom awaiters) are not detected. Queued work that has not started when the owning call-gate task retires is dropped, and its task never completes, even if its cancellation token is canceled later. Callers must not await or block on such a task during shutdown. Failed-startup cleanup cancels pending work instead.

api/dbtools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters..summary: Class SharedParameterFamilyMigration Namespace dbtools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Moves family parameters to target definitions and, for opted-in targets, direct annotation labels. public sealed class SharedParameterFamilyMigration Inheritance object SharedParameterFamilyMigration Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A loaded family keeps its own definition of a shared parameter. Its formulas, dimension labels and annotation labels refer to the parameter by GUID, so a project that replaces its own parameter leaves them on the old GUID. Deleting that parameter from the project also removes it from the labels of loaded families. Callers therefore run this migration before Migrate(Document, ParameterElement, ExternalDefinition, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, SharedParameterUseHandling) or any delete of the old parameter. Plan(Document, IReadOnlyList<SharedParameterFamilyTarget>) changes nothing. It opens each editable loadable family that may use a target and closes it unsaved. It also opens editable nested families recursively. A non-editable nested family is checked through its symbols and instances. Every SharedParameterFamilyTarget defaults to refusing a direct shared-parameter element that no family parameter carries. GM repair opts in to direct label moves. In Revit 2027, that path requires readable labels, the internal writer members, the target's spec, a non-measurable spec, no family record of the target GUID with another spec, no detail group type without placements, and no nested or uninspected family use. A label in a plain detail group moves after the change ungroups the group; an attached, nested or pinned group, a group with a member whose location cannot be read, or one with an assigned value that ungrouping would delete, refuses. It trials all changes for one family together, in apply order, in a transaction that commits with the failure handling of Migrate(Document, SharedParameterFamilyPlan) inside a transaction group that always rolls back. A family parameter still uses FamilyManager.ReplaceParameter(FamilyParameter, string, ForgeTypeId, bool) and Revit moves its label entries. This path does not require dbtools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters.SharedParameterLabels.CanWrite. A failed family-parameter trial is a family refusal. A failed direct-label trial remains a hand-fix label row. Revit 2026 refuses direct shared-parameter elements because it cannot read annotation labels. Other refusals: a nested shared family, another data type, a type parameter in a category that the target binds as an instance parameter, an element whose old and new values differ, and an in-place or non-editable top-level family that defines the parameter or may define it. Revit does not open such a family; when its elements show the parameter and a project binding could explain that, the plan rebinds the project parameter without the family's category in a transaction that always rolls back and reads the elements again. Migrate(Document, SharedParameterFamilyPlan) runs in one transaction group. A family that was reloaded or deleted after the plan refuses. Before writing, it opens each family and compares the planned label state, including label IDs, group membership and group type. A changed label refuses before the family write. For each family it records the old values of its types or elements, opens the family, replaces the parameter through a temporary family parameter (FamilyManager.ReplaceParameter(FamilyParameter, string, ForgeTypeId, bool), then the target definition) with the same group and instance or type kind, and checks in the family that every formula, value, dimension label, associated element parameter and label entry follows. For direct label changes it updates only the selected entries through the internal parameter-ID setter, validates them and checks their public formatting and the internal leading-parameter flag. It refuses measurable specs because Revit does not expose the label's unit format for comparison. It also checks for a remaining family parameter, nested-family symbol or instance, or readable label that uses the old GUID. Project view-filter rules are handled by FindFilterRules(Document, ParameterElement) when the project parameter is deleted. The family transaction and the reload delete no Revit warning outside a fixed list; any other warning or error rolls back and refuses with its description. Migrate compares every label with its expected state again after the commit, with every element of the family after an ungroup, and, by owner view, detail group name and position, in the reloaded family, where it also counts every element of the former group members' kinds at each place. An unused Autodesk.Revit.DB.SharedParameterElement may remain after replacement. In Revit 2026 it refuses an annotation family when that element remains because the family may use the GUID in a label that dbtools cannot read. It reloads the family over the loaded one, writes each recorded value that the reload did not keep and reads every value back. Any refusal or failure rolls the group back; the project keeps its families and values. Family files on disk do not change. A family loaded again from such a file brings the old GUID back. api/dbtools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters..summary: Class SharedParameterMigration Namespace dbtools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Replaces a project parameter with a shared parameter of another GUID, binds an unbound shared parameter, or rebinds a shared parameter as an instance parameter of more categories, and carries over every value. public sealed class SharedParameterMigration Inheritance object SharedParameterMigration Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Both operations change the project only when they can carry over every value. Before any change they plan one write per value: an instance-bound parameter keeps each element value; a type-bound parameter copies each type value to every instance of that type. A type value without an instance cannot be carried, so the call refuses. Migrate(Document, ParameterElement, ExternalDefinition, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, SharedParameterUseHandling) also requires the source and target specs to match (ForgeTypeId.NameEquals). One transaction group then changes the binding, writes the values and reads each one back. Revit refuses a changed value on a member of a group placed more than once when the parameter does not vary between group instances, so such writes run with the variance on, the original variance comes back after them, and every value is read back again; a parameter that Revit does not let vary is refused. If any write or read-back fails, or any step throws, the group rolls back and the project keeps the original parameter, binding and values. A refusal or a rollback after failed writes throws SharedParameterMigrationException with every value that could not be carried; each is also logged. Migrate(Document, ParameterElement, ExternalDefinition, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, SharedParameterUseHandling) deletes the source parameter. A loaded family that defines the source GUID keeps it in its own definition, and its labels and formulas then refer to a parameter the project no longer has; run SharedParameterFamilyMigration first. The target may already exist without a binding, because loaded families define it; the migration then binds it. Each source-bound element keeps the value that is not empty. The migration also records target-only values on elements in categories added to the binding, and restores them if binding changes them. Two different values refuse before any change. Bind(Document, SharedParameterElement, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, ForgeTypeId) handles a shared parameter that already exists in the project but has no binding. It records values that loaded families expose in the categories to bind, binds the parameter as an instance parameter, restores values that binding changes, and reads them back. A placed family type parameter refuses when the repair needs an instance binding. An unplaced family type parameter stays on its type. CheckBind(Document, SharedParameterElement, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, ForgeTypeId) runs the same plan without a lasting change. Every operation reads bindings through SharedParameterBindingLookup, so a dead key in Revit's binding map refuses it with SafeExecutionRefusedException before any change. A check that changes the project in a transaction that always rolls back (the group variance check, and the family ownership check of SharedParameterFamilyMigration) requires Revit to report the rollback. When Revit does not, or the rollback throws, the check throws SharedParameterRollbackException, a failure that is not a refusal. api/dbtools.Core.Revit.Transactions.ITra.summary: Interface ITransactionRunner Namespace dbtools.Core.Revit.Transactions Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Runs synchronous work in a Revit transaction, or in a subtransaction when the target document already has an open transaction. public interface ITransactionRunner Remarks A rejected delegate shape throws InvalidOperationException from the call itself. Every other failure arrives through the returned task. The work runs synchronously inside one Revit API callback of the call gate. The token is checked before the transaction starts and before and after the work runs. Cancellation alone rolls back an open transaction and cancels the task without faulting it. An erased Task or boxed ValueTask result, for example a task returned as object, is rejected after the work runs, and the transaction rolls back. A start status other than Autodesk.Revit.DB.TransactionStatus.Started, or a commit status other than Autodesk.Revit.DB.TransactionStatus.Committed, raises TransactionFailureException. TransactionName and Status identify the transaction. For a transaction commit, Warnings lists the suppressed warnings, and BlockingFailures, BlockingFailureDefinitionIds and BlockingFailureDefinitionGuids describe the errors that blocked it. The GUIDs follow the IDs in order; Core does not classify them. An InvalidOperationException refuses a missing active document, a target document that differs from a modifiable active document, and a call that the gate cannot run in its context. A work or Revit exception propagates unchanged after cleanup. When the rollback or the disposal also fails, an AggregateException holds the first failure followed by the cleanup failures. A disposal failure after a commit does not fail the call: Core logs it at Error and returns the committed result. api/dbtools.Core.Revit.Transactions.Tran.summary: Interface ITransactionGroupService Namespace dbtools.Core.Revit.Transactions.TransactionGroup Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Groups the active document's transactions into one Revit undo entry through separate begin and finalize calls. public interface ITransactionGroupService Remarks Revit rolls back an open group when the API callback that started it returns. An owned group must therefore begin and finalize through inline call-gate execution within that same callback, as in a modal command. Queued modeless work uses RunAsync<T>(string, Func<CancellationToken, Task<T>>, Func<T, bool>, CancellationToken), whose outcome contract covers an unconfirmed rollback. On a document that is already modifiable, BeginAsync(string, CancellationToken) creates no owned group but sets IsActive, and finalization only resets that state. Failures arrive through the returned task, and cancellation cancels it. When cleanup also fails, an AggregateException holds the first failure followed by the cleanup failures. Task BeginAsync(string name, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters name string ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks The task faults with InvalidOperationException when there is no active document or a session is already active, and with TransactionFailureException when an owned group fails to start. Task FinalizeAsync(TransactionGroupFinalization finalization, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters finalization TransactionGroupFinalization ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks An unsupported finalization value faults the task with ArgumentOutOfRangeException and leaves the session and its group unchanged. A supported value does nothing when no session is active. Commit expects a confirmed commit and Rollback expects a confirmed rollback. Another result raises TransactionFailureException, unless a Revit exception from the assimilation or rollback is already the failure. api/dbtools.Core.SafeExecution.Domain.IS.summary: Interface ISafeExecutor Namespace dbtools.Core.SafeExecution.Domain Assembly dbtools.Core.dll public interface ISafeExecutor Methods RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) Runs action inside the safe-execution boundary, reports its outcome, and rethrows every outcome except success. Task RunAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IBannerNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters action Func<Task> logger ILogger notifier IBannerNotifier opts SafeExecutionOptions ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks The returned task completes normally only for Succeeded. A Refused, Canceled or Failed outcome is reported first and then rethrown. The rethrown exception is the instance that the action threw, with its original stack trace, unless a reporting stage failed and the outcome became an AggregateException. Reporting follows opts. Failure banners use notifier, or the App default notifier when the call site has none. An exception that an inner run already showed (FailureReport) is logged again, without a second banner or failure presentation. A SafeExecutionRefusedException is Refused. It shows a warning banner, or writes a warning log entry when there is no notifier or banners are suppressed. It writes no exception diagnostics. Every OperationCanceledException is Canceled, also one that does not come from ct. It writes a warning log entry and shows no failure banner. A canceled ct stops the action before it starts. Any other exception is Failed. It is logged and shown in an error banner, as opts allows. The banner text is the exception message, or The operation failed. for a blank message. A success banner that throws makes the outcome Failed with that exception. A reporting failure makes an AggregateException with the operation's exception first and the reporting failure second. The stages run in this order: refusal reporting (the outcome is then Failed and takes the failure path), failure notification. When more than one stage fails, each later aggregate holds the earlier one as its first inner exception. The outermost run hands its failure record to the caller's handler, such as the window error boundary. Exceptions ArgumentNullException action, logger or opts is null. The returned task faults with this exception; nothing is reported. RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) Runs action with the reporting of RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) and returns the outcome instead of rethrowing it. Task<SafeExecutionResult> RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IBannerNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters action Func<Task> logger ILogger notifier IBannerNotifier opts SafeExecutionOptions ct CancellationToken Returns Task<SafeExecutionResult> The outcome. Exception is null for success; otherwise it holds the exception that RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) would rethrow. Exceptions ArgumentNullException action, logger or opts is null. The returned task faults with this exception; argument validation is not a handled outcome.

api/dbtools.Core.SafeExecution.Runtime.S.summary: Class SafeExecutor Namespace dbtools.Core.SafeExecution.Runtime Assembly dbtools.Core.dll public sealed class SafeExecutor : ISafeExecutor Inheritance object SafeExecutor Implements ISafeExecutor Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Constructors SafeExecutor(IBannerNotifier?) public SafeExecutor(IBannerNotifier? defaultNotifier = null) Parameters defaultNotifier IBannerNotifier Methods RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) Runs action inside the safe-execution boundary, reports its outcome, and rethrows every outcome except success. public Task RunAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IBannerNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters action Func<Task> logger ILogger notifier IBannerNotifier opts SafeExecutionOptions ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks The returned task completes normally only for Succeeded. A Refused, Canceled or Failed outcome is reported first and then rethrown. The rethrown exception is the instance that the action threw, with its original stack trace, unless a reporting stage failed and the outcome became an AggregateException. Reporting follows opts. Failure banners use notifier, or the App default notifier when the call site has none. An exception that an inner run already showed (FailureReport) is logged again, without a second banner or failure presentation. A SafeExecutionRefusedException is Refused. It shows a warning banner, or writes a warning log entry when there is no notifier or banners are suppressed. It writes no exception diagnostics. Every OperationCanceledException is Canceled, also one that does not come from ct. It writes a warning log entry and shows no failure banner. A canceled ct stops the action before it starts. Any other exception is Failed. It is logged and shown in an error banner, as opts allows. The banner text is the exception message, or The operation failed. for a blank message. A success banner that throws makes the outcome Failed with that exception. A reporting failure makes an AggregateException with the operation's exception first and the reporting failure second. The stages run in this order: refusal reporting (the outcome is then Failed and takes the failure path), failure notification. When more than one stage fails, each later aggregate holds the earlier one as its first inner exception. The outermost run hands its failure record to the caller's handler, such as the window error boundary. Exceptions ArgumentNullException action, logger or opts is null. The returned task faults with this exception; nothing is reported. RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) Runs action with the reporting of RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) and returns the outcome instead of rethrowing it. public Task<SafeExecutionResult> RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IBannerNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters action Func<Task> logger ILogger notifier IBannerNotifier opts SafeExecutionOptions ct CancellationToken Returns Task<SafeExecutionResult> The outcome. Exception is null for success; otherwise it holds the exception that RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) would rethrow. Exceptions ArgumentNullException action, logger or opts is null. The returned task faults with this exception; argument validation is not a handled outcome.

api/dbtools.Core.Settings.Persistence.IS.summary: Interface ISettingsProvider Namespace dbtools.Core.Settings.Persistence Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Reads layered settings and atomically commits per-year sections. public interface ISettingsProvider Methods CommitAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite>, CancellationToken) Replaces the supplied per-year sections with one atomic file swap. Task CommitAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters writes IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks Rejects an empty batch, null entries and repeated sections. Acquires a cross-process lock and rereads the file before replacing sections. Lock acquisition throws IOException after 10 seconds. A failed commit leaves the settings file unchanged. Get<TSettings>(SettingsSection<TSettings>) Synchronously rereads defaults and per-year settings without caching. TSettings Get<TSettings>(SettingsSection<TSettings> section) where TSettings : class, new() Parameters section SettingsSection<TSettings> Returns TSettings Type Parameters TSettings Remarks Missing files, sections and optional values use defaults. A value of the wrong JSON kind at an object or collection position reads as empty. An object, array or null at a string property reads as an empty string. A later file's null or scalar preserves an earlier object or array. Malformed JSON and missing JsonRequired members throw, including members of objects that read as empty. Values that cannot convert to a boolean or number throw, including null, objects and arrays. Other I/O errors propagate. RecoverAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite>, CancellationToken) Preserves the existing per-year file as raw bytes and atomically publishes the supplied defaults. Task<string?> RecoverAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters writes IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> ct CancellationToken Returns Task<string> Remarks Rejects invalid batches and serializes before changing files. Holds the same lock as CommitAsync through preservation and publication. An absent source needs no preservation copy. A valid JSON object keeps unwritten top-level values with their original JSON text. Invalid documents are replaced in full. Returns the completed preservation path, or null for an absent source. Completed sibling recovery copies remain after success, failure or cancellation. Before publication, failure or cancellation leaves the active file unchanged. Application defaults are outside this operation.

api/dbtools.Core.Tools.Commands.ToolComm.summary: Class ToolCommand Namespace dbtools.Core.Tools.Commands Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Base class for Revit commands to enforce ISafeExecutor, run-scope creation, and centralized error notification. [SuppressMessage("Usage", "VSTHRD002:Avoid problematic synchronous waits", Justification = "Revit IExternalCommand.Execute() must be synchronous - async pattern is for internal composability")] public abstract class ToolCommand : IExternalCommand, IExternalCommandAvailability Inheritance object ToolCommand Implements IExternalCommand IExternalCommandAvailability Derived AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand ErftNewCommand ElevationTagsCommand ElevationTagsSymbolTextCommand MoveCombinedFoundationTagsCommand UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsCommand AllowJoinSelectedCommand DisallowJoinSelectedCommand GmCommand UpdateJoistGirderWeightsCommand OrganizeFoundationTypesCommand RecordSetCommand SgtCommand SettingsCommand TdvExportCommand TdvImportCommand VtcCommand Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The parameterless constructor stays inert to satisfy Revit's Autodesk.Revit.UI.IExternalCommand contract. Runtime services are resolved during Execute(ExternalCommandData, ref string, ElementSet). Sync-over-Async Pattern: The Execute(ExternalCommandData, ref string, ElementSet) method uses .GetAwaiter().GetResult() because Revit's Execute(ExternalCommandData, ref string, ElementSet) method must return synchronously. The async pattern in RunAsync(ICommandContext) is for composability within the command implementation. Constructors ToolCommand() Creates a command that defers runtime service resolution until execute time. This is required by Revit's IExternalCommand contract (parameterless constructor). protected ToolCommand() Properties RequiresActiveDocument Whether the command works on the active document. A command that changes only application state returns false: its context captures no document, so it also runs when no model is open. protected virtual bool RequiresActiveDocument { get; } Property Value bool Methods Execute(ExternalCommandData, ref string, ElementSet) Overload this method to implement and external command within Revit. public Result Execute(ExternalCommandData commandData, ref string message, ElementSet elements) Parameters commandData ExternalCommandData An ExternalCommandData object which contains reference to Application and View needed by external command. message string Error message can be returned by external command. This will be displayed only if the command status was "Failed". There is a limit of 1023 characters for this message; strings longer than this will be truncated. elements ElementSet Element set indicating problem elements to display in the failure dialog. This will be used only if the command status was "Failed". Returns Result The result indicates if the execution fails, succeeds, or was canceled by user. If it does not succeed, Revit will undo any changes made by the external command. IsCommandAvailable(UIApplication, CategorySet) Implement this method to provide control over whether your external command is enabled or disabled. public bool IsCommandAvailable(UIApplication applicationData, CategorySet selectedCategories) Parameters applicationData UIApplication An ApplicationServices.Application object which contains reference to Application needed by external command. selectedCategories CategorySet An list of categories of the elements which have been selected in Revit in the active document, or an empty set if no elements are selected or there is no active document. Returns bool Indicates whether Revit should enable or disable the corresponding external command. Remarks This callback will be called by Revit's user interface any time there is a contextual change. Therefore, the callback must be fast and is not permitted to modify the active document and be blocking in any way. api/dbtools.Core.UI.Dispatching.WpfDispa.summary: Class WpfDispatcher Namespace dbtools.Core.UI.Dispatching Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Routes WPF dispatcher work through the generation-owned operation registry. public static class WpfDispatcher Inheritance object WpfDispatcher Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks After the registry retires, Post(Action, DispatcherPriority) returns a task that stays pending and never runs its callback. Queue(Dispatcher, Action, DispatcherPriority) and Invoke(Dispatcher, Action, DispatcherPriority) throw InvalidOperationException with the retired-registry message, including when Invoke runs on the dispatcher thread. An Invoke already waiting on a worker thread receives the same exception when retirement drops its queued callback. A Post reporter failure stays on its task and does not reach UnhandledException. A Queue callback failure reaches UnhandledException after registry cleanup. When the registry is open, Post throws InvalidOperationException if no dispatcher is available or it is shutting down. api/dbtools.ElevationTags.Settings.SpotE.summary: Class SpotElevationPreviewLayout Namespace dbtools.ElevationTags.Settings Assembly dbtools.ElevationTags.dll Places a spot type preview in paper inches. It shows one leader that runs down to the element point and one that runs up. X grows along the shoulder and canvas Y grows downward. public static class SpotElevationPreviewLayout Inheritance object SpotElevationPreviewLayout Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The label follows Align's placement rule, SpotElevationTextAligner.ComputeTextOffset, with the margin LabelGapFromLeaderEnd and the gap LabelGapFromShoulder at a view factor of 1. Above Leader and Below Leader draw alike. The label sits on the point's side of the shoulder. In-line text sits past the leader end and has no symbol. The family drawing uses X along the shoulder and Y up. Its position mirrors vertically for the up spot; its text stays upright. Fields ElementSize Side of the square element that both leaders point to. public const double ElementSize = 0.25 Field Value double InLineShoulder Length of shoulder for in-line text, which does not sit over the shoulder. public const double InLineShoulder = 0.375 Field Value double LabelGapFromLeaderEnd Margin from the leader end to the near edge of the label. public const double LabelGapFromLeaderEnd = 0.140625 Field Value double LabelGapFromShoulder Distance from the shoulder to the near edge of the capitals. public const double LabelGapFromShoulder = 0.015625 Field Value double LeaderDrop Vertical run of each leader from its shoulder to the element point. public const double LeaderDrop = 0.3125 Field Value double LeaderRun Horizontal run of each leader from its shoulder to the element point. public const double LeaderRun = 0.5 Field Value double Margin Clear space around the drawing. public const double Margin = 0.125 Field Value double ShoulderPastLabel Length of shoulder past the far edge of the label without offsets. public const double ShoulderPastLabel = 0.0625 Field Value double Methods Compute(double, double, SpotTextLocation, double, double, SpotElevationSymbolDrawing?) api/dbtools.ElevationTags.Settings.html.title: Namespace dbtools.ElevationTags.Settings | dbtools
api/dbtools.ElevationTags.Settings.html.summary: Namespace dbtools.ElevationTags.Settings Classes ElevationTagsSettings Persisted settings for elevation-tag alignment workflows. PreviewContext Draws the selected spot elevation type as Align places it. The preview shows one spot whose leader runs down to the element point and one whose leader runs up to it. The family symbol, shoulders, leaders and elevation text use paper-inch layout and the type's visual properties. SettingsPackContext Settings pack context for elevation tag configuration. Coordinates pattern, type, and preview contexts for the settings UI. SpotElevationPreviewLayout Places a spot type preview in paper inches. It shows one leader that runs down to the element point and one that runs up. X grows along the shoulder and canvas Y grows downward. SpotElevationPreviewScene A laid-out preview: two spots of one type whose leaders run down and up to one element point. ShowsSymbol is false when the type has no symbol drawing or uses in-line text. SpotElevationPreviewTag One spot in the preview. The symbol center is LeaderEnd; the shoulder runs from there to ShoulderEnd, where the leader turns to the element point. Label and BaseLabel span the capitals, from their top to the baseline; BaseLabel is the label without offsets. SpotElevationPreviewTag.SymbolPlacement The symbol's leader-end origin and its canvas-space extent. SpotElevationSymbolDrawing A Revit-free spot symbol drawing in paper inches. The family origin is the leader end. X grows along the shoulder and Y grows up. SpotElevationSymbolDrawing.Fill One solid filled region with all its boundary loops. SpotElevationSymbolDrawing.Path A tessellated family curve or region boundary. SpotElevationSymbolDrawing.Text A plain family text element; its position is the Revit anchor selected by vertical alignment. SpotElevationTypeSnapshot Immutable snapshot of a spot elevation type's visual properties for WPF preview rendering. No Revit API references — safe to use on the UI thread. TypeAlignmentOffsets Leader-relative nudges stored per spot elevation type. TypeContext A base class for objects of which the properties must be observable. TypeSelection Structs PreviewPoint A preview point in paper inches. PreviewRect A preview rectangle in paper inches. SpotElevationSymbolDrawing.Bounds Axis-aligned family-view extents in coordinates where Y grows up. Enums SpotElevationSymbolDrawing.HorizontalAlignment SpotElevationSymbolDrawing.VerticalAlignment SpotTextLocation Values of a spot elevation type's Text Location parameter (SPOT_ELEV_TEXT_LOCATION).

api/dbtools.Presentation.Behaviors.Wheel.summary: Class WheelForwarding Namespace dbtools.Presentation.Behaviors Assembly dbtools.Presentation.dll Passes a mouse wheel turn that a nested scroll viewer cannot use to the next scroll viewer outward. WPF's ScrollViewer marks every wheel event handled, even at the end of its range or when it has nothing to scroll, so a grid, list or text box inside a scrolling page stops the page. api/dbtools.Presentation.Behaviors.html.summary: Namespace dbtools.Presentation.Behaviors Classes BehaviorState Keeps attached behavior state weakly keyed by its element and releases all state for an element during tool-window retirement. The table is stable; its values must be cleared by Release(DependencyObject) before a payload generation is unloaded. ContextMenuOnClickBehavior Opens a button's context menu from its click, placing it below the button. A toggle button keeps its checked state synchronized with the menu's open state. FocusRequestBehavior Focuses the attached control when a bound request value changes. The request is a plain counter or token owned by the view model; the behavior owns and aborts its posted operation. PreviewZoomBehavior Resets an image to its layout fit when its source changes or the Zoom Extents button is clicked. SelectOnRightClickBehavior Selects and focuses an items-control container before its context menu opens. TreePathNavigationBehavior Expands a tree path and selects its final item. By default it brings that item into view and focuses it. Paths contain item values, so payload types do not enter the stable behavior assembly. TreePathRequest Plain path request consumed by TreePathNavigationBehavior. WheelForwarding Passes a mouse wheel turn that a nested scroll viewer cannot use to the next scroll viewer outward. WPF's ScrollViewer marks every wheel event handled, even at the end of its range or when it has nothing to scroll, so a grid, list or text box inside a scrolling page stops the page. The theme's implicit ScrollViewer style sets IsEnabled; a viewer inside a popup has no outer viewer and keeps its wheel. Interfaces IReleasable Releasable state owned by one stable attached behavior.

api/dbtools.Presentation.Controls.html.title: Namespace dbtools.Presentation.Controls | dbtools
api/dbtools.Presentation.Controls.html.summary: Namespace dbtools.Presentation.Controls Classes DialogFooter Arranges the buttons at the bottom of a dialog or tool window. Tertiary buttons sit at the left; secondary buttons and then the primary button sit at the right, so the primary button is rightmost whatever the declaration order. The tab order follows the arranged order. A destructive confirmation gives the danger button the Primary role and makes Cancel the default (IsDefault), so Enter cancels. ListEmptyState The line that a list, tree or data grid shows while it has no items, such as "No library files. Add one with Add library file…". The theme templates of ListBox, TreeView and DataGrid show it; without it an empty list stays blank. SearchBox A filter-as-you-type text box that reads as search at a glance: a leading magnifier, a placeholder that names what it filters, an optional result count and a clear button that shows only while there is text. Escape clears the text. It is a TextBox, so a Text binding and its automation id work as on a plain text box. SettingsPack One settings pack with a title, status markers and a reset action above its content. The reset action is enabled only while the pack differs from its defaults. UI Automation exposes the pack as a group. ToolbarRow A row of commands that act on the list or content next to it, such as Add, Remove and Validate. Children sit left to right in declaration order with one gap between neighbors and are centered vertically. The row does not wrap. Enums DialogFooterRole The place of a button in a DialogFooter.

api/dbtools.Presentation.RevitCallback.R.summary: Class RevitCallbackRelay Namespace dbtools.Presentation.RevitCallback Assembly dbtools.Presentation.dll A callback object for Revit whose type belongs to the never-reloaded tier. Revit keeps some callbacks after the call that received them; for example, it keeps native copies of failure handling options, with their failures preprocessor, until it next pumps. A reloadable callback held that way keeps its Dev Mode generation alive while a reload proves the generation unreachable. api/dbtools.Presentation.ToolWindows.ITo.title: Interface IToolWindowSession | dbtools
api/dbtools.Presentation.ToolWindows.ITo.summary: Interface IToolWindowSession Namespace dbtools.Presentation.ToolWindows Assembly dbtools.Presentation.dll Owns a raw-XAML view and its stable window shell. public interface IToolWindowSession Remarks Register payload event handlers and cleanup through the session. Retire synchronously on the shell's UI thread before unloading a payload generation. Window and View are unavailable after retirement. Host-owned creation, lifecycle, root layout and dispatcher callbacks temporarily clear contextual reflection and restore the caller's scope on return. Raw templates resolve through the stable schema. The close gate, subscribed handlers and AddCleanup callbacks re-enter the creation context with ExecutionContext flow suppressed. Retirement releases that context on every exit. Flow suppression prevents captures. Clearing contextual reflection controls synchronous resolution. A command must suppress flow throughout its payload reflection scope, including tool-triggered layout outside shell overrides. WPF can measure an invalidated subtree directly. StrokeThickness and the lengths in StrokeDashArray are in device-independent pixels (DIP). The dash array alternates dash and space and starts with a dash; every dash and space is at least one device pixel long. A null dash array, or one without a space, is a solid line. A WPF shape multiplies its dash array by its stroke thickness; this element does not, so a Revit pattern keeps its length at every line weight. Commands can complete the same edit before a deferred native completion runs. SgtDataGridTextCommitBehavior Commits the active text editor before the DataGrid removes its editing element. SgtDecisionSelectionConverter Prevents a recycled selector's transient null from clearing its bound decision. SgtPreviewInputBehavior Releasable WPF input adapter for the SGT preview raw view. SgtThemeResourceExtension Supplies the SGT raw views with one theme dictionary per WPF dispatcher. SgtTreeViewSelectedItemBehavior Forwards SGT TreeView selection changes through a stable two-way attached property. It observes the control's actual selection event and does not synthesize mouse selection. SgtWindowDragInput Reads pointer positions and mouse capture from WPF input. SgtWindowInteractionBehavior Stable event adapter for SGT's raw view graph. It owns WPF input mechanics and keeps payload decisions behind ISgtWindowInteractionSurface. Interfaces ISgtDataGridRowEditGate Payload-implemented policy for deferred parent-row edits. ISgtPreviewInputSurface Stable input port for SGT's reloadable 2D preview. WPF event subscription stays in Presentation while the payload retains the editing and selection decisions. ISgtWindowDragInput External pointer coordinates and capture used by SGT flyout and preview drag handlers. ISgtWindowInteractionSurface Plain-value interaction port implemented by the reloadable SGT view model.

api/dbtools.Presentation.Tools.VTC.VtcCo.summary: Class VtcConflictConverter Namespace dbtools.Presentation.Tools.VTC Assembly dbtools.Presentation.dll Looks up a row key in a plain string dictionary for raw VTC XAML. public sealed class VtcConflictConverter : IMultiValueConverter Inheritance object VtcConflictConverter Implements IMultiValueConverter Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The first multi-binding value is the row key and the second is an IReadOnlyDictionary<TKey, TValue>. The converter has no reference to the payload result type, so the stable tier remains collectible-safe. Methods Convert(object?[], Type, object?, CultureInfo) Converts source values to a value for the binding target. The data binding engine calls this method when it propagates the values from source bindings to the binding target. public object Convert(object?[] values, Type targetType, object? parameter, CultureInfo culture) Parameters values object[] The array of values that the source bindings in the MultiBinding produces. The value UnsetValue indicates that the source binding has no value to provide for conversion. targetType Type The type of the binding target property. parameter object The converter parameter to use. culture CultureInfo The culture to use in the converter. Returns object A converted value. If the method returns null, the valid null value is used. A return value of DependencyProperty.UnsetValue indicates that the converter did not produce a value, and that the binding will use the FallbackValue if it is available, or else will use the default value. A return value of Binding.DoNothing indicates that the binding does not transfer the value or use the FallbackValue or the default value. ConvertBack(object?, Type[], object?, CultureInfo) Converts a binding target value to the source binding values. public object[] ConvertBack(object? value, Type[] targetTypes, object? parameter, CultureInfo culture) Parameters value object The value that the binding target produces. targetTypes Type[] The array of types to convert to. The array length indicates the number and types of values that are suggested for the method to return. parameter object The converter parameter to use. culture CultureInfo The culture to use in the converter. Returns object[] An array of values that have been converted from the target value back to the source values.

The caption takes SurfaceWindow, its text Text and the window border StrokeWindow. The attributes are documented from Windows 11 (build 22000); on Windows 10 the window keeps the system caption. A window that has been painted is painted again when ColorThemeState changes. public static class WindowCaption Inheritance object WindowCaption Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Methods Apply(Window) Paints the caption of window and repaints it on each theme change. api/dbtools.RecordSet.Features.Operation.summary: Interface ISafeFileSystemOperations Namespace dbtools.RecordSet.Features.Operations Assembly dbtools.RecordSet.dll public interface ISafeFileSystemOperations Methods AcquireLock(RecordSetSafeOperationContext) void AcquireLock(RecordSetSafeOperationContext context) Parameters context RecordSetSafeOperationContext CopyPath(SafeCopyPathRequest, RecordSetSafeOperationContext) Copies a file, or each file under a directory at the same relative path, to a destination in the target root. void CopyPath(SafeCopyPathRequest request, RecordSetSafeOperationContext context) Parameters request SafeCopyPathRequest The source and destination paths, the file filter and the verification option. context RecordSetSafeOperationContext The target root, long-path mode, log and cancellation token of the run. Remarks A file that ShouldCopyFile rejects is skipped with a log line and is not a failure. Each accepted file overwrites its destination and gets the source creation, last-access and last-write times. With VerifyAfterCopy, the SHA-256 hash of each accepted destination file must equal that of its source. A normal return means that every accepted file was copied and verified as requested, not that every source file was copied. The resolved destination is checked against the target root before each write. The check and the write are separate operations, so a concurrent path replacement can race them. Cancellation is observed between operations; a running file copy or hash read is not interrupted, so a late cancellation can return normally. A copy, timestamp, callback or verification failure, or a cancellation, can leave destination files changed, and execution does not restore them. An exception from ShouldCopyFile or Log propagates unchanged. Exceptions ArgumentNullException request, context or the context runtime is null. InvalidOperationException The destination, or a file destination under it, resolves outside the target root. OperationCanceledException The context cancellation token was canceled before an operation started. IOException The source does not exist, a read or write failed, or verification found a missing or different destination file. UnauthorizedAccessException The process cannot read the source or write the destination. api/dbtools.SGT.Domain.Plans.IPlanStore..summary: Interface IPlanStore Namespace dbtools.SGT.Domain.Plans Assembly dbtools.SGT.dll Mutable source of truth for the current SGT plan and its change version. public interface IPlanStore Properties Plan Detached snapshot of the active plan; throws when cleared or not initialized. Plan Plan { get; } Property Value Plan Version 0 when cleared; increments on initialize and on each accepted update. int Version { get; } Property Value int Methods Clear() void Clear() Initialize(Plan) Admits a detached copy without modifying the caller's plan. void Initialize(Plan plan) Parameters plan Plan TryGetPlan(out Plan?) Returns a detached snapshot when a plan is initialized. bool TryGetPlan(out Plan? plan) Parameters plan Plan Returns bool Update(Action<Plan>) Updates a private candidate. Only an accepted change replaces state and advances its version. int Update(Action<Plan> mutator) Parameters mutator Action<Plan> Returns int The version of this update, or the current version when it is a no-op. Remarks mutator changes a detached copy of the accepted plan. A candidate with unchanged content is a no-op: the version stays and no event is raised. An exception from mutator and a rejected admission keep the accepted plan and version. An accepted candidate advances the version once and then raises PlanChanged. An exception from a PlanChanged subscriber propagates after that commit; the committed plan and version stay. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The store has no initialized plan. SpecFailureException Admission rejected the changed candidate. The failure code is PlanValidationFailed, and the detail lists each rule failure. Events PlanChanged Raised after initialize, accepted update, and clear. Published plans are detached from stored state. Clear publishes a null plan with version 0. event EventHandler<PlanChangedEventArgs> PlanChanged Event Type EventHandler<PlanChangedEventArgs>

Jamb extent for an opening row being edited. public static Result<MemberAxisRange, SpecFailure> Resolve(EditableOpeningRow opening, OpeningMemberConfig? config, double baseElevation, double topElevation, IEnumerable<double>? girtElevations, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, double>? girtElevationByKey) Parameters opening EditableOpeningRow Opening row whose elevation range is relative to baseElevation. config OpeningMemberConfig Jamb settings, or null; their override elevations are relative to baseElevation. baseElevation double Absolute plan base elevation in feet: the wall bottom, or the foundation top in Foundation mode. topElevation double Absolute plan top elevation in feet: the wall top, or the base plus the seed band in Foundation mode. girtElevations IEnumerable<double> Girt elevations relative to baseElevation, searched for the nearest girt beyond each opening edge. girtElevationByKey IReadOnlyDictionary<string, double> Girt elevation relative to baseElevation by girt member key, in an ordinal map. Returns Result<MemberAxisRange, SpecFailure> The jamb range in absolute elevations, or the typed failure. Remarks A missing or unresolvable grid target returns a typed failure, so the editor can refuse the edit. A null config extends each end from the opening edge to the nearest girt beyond it, or to the wall base or top when there is no such girt.

api/index.html.title: API reference | dbtools
api/index.html.summary: API reference This section is generated from the XML documentation comments in the source code. It lists the public types and members of the dbtools assemblies. Generating the reference Run the documentation build from the repository root: bash .github/scripts/build-docs.sh full-api Use the SDK pinned by global.json. The script restores DocFX 2.78.5 from wiki/.config/dotnet-tools.json. It builds the Release product and Sandbox for Revit 2026 to supply build tasks, dependency assemblies and generated WPF source. The build runs on Linux with Windows targeting enabled. It does not start Revit. The script restores each non-test project in src/ with the metadata properties from wiki/docfx.json. DocFX's automatic restore is disabled because version 2.78.5 does not pass these properties to dotnet restore: Property Value Purpose Configuration Release Match the prerequisite builds and DocFX's default configuration. RevitYear 2026 Select the Revit API packages and year-specific restore assets. EnableWindowsTargeting true Resolve Windows and WPF reference packs on Linux. Set for every project by Directory.Build.props. DesignTimeBuild false Include Revit source excluded by XAML designer builds. DBT_IsDesignerBuild false Use normal project paths and source inclusion. _DBT_MergeDesigner true Retain public package references for DocFX's unmerged project symbols. _DBT_MergeDesigner controls package visibility separately from source inclusion. The product build merges public dependencies into their owning assemblies. DocFX reads project source, so its compilation needs those dependencies as package references. Keep the restore properties in the script aligned with the metadata properties in wiki/docfx.json. DocFX reads the projects in src/, excludes test projects, writes metadata to wiki/api/, and builds the site into wiki/_site/. Both modes use wiki/docfx.json and fail on DocFX warnings. The conceptual mode skips the product builds and API metadata generation. The reference covers the namespaces of dbtools.Core, dbtools.App, dbtools.Presentation and the tool assemblies (dbtools.GM, dbtools.SGT and others). Members without an XML comment appear without a description. Writing documentation comments Document each public type and member with /// comments. Give a <summary> for every member, a <param> for every parameter, <returns> for non-void methods and <exception> for exceptions that callers handle: /// <summary> /// Runs an action inside a Revit transaction. /// </summary> /// <param name="action">The action to run in the transaction.</param> /// <returns><see langword="true"/> if the transaction committed; otherwise <see langword="false"/>.</returns> /// <exception cref="InvalidOperationException">No document is active.</exception> public bool Execute(Action action) Use <remarks> only for constraints that a caller must know.

developer-guide/architecture/assembly-lo.title: Assembly Loading Contract | dbtools
developer-guide/architecture/assembly-lo.summary: Assembly Loading Contract The product is a tree of ordinary files: one entry assembly, two top-level libraries and one assembly per tool. The installed add-in loads in Revit's default AssemblyLoadContext. Revit-hosted tests and Dev Mode load the product into a context that the dbtools-daemon creates. In every host, App loads each tool assembly by explicit path into the context that holds dbtools.dll, and Revit calls each command by its assembly path and class name. Installed layout Each supported year has one directory of ordinary files. This is the product tree that the installer, Revit-hosted test staging, Sandbox and Dev Mode use: <year>/ ├── dbtools.addin ├── dbtools.dll ├── dbtools.Core.dll ├── dbtools.Presentation.dll └── Tools/ ├── dbtools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.dll ├── dbtools.DialogSuppression.dll ├── dbtools.ElevationTags.dll ├── dbtools.ERFT.dll ├── dbtools.FoundationTags.dll ├── dbtools.FramingJoins.dll ├── dbtools.GM.dll ├── dbtools.JoistGirderWeight.dll ├── dbtools.OrganizeFoundationTypes.dll ├── dbtools.RecordSet.dll ├── dbtools.SGT.dll ├── dbtools.Settings.dll ├── dbtools.TDV.dll └── dbtools.VTC.dll dbtools.addin names dbtools.dll and the class dbtools.App.Addin.AddinEntry. dbtools.dll contains the entry point and host infrastructure and no tool code. WPF needs the physical location of Presentation, so it stays at the top level. Merged libraries Every third-party runtime library is merged into one owner assembly; no third-party DLL is staged. build/Merging/AssemblyMerges.props declares the merges: Core owns the manifest parser, YamlDotNet, CommunityToolkit.Mvvm and CSharpFunctionalExtensions. SGT owns LibTessDotNet privately. The double-precision assembly is not merged. Presentation owns the Helix and SharpDX closure, Serilog, its logging provider and the Microsoft.Extensions logging, dependency injection, options and primitives libraries. SGT and ERFT declare CSharpFunctionalExtensions directly. Desktop builds share its public types through Core. Portable dependencies retain their NuGet identities. Installed Revit loads Presentation in the default AssemblyLoadContext. In Dev Mode, the daemon loads it in a non-collectible stable context and shares it across generations. LoggerFactoryScopeProvider and SerilogLoggerProvider keep their scopes in AsyncLocal fields in Presentation. Serilog's thread-static state also lives there. SerilogStack coordinates the process-wide logger across Core generations. App and Core bind to the merged logging types through dbtools.Presentation. Standalone package copies used by other add-ins have different assembly identities. Presentation owns the ambient Revit application slot (RevitApplicationContextSlot) and the asynchronous call timing state (RevitCallGateActionTiming). Their slots hold stable types across Core generations. A declaration's Include is the assembly name. A NuGet package that supplies that assembly uses the same name as its package ID. MSBuild passes each merge its inputs as items: the resolved runtime asset of a package, or the output of a project. The merge copies its evaluated reference files into a temporary reference directory. ILRepack searches only that directory and resolves framework identities only from those files, so other package or compiler-output files and the runtimes installed on the build host cannot change the result. MSBuild Inputs and Outputs, including the owner's project.assets.json, decide when a merge reruns. The task deletes its temporary files afterwards. MergeReferenceGuard checks merged images against the evaluated references. It rejects unresolved types or members, newer reference versions and references to assemblies that the merge removed. App host references App compiles against the selected Revit year's API references. RibbonNativeAccess reads the native Autodesk.Windows ribbon panel and item from their Revit API wrappers. Entry and idle acknowledgement AddinEntry has a public parameterless constructor for Revit. OnStartup first calls AddinIdle.TryAcknowledge. If DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_ROLE is set to any nonempty value and the entry assembly is in exactly AssemblyLoadContext.Default, it sets the AppContext data dbtools-daemon.IdleAddin:dbtools to the entry assembly's file location and returns Succeeded before any runtime, ribbon, logging or tool work. OnShutdown returns Succeeded immediately for that instance. Otherwise startup applies DBT_USER_DATA_DIR with AddinUserData, which uses BCL APIs and constants only. If the directory is refused, the entry formats and reports the reason before loading product dependencies, then returns Failed. A validated directory allows AppStartupBoundary.Start, a non-inlined method, to start the App lifecycle inside ToolWindowCallbackScope. Startup, shutdown and ribbon failures that cannot reach the normal log are written to Logs\dbtools.Fallback.log below AppPaths.BaseDir with BCL APIs only. Tool resolution ToolAssemblyResolver.LoadAssembly(rootAssembly, assemblyName) loads a manifest-declared assembly. The name must be a simple assembly name: it does not end with .dll in any case and contains no /, \, , or :. Other names throw ArgumentException before any file lookup. If the name equals the root assembly's name, the root is returned. Otherwise the resolver: requires a file-backed root assembly; resolves <root directory>/Tools/<assemblyName>.dll and requires the file; reads the file's assembly name and requires the declared simple name; returns an assembly of that name already loaded in the root's context, if its full identity and location match the file; a different identity or location is an error; otherwise loads the file with that context's LoadFromAssemblyPath. The resolver does not search other contexts, install an AppDomain resolver or create a load context. The ribbon registers each command by its assembly location, full class name and availability type name. Availability is implemented by the command's own assembly. Command and availability callbacks enter ToolWindowCallbackScope, which suppresses ExecutionContext flow and sets contextual reflection to the command's load context. Hosted tests and Dev Mode The daemon creates ProductLoadContext for hosted tests and DevModeLoadContext for Dev Mode. App loads each declared tool from Tools/ into that context; Dev Mode does not probe other subfolders. Presentation stays loaded for the life of the process. App, Core and the tool assemblies can be reloaded, as the host decides. DevModeCollectibleUnloadTests composes such a generation on Linux and requires it to unload; see Testing Tools. A Dev Mode fleet job loads the Dev Mode scenario into a separate test context in the Revit process for each generation. The scenario references the testing bridge and exercises the product through Revit, verified ribbon proxies, windows and the log in the private data directory. The scenario references no dbtools product assembly and holds no type or object from a product generation. Linux lifetime checks The BUILD lane checks reloadable product code for common Dev Mode lifetime failures against both supported Revit years. The resolver fixture inventories AssemblyResolve and AssemblyLoadContext.Resolving registrations, plus AssemblyLoadContext.Load overrides, across product source under src. Each inventoried resolver has a named safety exercise. The exercises use missing names, unusual versions (including 1.0.0 and 0.0.0.0), culture and public-key differences, and dbtools-owned names. A resolver returns a matching assembly or null; it does not throw. The raw XAML audit scans product XAML under src, including Presentation. It checks each binding path segment against a dependency property or a property on a type that implements INotifyPropertyChanged. A OneTime binding does not require change notifications. The audit resolves sources from code-behind data contexts, d:DataContext, DataTemplate.DataType, RelativeSource, and ElementName when their types are known. It reports unresolved counts by source group and sample file locations. An unresolved binding remains unverified and does not count as a pass. Reloadable code cannot call Window.Show or Window.ShowDialog directly. Registered tool windows go through ToolWindowRegistry. Revit application event subscriptions go through Core's hook lifecycle. The contextual ribbon selection controller is part of that lifecycle. A suppression for DBTDEV002, DBTDEV003, or RS0030 must name its rule, include a non-empty reason, and apply to one member. Assembly, module, namespace, and pragma suppressions fail the BUILD check. A diagnostic severity override or NoWarn entry that disables or downgrades these rules also fails. Reloadable code cannot call Dispatcher.BeginInvoke, Dispatcher.InvokeAsync, or Dispatcher.Invoke directly. It also cannot call the matching DispatcherExtensions.BeginInvoke or DispatcherExtensions.Invoke methods. It uses Core's WpfDispatcher registry. The rule does not cover DispatcherTimer. See the dispatcher operation retirement contract. Sandbox Sandbox runs one new process in the default context for each candidate year. Its entry point uses only BCL types. It validates the candidate and loads its root assemblies before starting WPF through a non-inlined method. Sandbox loads tool assemblies from Tools/ on demand and exits after headless validation. See Sandbox Validator. Distribution hashes Distribution validation checks the exact relative file set, PE identities, source-derived versions, first-party reference identities, file lengths and SHA-256 hashes. The hashes identify the staged candidate. Nothing checks them when an assembly loads. See Build Pipeline, Architecture Overview and Installation.

developer-guide/architecture/build-pipel.title: Build Pipeline | dbtools
developer-guide/architecture/build-pipel.summary: Build Pipeline NAME build pipeline - stage, validate and publish a dbtools distribution SYNOPSIS Graph build/Build.proj Task dbtools.Build.Tasks.BuildPipelineStep Source build/Tasks/Pipeline/ DESCRIPTION BuildApp stages the product for each selected Revit year. BuildAll validates and publishes the complete Release distribution. See Build commands for targets and options. Desktop builds use the Nice3point Revit API packages pinned in Directory.Packages.props. These packages supply the metadata for compilation. The product tree excludes their runtime assets. STRUCTURE Owner Role build/Build.proj Orders the targets and launches the child builds. build/MSBuild/ProductOutput.proj Stages dbtools.dll (App), dbtools.Core.dll, dbtools.Presentation.dll and dbtools.addin at the year root. It stages the tool assemblies under Tools/. build/Merging/AssemblyMerges.props Assigns each merged library to its owning assembly. See Assembly Loading Contract. build/Distribution/ Defines and checks the distribution file set, assembly metadata and validation receipts. CONTRACTS A publication build requires a clean Git checkout and a Release build for Revit 2026 and 2027. DistributionContract.ProductFiles defines the exact file set for each year. When adding a tool, include its Tools/<name>.dll path in this list. StageProductOutputTask rejects a mismatch. Directory.Packages.props pins Protocol and DevMode.Testing to 0.22.12. The scenario and Windows acceptance builds check the vendored and restored DevMode.Testing packages against the SHA-256 in that file. testing/Daemon/Directory.Build.props pins the Revit test adapter to the same release and records its SHA-256. Update the dbtools-daemon.Protocol version in Directory.Packages.props, the lock in build/Distribution/protocol-package-lock.json and the matching vendor/DaemonProtocol/dbtools-daemon.Protocol.<version>.nupkg together. The build checks the package version and SHA-256 against the pin. Promotion requires a portable acceptance receipt for the same source, candidate bytes and validator. In the runtime inputs, dbtools.dll retains its mapped CodeView path, GUID and stamp to pair with dbtools.pdb. The Core merge writes dbtools.Core.pdb and records that file name in its CodeView entry. Both PDBs retain mapped source documents. Public merged types remain available to dependent product assemblies through their owning assembly. Content versions ContentVersion.targets derives product assembly versions from the SHA-256 of the build inputs. It includes source, resource names and bytes, resolved references and merge inputs. It records the hash in AssemblyInformationalVersion as <AssemblyVersion>+inputs.<hash>. SourceVersionEvidence checks the version against the input hash. It also requires byte-identical Presentation assemblies across Revit years. To trace a version change, compare the input lists under .artifacts/obj/content-version/. FLOW In the publication graph, Restore captures the clean Git commit and tree. BuildValidationRunner builds the Validation Runner and authenticates its Protocol package. BuildAppPerYear stages each year tree. AssembleDistributionCandidate copies the declared files into the candidate and writes its hashes and source identity to its build.json. StagePortableAcceptanceInput stages the Revit metadata references. ValidateDistributionCandidate checks assembly and manifest metadata and runs the Dev Mode preflight for each year. ValidateManifestTypes resolves the types named by tool manifests in the built assemblies. BuildDevModeScenario compiles the hosted scenario for each year. PromoteToDist replaces the distribution and acceptance trees. DistributionPublisher moves .artifacts/build.json into place last. Read the published files after the command succeeds. Dev Mode preflight DevModePreflightWorker calls DevModeStableGraphPreflight.Run for each year's App assembly. The pinned dbtools-daemon.Protocol package supplies policy devmode-stable-graph/v4 under schema 2 and contract devmode-preflight/v2. Each year has a three-minute runner limit. A collectible-boundary warning fails validation. DATA Path Contents .artifacts/bin/<Configuration>/<year>/net10.0-windows/ Staged product from BuildApp. .artifacts/.staging/<build-id>/distribution-candidate/Release/<year>/ Unpublished candidate. .artifacts/.staging/<build-id>/build.json Build metadata for the unpublished candidate. .artifacts/.staging/<build-id>/portable-validation-result.json Staged portable acceptance receipt. .artifacts/dist/Release/<year>/ Promoted product. The parent directory contains promotion-receipt.json. .artifacts/build.json Build metadata for the promoted distribution. .artifacts/acceptance/ Tool contract and Dev Mode scenario for the promoted distribution. Inspect staged files after a failed or unpromoted run. After publication, PromoteToDist removes .artifacts/.staging/<build-id>/. A cleanup warning means the staging directory may remain. Portable acceptance receipt PromoteToDist embeds the staged receipt in the validation field of promotion-receipt.json. BuildBundle --candidate-dist rechecks it against the distribution bytes, source and Protocol pin. The receipt covers metadata and static policy only. For Windows UI checks and tests in Revit, see Sandbox Validator and Test Pipeline. Dev Mode scenario testing/dbtools.DevMode.Scenario/ owns the hosted scenario. It compiles against dbtools-daemon.DevMode.Testing.Scenario from the dbtools-daemon.DevMode.Testing package. The daemon supplies bridge assembly version 2.0.0.0 at runtime. DevModeScenarioManifestWriter publishes its payload under .artifacts/acceptance/dev-mode-scenario/<year>/. The adjacent dev-mode-scenario.json binds it to the product, the model and the preflight result for each year. The writer reads bridge_contract_version from the scenario's bridge assembly reference and writes 2. See Test Pipeline for test execution. The scenario calls ExpectDialogs before it prepares a modal command. Each declaration matches the exact UI Automation name and native caption. The scope covers the interaction and window cleanup. Settings with Save declares dbtools - Settings, dbtools for its alerts, and dbtools Notification for its feedback banner. TDV declares the library selection and transfer windows. Window searches omit closed windows. The close wait searches until the original window token is absent. Cleanup handles DevModeWindowClosedException when a window closes before the close request reaches it. When an action rebuilds controls, the scenario polls InspectControlAsync with the selector of the next control it uses. A control wait has a deadline. Its timeout names the scenario step and the selector. Download window captures Submit a published distribution with the two models that match its scenario manifest. dbtools-daemon-cli devmode-submit \ --archive path/to/published-distribution.tar.gz \ --model 2026=testing/RevitTestModels/2026/GM/gm_test_model.rvt \ --model 2027=testing/RevitTestModels/2027/GM/gm_test_model.rvt Save the test attachments for each year using the child job ID from the submission report. dbtools-daemon-cli report --job '<2026-child-job-id>' --attachments --out ./devmode-captures/2026 dbtools-daemon-cli report --job '<2027-child-job-id>' --attachments --out ./devmode-captures/2027 The CLI creates one folder per test. Each window capture name ends in <route>--<state>.png. If the daemon refuses a capture for size, the attachment ends in <route>--<state>.txt and contains the reason. The scenario captures a notification window as soon as its expected control is visible. If the window closes during capture, the text attachment contains the observed control and the reason. The model and command outcome determine which conditional scenes appear. Tool contract build/Distribution/tool-contracts.json lists the ribbon command types and the UI text the Dev Mode scenario checks. The Sgt and ErftNew entries identify command proxies. DevModeScenarioTests.Routes excludes their interactive picks, which wait for Revit user input. PromoteToDist copies the contract to .artifacts/acceptance/. DIAGNOSTICS ValidateDistributionCandidate reports the preflight summary for each year. Revit <year> Dev Mode preflight: <n> failures, <m> warnings; outcome=<outcome> The runner writes its response to .artifacts/.staging/<build-id>/devmode-preflight-<year>.json. Message Action <target>: authoritative distribution requires a clean tracked and untracked source tree. Run from a clean Git checkout. <context>: expected exact years [<expected>], actual [<actual>]. For the complete distribution, use both supported years. Revit <year> Dev Mode preflight rejects <code> warning in <assembly> <type> <member>: <message> Fix the code named in the warning. Resolved product files disagree with the distribution contract. Missing: <missing>; unexpected: <unexpected> Match the staged files to DistributionContract.ProductFiles. See Build commands for build log paths. TESTS Fixture Checks ContentVersionTests An image input change changes the version. PortableAcceptanceReceiptTests Checks receipt completeness, stale source identity and changed validator identity. DistributionPublisherTests The published build metadata appears after both trees move. DevModeScenarioManifestWriterTests The manifest binds the scenario and each year's inputs by hash. ResourceAssemblyVersionContractTests.AppAndCorePdbCodeViewPathsMatchDistributionAndKeepSourceDocuments Checks App and Core CodeView records and mapped PDB source documents for both years. ToolContractsTests The contract matches ribbon command types and source strings. SEE ALSO Build commands, Build troubleshooting, Assembly Loading Contract, Sandbox Validator, Test Pipeline

developer-guide/architecture/overview.ht.title: Architecture overview | dbtools
developer-guide/architecture/overview.ht.summary: Architecture overview NAME architecture - the dbtools assemblies, how they start and how they run a command SYNOPSIS entry dbtools.addin -> dbtools.dll, dbtools.App.Addin.AddinEntry source src/dbtools.{App,Core,Manifest,Presentation,Sandbox} tools src/Tools/{Common,Structural,Experimental,Services}/<Tool>/ (manifest.yml) years Revit 2026 (2026.5+), 2027: net10.0-windows (build/Distribution/RevitYearContract.cs) placement .agents/canon/CANON.md (where each kind of code belongs) DESCRIPTION Revit loads dbtools.dll through dbtools.addin. Its App code builds the services and the ribbon, and loads the tools from Tools/. Tools from the Experimental folder appear on the dbtools Testing panel. The daemon (dbtools-daemon) starts Revit for hosted tests. In Dev Mode, it reloads each new build into a running Revit. STRUCTURE flowchart TB Revit[Revit] -->|dbtools.addin| App[dbtools.dll] App --> Core[dbtools.Core.dll] App --> Presentation[dbtools.Presentation.dll] Core --> Presentation App -->|Tools/ path| Tools[Tools/dbtools.Tool.dll] Tools --> Core Tools --> Presentation Project Assembly Role src/dbtools.App dbtools.dll Startup, shutdown, services and ribbon. App embeds the tool manifests.
