Nullable values, collections, dictionaries, and nested DTOs must resolve to those leaf types. Add-in enums and custom TypeConverter/JsonConverter implementations are not supported settings types. Use settable properties with initialized defaults so missing keys retain those defaults. Pure and Revit-hosted test executables disable reflection-based JSON serialization. Read semantics and failures The reader recursively overlays objects and merges arrays by index. A shorter override array retains the default array's remaining elements. A later scalar or null does not replace an earlier object or array. A different container kind replaces the earlier container. Normalization preserves scalar conversions for strings, Booleans, and doubles. String nulls become empty strings. Boolean and double values parse from scalar text. Doubles use invariant culture. Invalid values fail the section read. Missing sections return a new settings instance. Only a missing file or parent directory means absent configuration. Invalid JSON, a non-object root, access faults, and a directory at a file path remain errors. Comments and trailing commas are accepted. Commits preserve unrelated sections but do not retain comments. Manifest declaration Declare the persistence key and pack metadata in manifest.yml: id: dbtools.MyTool assembly: dbtools.MyTool moduleType: dbtools.MyTool.App.Composition.MyToolToolModule order: 0 panel: Common tool: settings: configSection: Tools.MyTool settingsPacks: - key: common.my_tool title: "My Tool" warnings: - id: core.my_tool.configuration title: "My Tool Configuration Invalid" message: "Correct the family pattern and save settings." disableTools: - dbtools.MyTool configSection names the JSON property. Pack key and warning id are unique catalog identities. They do not have to equal that property. Existing keys use forms such as structural.foundation_tags and core.structural.combined_tags. Each warning requires id, title, and message. disableTools is optional. See Feature Warnings for activation and command blocking. The module's panel supplies the pack's group through GetRequiredPanel(): Value Settings group Settings dbtools Settings Common dbtools Common Structural dbtools Structural Testing dbtools Testing Services dbtools Services Registration Register the typed section in ToolModule.RegisterSettings: public override void RegisterSettings(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { services.AddSingleton(new SettingsSection<MyToolSettings>( manifest.GetRequiredConfigSection(), MyToolSettingsJsonContext.Default.MyToolSettings)); } Register the editor in RegisterSettingsPacks. The method resolves the typed section that RegisterSettings added to dependency injection. The following excerpt assumes SettingsPackContext implements ISettingsPackLifecycle<MyToolSettings>, accepts a warning ID, and exposes HasWarning. MyToolSettingsView is the tool-owned pack view: public override void RegisterSettingsPacks(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { services.AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition<MyToolSettings, SettingsPackContext>( manifest, (_, input) => new SettingsPackContext(input.RequireWarningId()), context => new MyToolSettingsView { DataContext = context }, context => context.HasWarning, (context, active) => context.HasWarning = active); } These APIs live under dbtools.Core.Settings.Composition, .Persistence, .SettingsPack, and .Warnings. Manifest extension methods live under dbtools.Core.Tools.Manifest. Use the tool's real namespaces for its context, view, and DTO. AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition reads the single settings pack and panel from the manifest. It resolves the same registered SettingsSection<TOptions> used by the tool's settings provider. The pack applies at NextToolRun. Supply both warning flag delegates when the pack declares one warning. The registration maps its ID, title, message, and disabled tool names from the manifest. Supply neither delegate when the pack declares no warnings. The registration rejects other warning or delegate counts. Apply timing ISettingsPackDefinition.ApplyBehavior tells the Settings window when saved values take effect. AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition always sets NextToolRun. Value Meaning Immediate Saved values apply immediately, such as ribbon visibility flags. NextToolRun Commands or view-activation tasks read saved values on their next run. RequiresRestart The pack documents a specific restart requirement. Do not show a blanket restart warning for all settings. Read settings at the operation boundary so saved changes reach the next operation. Runtime and context ownership ISettingsPackDefinition supplies catalog metadata and creates one ISettingsPackRuntime for an editor row. That runtime binds the exact context, typed section, lazy view factory, staged writes, and warning delegates. Callers cannot pair an unrelated context with a warning definition. SettingsPackCollection carries SettingsPackHostContext from the window factory into runtime creation. Use SettingsPackHostContext.Empty without a host or FromApplication(application) with one. A context extracts the typed application through TryGetApplication<TApplication>(). Initialize bindable state in constructors. Perform model changes through explicit editor actions. Elevation Tags uses host data for preview snapshots and accepts no active document as an empty preview. Combined Foundation Tags loads its shared-parameter status when its view loads and uses Install/Repair and Fix for prerequisite work. Without an active project it shows an empty state that names the reason, and Install/Repair is unavailable. Context interfaces The editor implements these base contracts: public interface ISettingsPackContext { Task<SettingsValidationResult> ValidateAsync(CancellationToken ct = default); } public interface ISettingsPackContext<TOptions> : ISettingsPackContext { void Load(TOptions options); TOptions BuildOptionsSnapshot(); } public interface ISettingsPackLifecycle<TOptions> : ISettingsPackContext<TOptions>, IPendingChangesContext, ISettingsStateContext, ISettingsPackSaveState<TOptions> { } Every registered editor context implements ISettingsPackLifecycle<TOptions>. It requires HasPendingChanges, StateChanged, and MarkSaved(committedOptions) alongside typed load, snapshot, and validation. The runtime forwards pending state and notifications to its owned context and rebaselines it after commit. Optional contracts add specific behavior: Interface Responsibility IOwnerAwareContext Receive an owner handle provider for dialogs. ISettingsWarningContext Identify the warning that validation evaluates. ISettingsPackSaveValidation Expose BlockSaveOnInvalid to refuse invalid drafts. IWarningFixProvider Supply a matching warning's Fix action and label. SettingsValidationResult.Success is a property. Use SettingsValidationResult.FromErrors(...) for invalid values. Exceptions mean validation failed to run. They are not an invalid-result substitute. Honor cancellation and return messages that identify the invalid value and its correction. Auto-update editor base SettingsPackAutoUpdateStateContext<TOptions> in dbtools.Core.Settings.SettingsPack.AutoUpdate implements the required lifecycle. It owns title/description/tooltip text, AutoUpdateEnabled, HasWarning, ToggleEnabled, pending-change tracking, StateChanged, and validation. It blocks saving invalid options. Its protected constructor takes title, description, and toggle tooltip strings. SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext<TOptions> derives from the state base and adds ISettingsWarningContext, WarningId, and ClearWarningCommand. Clearing an active warning raises one state event. Clearing an inactive warning raises none. Its protected constructor supplies warning identity and editor text: protected SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext( string warningId, string title, string description, string toggleToolTip); Derived contexts implement: protected abstract void LoadCore(TOptions options); protected abstract void CollectValidationErrors(List<string> errors); protected abstract bool SettingsEqual(TOptions left, TOptions right); public abstract TOptions BuildOptionsSnapshot(); Load applies the toggle, clears the context warning, calls LoadCore, and notifies state changes. LoadCore sets a baseline through SetBaseline. MarkSaved uses the exact committed options, not the latest editable snapshot. Edits made while a commit is pending therefore remain dirty. Elevation Tags, Joist Girder Weights, and the design-time auto-update previews use the warning-aware base. Combined Foundation Tags uses the state base and retains its prerequisite warning publication and repair actions. It does not implement ISettingsWarningContext. Its MarkSaved override copies committed options before setting the baseline. Regex pattern lists RegexPatternListContext owns RegexPatternEntry rows, add and remove commands, the row limit, and state-change events. Load keeps the first nonblank patterns up to the limit. When all entries are blank or the list is empty, it shows the default. Removal retains at least one row. A snapshot omits blank rows and saves the remaining pattern text as entered. IsDefaultPattern trims the entered text only for comparison with the default. A list with a sole default saves as an empty list. Joist Girder Weights uses the same comparison to save a default in an individual field as an empty string. Elevation Tags, Combined Foundation Tags, and Dialog Suppression bind their views directly to the shared context and limit each list to three rows. Each pack owns its validation rules. Tool settings examples Combined Foundation Tags persists TagFamilyPatterns, PierFamilyPatterns, and FootingFamilyPatterns. Empty lists select these tool defaults: TagFamilyPatterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ PierFamilyPatterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ FootingFamilyPatterns ^(?:Footing|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ Elevation Tags uses TagNamePatterns with default ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete|Steel|Wall) Label$, plus TypeOffsets keyed by spot-elevation type name. Joist Girder Weights supplies these defaults for blank individual patterns: FamilyNamePattern ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ DeadLoadPattern (?:^DL$|Dead\s*Load) LiveLoadPattern (?:^LL$|Live\s*Load) TotalLoadPattern (?:Point\s*Load|Total\s*Load) Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) uses LibraryOptions, which contains a Files list of LibraryFile values. Its pack owns file selection, validation, and pending changes. Read each tool's DTO and generated JSON context when extending it. Runtime reads and programmatic writes ISettingsProvider exposes typed reads and heterogeneous batch writes: TSettings Get<TSettings>(SettingsSection<TSettings> section) where TSettings : class, new(); Task CommitAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default); Task<string?> RecoverAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default); Inject the provider and typed section. Read once per operation, then pass that snapshot to the work: var current = settingsProvider.Get(section); if (!current.AutoUpdateEnabled) return; For view-activated updates, ViewActivationTask<TSettings> reads once during admission and captures the snapshot in the admission. It checks session warnings separately. See Hooks. A programmatic write uses the same typed metadata: var current = settingsProvider.Get(section); current.AutoUpdateEnabled = true; await settingsProvider.CommitAsync(new[] { section.CreateWrite(current) }, ct); Batch related section changes in one CommitAsync. A direct commit persists options. The Settings workflow additionally applies flags, baselines, and warning publication. Save and reset sequence The Settings tool owns the window workflow under src/Tools/Common/Settings. SettingsToolModule registers the singleton window factory, startup workflow and startup publisher. Each factory call creates an independent editor session. Core retains the public catalog, warning service, warning validator and pack contracts. Core-only composition registers no Settings window or startup publisher. The tool uses these public contracts without Core friend access. SettingsWindowFactory opens the raw dbtools.Presentation.Settings.Views.SettingsWindow.xaml resource through ToolWindowFactory. The registered modal session owns the window, error boundary, owner, handlers, and cleanup. Packs remain separate tool-owned views. SettingsPackViewModel owns one bound runtime, lazy view creation, pending changes, reset state, owner propagation, warning projection, and disposal. SettingsPanelBlock groups rows. SettingsWindowViewModel delegates persistence to SettingsPersistenceWorkflow under the Settings tool’s Features/Editing/Persistence. Save proceeds in this order: Evaluate the unsaved drafts. A blocking invalid result stops the save. This pass can update editor warning flags but does not change command blocking. Capture current pack writes and the flags snapshot. Commit the complete batch with one file swap. Mark each pack saved against its exact committed options. Apply committed flags. Validate saved settings in fresh warning-aware runtimes, record the decisions, then dispose all of the runtimes. Project and publish warning decisions to the ribbon and Settings UI. A disposal that also fails on its retry fails the warning validation phase with the pack key and both causes. When the validation itself fails, that phase reports both failures and Save stops. When the decisions were recorded, step 6 still publishes them and Save reports the cleanup failure afterwards. When more than one phase fails after the commit, the phase is apply committed state and the inner AggregateException holds the failure of each phase. The Validate button diagnoses draft values. It does not publish the draft as saved warning state. Opening Settings validates loaded options. Startup checks warning-aware packs without constructing their views. See Feature Warnings. A validation or writer failure before publication leaves the settings file and saved baselines unchanged. A failure after the swap becomes SettingsPostCommitException, which identifies the operation and phase. Persisted values remain the saved baseline and the window stays open. Concurrent edits remain pending against that baseline. Reset All commits default flags and every pack's default snapshot. It attempts to apply all committed defaults before warning validation and aggregates application failures. A pack reset commits only that pack. Both actions ask for confirmation and use the normal warning/feedback path. Cancel preserves current state and feedback. Choosing Reset Settings in the load-problem alert already confirms recovery, so it does not prompt twice. This action uses RecoverAsync to recover the per-year override. Normal reset uses CommitAsync and rejects corrupt documents. Both operations apply defaults only after persistence succeeds. Post-commit application or warning failures report the failed phase and retain the committed defaults. They do not retry persistence. Atomic persistence SettingsSectionWriter performs these steps: Reject an empty batch, null entries, and case-insensitive duplicate section names. Serialize calls on the writer instance and acquire the sibling settings.<year>.json.lock file exclusively. Re-read the current document under that lock. Replace only the supplied sections. Serialize with each section's generated metadata into one document. Write a .<guid>.tmp file in the same directory and publish it with File.Move(source, destination, overwrite: true). Attempt staged-file cleanup on success, failure, and cancellation. A competing process can hold the lock for up to 10 seconds before the writer fails with IOException. Cancellation while waiting leaves the file unchanged. The OS releases the lock on handle close or process exit. The empty lock file persists and does not indicate a live lock. TextFileIO.s_publicationGate serializes file publication process-wide across writer instances. The writer's own semaphore serializes its commits, while the sibling lock file coordinates separate processes. TextFileIO allows at most six publication attempts for transient sharing, locking, and access-denied failures. It refuses known read-only destinations immediately and surfaces publication access denial as IOException with the original cause. Cleanup does not replace the primary failure. Ordinary commits retain no backup file. Explicit load-problem recovery retains preservation copies as described below. Same-year Revit processes share this file. Re-reading under the cross-process lock preserves other sections published by the previous writer. A case-variant section name replaces that section in place. An absent file starts an empty object. An existing empty, whitespace-only, malformed, or non-object file is corrupt and is not silently reset. A file that repeats a top-level name, also with different letter case, is corrupt too. SettingsJson.RequireObject applies this rule to reads and commits. Both report a corrupt file as InvalidDataException with the message Settings file '<path>' is corrupt. and the JsonException cause; the Settings window shows that message. A section value that its type cannot convert is not file corruption: Get reports it as InvalidOperationException with the section name. RecoverAsync serializes the default sections before changing files. It holds the writer semaphore and the same exclusive sibling lock through source preservation and defaults publication. It reads the per-year source as raw bytes, including invalid UTF-8. It writes and flushes a complete sibling stage, then publishes it without overwrite as settings.<year>.json.recovery-<guid>.bak. Each recovery keeps all earlier completed copies. An absent source needs no copy. Other source or preservation failures include the path and stop recovery. After preservation, recovery parses the exact preserved source under the same locks. When reads accept the source, recovery keeps every unwritten top-level value with its original JSON text, including whitespace, numeric spelling and string escapes. Supplied section names match case-insensitively and receive defaults. Recovery replaces any other source in full: invalid JSON, a non-object root, or a repeated top-level name. Recovery returns the completed copy path, or null when the source was absent. Only after preservation succeeds does TextFileIO.WriteAllTextAtomicAsync publish defaults. Recovery never removes or renames the active source first. Failure or cancellation before publication leaves the active bytes unchanged. Completed copies remain if publication fails or is cancelled. Incomplete stages are removed without replacing the primary error. Recovery affects only the per-year override. It does not repair corrupt appsettings.json or bypass access failures. After successful publication, the writer logs the preservation path at Information. The recovery success banner includes that path. A later state or warning failure does not remove the committed defaults or the preservation log entry. Designer samples The Settings tool’s App/DesignTime supplies four neutral sample packs in the Common and Structural panels. Three use DesignTimeAutoUpdatePackContext, a private subclass of the production auto-update context. The Structural warning sample starts with an active warning. The library sample uses an empty serialization model and a text preview. The manifest names the public dbtools.Settings.App.DesignTime.SettingsWindowDesignTimeViewModel in dbtools.Settings. Editor views Create a tool-owned view for the editor. Bind the auto-update toggle to AutoUpdateEnabled and ToggleEnabled. Bind regex row editors to their explicit properties and commands. Pack views created by ViewFactory are embedded editors. See Modularity for top-level tool-window resources. Use the theme's sizes and spacing for action buttons in the Settings window and pack views. DialogFooter and ToolbarRow space adjacent buttons 8 px apart by default. In a pack row with its own layout, set Margin="{DynamicResource ButtonGap}" on each button after the first. Use the same margin for a button after a field. The theme sets footer buttons to Size.Control (28 px). Pack buttons use MinHeight.Button (28 px) as their minimum height. The window footer is a DialogFooter: Reset All… at the left, then Validate and Save Settings, the one primary action, at the right. The section links open their sections in the scrolling page. A gold dot marks active warnings. An accent dot marks unsaved changes. A link can show both dots. Use SettingsPack for the title, modification status and reset action. Use SettingsRow for a setting with a label on the left and an editor on the right. Auto-update packs use SettingsAutoUpdateRow. Bind RegexPatternEditor to the pattern list context. Place pack actions next to the fields or selection they act on. Use secondary or subtle buttons. Keep destructive confirmations in the alert and make Cancel the default. A pack that lists entries shows every value in full at any window width, without horizontal scrolling and without a value that only a tooltip shows. Use one item per entry: the primary name first, with a status at the right when the entry has one; secondary facts on a muted line; a problem sentence only when there is one. Every text wraps. Do not use a multi-column grid for such a list: its columns cannot fit the pack at the window's 800 px default. Give a list, tree or grid that can be empty an empty-state line with ListEmptyState.Text, for example controls:ListEmptyState.Text="No files. Add one with Add File.". Use TreeView.InScrollViewer for a settings tree whose rows expand within the page. The page handles wheel input over the tree. For a larger panel, use the theme's empty state: an EmptyStatePanel border with an EmptyStateIcon glyph, an EmptyStateTitle and an EmptyStateDetail that names the reason or the next step. See Testing Tools for execution commands and Feature Warnings for warning publication and Fix actions.

developer-guide/developing/testing-tools.title: Testing Tools | dbtools
developer-guide/developing/testing-tools.summary: Testing Tools Use test.sh to select, build, and execute repository tests. Use build.sh on Linux/WSL or build.ps1 on Windows to compile product and test graphs. Static discovery and request validation do not execute tests. Run commands from the repository root. Pure tests run without Revit. Revit-hosted tests use the local scope. Design Automation tests use the da scope and execute real APS WorkItems. Execution hosts Tool keys in the examples include Global Mapper (GM) and Super Girt Tool (SGT). Choose the scope for the behavior you need to test: Scope Host pure NUnit/VSTest without Revit. Most tool, App, and Core projects require Windows, including WPF fixtures. *.Portable.Pure.Tests projects run on Linux. local Revit-hosted tests on a daemon worker, marked [RevitLocal]. da Design Automation tests using real APS WorkItems, marked [RevitDA]. BUILD includes Linux-native contract tests and Windows Sandbox Pure tests. DIST selects Windows distribution acceptance and requires the daemon. Daemon runs use a hidden desktop. Other Windows Pure tests can also run locally on Windows with the required runtimes installed. See Test Pipeline for project membership, routing, staged inputs, and daemon adapter design. Build and validation commands ./build.sh [Target] [parameters] pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 [Target] [parameters] Both wrappers map options to build/Build.proj and acquire the SDK pinned in global.json. Native Windows uses PowerShell. build.sh refuses that host. Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027 use net10.0-windows. Year selection chooses references and output placement. Build targets Target Behavior BuildAll Default wrapper target. Build, validate, and promote the Release distribution with the Dev Mode scenario and other acceptance inputs. BuildApp Build product outputs for the selected years. ValidatePrePush Build App outputs and validate manifest type references. BuildTests Compile the Pure, Local and Design Automation test graphs. Execute no tests. BuildSelectedPureTests Compile the selected Pure projects. BuildSelectedLocalTests Compile the selected hosted projects without launching Revit. BuildSelectedDesignAutomationTests Compile selected DA projects. AssembleDistributionCandidate Assemble product files and candidate metadata. StagePortableAcceptanceInput Stage the candidate and references for portable acceptance. ValidateDistributionCandidate Run candidate metadata and static Dev Mode policy validation. PromoteToDist Publish the current accepted candidate to the distribution tree. ValidateManifestTypes Check manifest types against compiled output. VerifyArtifacts Check the built product files. BuildSandbox Compile the standalone Windows Sandbox for the selected years. BuildValidationRunner Build the portable .NET 10 Dev Mode policy worker. BuildDevModeScenario Build the hosted Dev Mode scenario for the selected years. PackageSandboxValidationInput Package candidate and Sandbox for native Windows validation. BuildBundle Package a promoted distribution, or consume --candidate-dist. Restore Restore the production and validation graphs for the selected years through either build wrapper. Clean, Info Clean build state or print configuration. Acceptance targets require a clean committed source tree and both supported years. Leave the year filter unset for BuildAll, portable acceptance, and Sandbox validation packaging. Focused product/test builds and candidate assembly support normal edited-source development. BuildAll validates metadata and static Dev Mode policy on Linux. It does not run native Sandbox, WPF interactions, Revit, or live Dev Mode injection. It builds and publishes the Dev Mode scenario for the daemon's Dev Mode fleet job. Build parameters Parameter Default and meaning --Configuration CONFIG Release or Debug. Default Release. -d or --debug selects Debug. --Years YEARS, -y, --year All supported years for builds. Accept one year or a space/comma-separated list. --SkipClean BOOL true. --clean selects false. --Verbose [BOOL], -v false. Bare flag selects true. -q/--quiet selects false. --DryRun [BOOL] false. Bare flag selects true. --TestProjects A,B Required for selected test targets. Use exact project filename stems without .csproj. --CandidateDistributionPath DIR, --candidate-dist DIR Package an already-promoted distribution without rebuilding or promoting it. --Revit2026Dir DIR, --Revit2027Dir DIR Override installed Revit reference directories. Full option names ignore case and dashes. Boolean values must be true or false. Selected test graph targets reject --clean and --DryRun. Read the complete reference with ./build.sh --help or pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 --help. ./build.sh BuildApp -y 2026 ./build.sh Restore --Years 2026,2027 ./build.sh BuildSelectedLocalTests --TestProjects dbtools.GM.Local.Tests -y 2026 ./build.sh BuildSelectedPureTests --TestProjects dbtools.GM.Pure.Tests ./build.sh BuildTests Build logs and child binlogs live under .artifacts/build/<build-id>/. console.log contains detailed output even when the terminal is quiet. .artifacts/build/console.log copies the latest invocation's log. A completed marker records the invocation's end. The test graph targets write test-restore.binlog and test-build.binlog in the same run folder. Source checks Check source placement and the repository tooling separately from compilation: python3 .agents/work/canon_source_fidelity.py --gate --mechanical-root testing --mechanical-root build python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/work/tests .githooks/pre-push The unittest suites in .agents/work/tests/ test the CANON gate, the worktree guard, .agents/checks/integrity.py and .githooks/pre-push. They need Python 3, Git, Bash and flock. See Build Pipeline for distribution acceptance, Dev Mode preflight, and build-server configuration. .githooks/pre-push always runs the wiki src/ path check and the component resource URI check. It also runs the CANON gate and ./build.sh ValidatePrePush, and prints why. It skips these two, prints the reason, and prints that they did not run, only for a push of one ref that fast-forwards an existing remote branch to the checked-out HEAD with new commits whose paths are all documentation or agent guidance: wiki/, docs/, .agents/, .claude/ and top-level *.md files. .agents/canon/ and every file in .agents/work/ except its tests/ and Markdown files are inputs of these checks. A new branch, a deletion, a rewind or rewrite, several refs, a pushed commit other than HEAD and a commit that the remote already has run every check. The hook runs the tooling tests when it runs the CANON gate, and also when a changed path is in .agents/work/tests/ or .agents/checks/. It prints why it runs or skips them. Run by hand without arguments, the hook compares the working tree, untracked files included, with the upstream branch of HEAD, and uploads nothing to Git LFS. Without an upstream branch, or when HEAD does not contain it, every check runs. Run the commands above directly to check a tree that the hook would skip. test.sh command reference ./test.sh <verb> [options] Verb Action build Delegate remaining arguments to build.sh. test Build selected current artifacts, freeze them, then execute. list Statically list tests or projects without execution. validate-request Resolve and validate selectors/projects without test execution or submission. submit Build and submit Local hosted tests. Reject Pure and DA. rerun --request ID Replay failures from a previous daemon request's submitted bytes. The default scope is pure. Without tool selection, discover owners for the requested scopes. Local execution, including compile-only, requires an explicit year or DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_YEARS. Pure-only requests are year-free and reject --year/--years. DA uses 2026. Selectors and build options Option Meaning --tool TOOL[,TOOL] Tool directory keys, case-insensitive, or BUILD, APP, CORE, PRESENTATION, SANDBOX, DA-SENTINEL, DIST. SANDBOX selects the Sandbox Pure project. --scope SCOPE[,SCOPE] pure, local, da, or all. --project PATH[,PATH] test, validate-request, or list only. Repeatable repository-relative project paths with forward slashes. Intersect other selectors. --fixture NAME Repeatable exact fixture/class selector. Narrow compilation to owning projects. -f FILTER, --filter FILTER VSTest filter locally. Supported exact/prefix FQN translation for daemon jobs. --fqn FQN Repeatable exact test identity. -y YEAR, --year YEAR Repeatable hosted year. --years 2026,2027 Hosted years as CSV. --changed-since REV test only: select affected owners. Documentation and agent guidance select none; when no other path changed, run no tests. DIST enters the selection only when --tool names it. A path read only by DIST selects no other owner. Unknown inputs select all. --compile-only, --build-only test only: compile and record inputs without executing tests. --no-build Strictly consume matching prepared artifacts. Available with test, submit, and validate-request. --projects list only: sorted scope<TAB>project.csproj rows, including empty projects. --summary Summarize static method counts by project. Cannot combine with --projects. --request ID Previous daemon request for rerun. Choose exactly one selector form: fixtures, filter, or FQNs. Fixture names select exact classes rather than similarly named longer classes. A fixture narrows the requested scopes to those that own it. An ambiguous short fixture name fails with exit 2. Use its namespace-qualified name or an explicit tool. Without --tool, the wrapper infers ownership from --filter, --fqn, or --fixture. Ambiguous filter/FQN matches across tools fail with exit 2. Resolved fixtures can select several owners. Without a usable inferred owner, the request retains the owners selected by its other options. Source discovery handles qualified attributes, combined/separate attribute lists, and implicit NUnit fixtures. Static method counts do not expand parameterized cases and are not runtime pass counts. list narrows fixture ownership to projects, then lists those projects' indexed methods. It does not apply the runtime fixture/filter expression to each printed method. Unknown project paths, paths outside the selected tool/scope, invalid selector combinations, and empty required selections fail with exit 2. There is no arbitrary dotnet argument passthrough after --. The APP Pure selection is dbtools.App.Pure.Tests. APP Local also includes dbtools.App.HostedTurns.Local.Tests. All three App test projects link ProfileIsolationTestAssemblySetup. It redirects the dbtools profile to a temporary root and checks the real profile for test logs and fallback records from the test process. Teardown restores the profile root and reports realProfileUntouched=True when these checks pass. RibbonControlPlanExecutorTests binds the App-owned RibbonFixtureCommand and RibbonFixtureAlternateCommand types. Its ribbon_fixture icons come from the App Local test assembly's embedded resource. Real-tool composition and XAML tests use the tool projects they reference. CORE selects both Windows and portable Pure projects, or both Core Local and HostedTurns Local projects. GM Local includes dbtools.GM.Local.Tests and dbtools.GM.HostedTurns.Local.Tests. PRESENTATION selects dbtools.Presentation.Pure.Tests or dbtools.Presentation.Local.Tests; it owns every Presentation test, including the tests of tool-specific Presentation types. A Local request without --tool includes the App, Core and Presentation Local projects and every tool Local project. SGT Pure selects its Windows and portable projects. RECORDSET Pure defaults to dbtools.RecordSet.Pure.Tests. dbtools.RecordSet.Cad.Pure.Tests declares DBT_OptInTests=true and contains only CadLiveTests. Default project selections exclude projects with this property, including global Pure selections. --fixture CadLiveTests or --project src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/Tests/dbtools.RecordSet.Cad.Pure.Tests.csproj selects the CAD project. It requires AutoCAD. A selected project with zero executed tests still fails admission. Tool project selection follows the actual Tests/ projects rather than a hard-coded fixture list. Daemon options Option Meaning --relay URL Override DBTOOLS_DAEMON_RELAY_URL. --machine MACHINE Explicit diagnostic machine pin. Ordinary hosted requests use automatic selection. --headers-env NAME Name of an environment variable containing relay headers JSON. --header 'Name: Value' Repeatable explicit header. Keep credentials out of command history. --label LABEL Job label. --queue-timeout HH:MM:SS Bound queue/claim wait, including the hosted Revit lease. --execution-timeout HH:MM:SS Bound execution after lease acquisition. --isolation MODE Hosted isolation mode. Invalid for Pure-only requests. --keep-open Request that hosted Revit remain open. Invalid for Pure-only requests. --result-json PATH Write daemon terminal evidence. Local-only Pure runs remove this path and use TRX counts. --include PATH Repeatable extra file/directory to stage. The wrapper forwards queue and execution timeouts independently. It supplies no single --timeout option or local default for either value. Hosting behavior belongs to the daemon. The wrapper accepts --keep-open. APS Design Automation Sentinel DA-SENTINEL --scope pure runs the network-free client, billing parser, ledger and record tests on Linux: ./test.sh test --tool DA-SENTINEL --scope pure LightweightSentinel_ExecutesRealDesignAutomationWorkItem is the single live test. It loads the Sentinel bundle in the Revit 2026 engine without a model. One command writes JSON with the Sentinel identity, Revit version and completion time. The test checks the output and engine report. Run live tests only through testing/run-design-automation.sh. Direct ./test.sh test --scope da requests fail before build. The runner checks the fixed ledger before build and before it reads the credential file. It writes every attempt to .artifacts/test-results/da-<UTC>-<id>/run.json and publishes it to the daemon. Billing and limits Autodesk's cost calculation counts processing seconds from timeDownloadStarted through timeUploadEnded. This interval includes download, instructions and upload. The WorkItem status reference lists timeQueued, timeDownloadStarted, timeInstructionsStarted, timeInstructionsEnded, timeUploadEnded and timeFinished. Its completed examples include timeDownloadStarted and timeFinished, but omit timeUploadEnded. The live test and resolver use timeFinished when timeUploadEnded is absent. The live test and resolver require timeDownloadStarted and either end time to compute processing seconds. If those timestamps are missing, the live test fails and the resolver keeps the reservation unresolved. The WorkItem reference defines limitProcessingTimeSec as the processing cap, including transfers. testing/design-automation.json sets a 120-second WorkItem cap and a 30-minute monthly budget. The runner rejects budget_minutes values above 30. The runner does not publish a new DA record when budget_minutes is invalid. The public docs do not specify per-WorkItem rounding or a minimum. The guard rounds the cap up to a whole minute, then reserves one more minute. It reserves three minutes for each WorkItem. The model-free test is expected to take under two processing minutes, but this estimate has not been measured. Five weekly runs reserve at most 15 minutes. testing/db-da-service-limit.py reads and updates the APS service limits for the app's Client ID. The coordinator runs it once before it installs the credential file. The script reads the current limits and sends only the properties the API allows clients to update. It keeps each other engine's current limitProcessingTimeSec value. If the GET response reports an Inventor limit of 360 seconds, the PUT body is: GET /da/us-east/v3/servicelimits/me PUT /da/us-east/v3/servicelimits/me Content-Type: application/json {"frontendLimits":{"limitMonthlyProcessingTimeInHours":1}, "backendLimits":{"Revit":{"limitProcessingTimeSec":120}, "Inventor":{"limitProcessingTimeSec":360}}} The GET reference documents the response shape. The PUT reference lists the two updateable fields and returns the applied limits. The script reports success only when the PUT response confirms both values. Autodesk enforces the 120-second cap for each WorkItem and a one-hour monthly cap across all engines for the app. The 30-minute ledger budget is lower than the 60-minute APS monthly cap. The test also sends limitProcessingTimeSec: 120 on its WorkItem. Ledger and budget guard The runner stores the append-only ledger at $XDG_STATE_HOME/dbtools/design-automation/ledger.jsonl. When XDG_STATE_HOME is unset or not absolute, it uses $HOME/.local/state/dbtools/design-automation/ledger.jsonl. HOME must be set to an absolute path. HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME must not contain a .. path segment. No runner option or dbtools environment variable changes this path. The runner sets the directory and ledger file permissions for the account owner only. The first ledger record must initialize prior account usage for the current UTC month. Empty, missing and invalid ledgers stop the run before a WorkItem is submitted. The error includes the fixed path and the initialization command. The coordinator supplies the account's actual prior usage in seconds: testing/run-design-automation.sh --initialize-ledger --prior-used-seconds 900 The initialization record has this format: { "schema_version": 1, "kind": "initialization", "run_id": "initialization:2026-11", "started_at": "2026-11-01T00:00:00+00:00", "finished_at": "2026-11-18T12:00:00+00:00", "result": "initialized", "tests": null, "work_items": [], "billed_seconds": 0, "billing_is_upper_bound": true, "budget_minutes": 30, "worst_case_seconds": 0, "commit": "", "scheduled": false, "month": "2026-11", "month_used_seconds": 900, "state": "finished", "revision": 1 } month_used_seconds on this record is the prior account usage. At the start of a later month, run the same command with that month's prior account usage. The client reserves the rounded timeout plus one minute before its single WorkItem POST. The ledger flushes that reservation before submission. A lost submit response remains charged. The budget check refuses when the reservation would exceed 30 minutes. Near either side of a UTC month boundary, it also checks the adjacent month's remaining budget. The run counts in the UTC month of the reservation's started_at. The relay and Studio derive that month from the first snapshot's started_at and total the runs themselves. The 30-minute ledger guard covers WorkItems submitted through this runner. Do not submit WorkItems for this app outside the runner. A WorkItem that has no terminal status is charged in its submission month and the next month only. To resolve one with a known ID, poll the APS status endpoint until it returns a terminal status: curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $APS_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ "https://developer.api.autodesk.com/da/us-east/v3/workitems/<work-item-id>" \ > /path/work-item-status.json python3 build/Testing/da_run.py resolve --run-id <run-id> \ --status-file /path/work-item-status.json --project <project-id> The resolver verifies the ID and terminal status, writes a higher revision, updates the ledger and publishes the new snapshot. The APS token is an app-only token with the code:all scope. If the submit response was lost and the record has no WorkItem ID, list the app's WorkItems from the reservation time to find the ID before polling. For a finished WorkItem, the local guard uses the minimum and maximum of SubmittedAt, all APS stats times and FinishedAt to find every UTC month the activity spans. This local calculation preserves a conservative bound. Studio uses the fixed reservation month. Schedule and records The disabled systemd user unit templates are next to the runner: testing/dbtools-design-automation.service.in testing/dbtools-design-automation.timer.in Before installing the service, replace its placeholders: @WORKTREE@ (the checkout), @BUILD_ENV@ (the host's build environment script), @CREDENTIAL_FILE@ (the APS credential file) and @PROJECT_ID@ (the relay project). The timer starts on Mondays at 04:00 UTC and does not catch up missed runs. The ledger enforces a six-day interval between WorkItem reservations. A build or credential failure without a reservation does not start that interval. Each run is one JSON object with these exact fields: schema_version, kind, run_id, started_at, finished_at, result, tests, work_items, billed_seconds, billing_is_upper_bound, budget_minutes, worst_case_seconds, commit, scheduled, month, month_used_seconds, state, revision kind is design-automation for runs. month (UTC YYYY-MM) and month_used_seconds (the guard's month total after it reserves the WorkItem) stay in the local ledger only. The published record omits them, because the relay derives the month and recomputes the total. state is reserved for the durable reservation and finished for the final snapshot. The reservation has null result, tests and finished_at fields. Its billed_seconds equals the three-minute bound. revision starts at 1 and increases for each snapshot with that run ID. A reserved snapshot never follows a finished snapshot. tests has total, passed, failed and skipped. work_items is an array with id, status, submitted_at, timeout_seconds, stats, processing_seconds, billed_seconds and billing_is_upper_bound. stats holds the raw valid APS timestamp strings timeQueued, timeDownloadStarted, timeInstructionsStarted, timeInstructionsEnded, timeUploadEnded and timeFinished. Timestamps use YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fraction]Z or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fraction]±HH:MM. The WorkItem billing bound stays at three minutes unless an observed interval needs a larger bound. No window opens and no Revit call runs, so Revit-side caches, Revit events and WPF resource lookups after a reload are outside this test. Inspect %APPDATA%/dbtools/Logs/ first for reported application failures. Hosted job output returns application logs. Use the selected Revit year's journal for a crash only when those logs are inconclusive. See Test Pipeline and Build System.

developer-guide/documentation.html.title: Documentation | dbtools
developer-guide/documentation.html.summary: Documentation NAME documentation - how to write and check wiki pages SYNOPSIS --- template: user-tool # user-tool | user-topic | dev-tool | dev-component | reference | how-to | dev-topic sources: # code the page describes - src/Tools/Structural/JoistGirderWeight/ --- python3 build/Documentation/lint_wiki.py wiki bash .github/scripts/build-docs.sh conceptual bash .github/scripts/build-docs.sh full-api Both build modes use wiki/docfx.json and write to wiki/_site. Model pages: Update Joist Girder Weights, dbtools.JoistGirderWeight, Architecture overview. DESCRIPTION A wiki page reads like a good man page: short, plain and exact. It gives the facts for a task, and stops. TEMPLATES The title is the only H1. Sections are H2s in capital letters, in this order. Leave out a section that has nothing to say. Template Use it for Sections user-tool A ribbon tool or a service NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS, REQUIREMENTS, SETTINGS, RESULTS, MESSAGES, FILES, LIMITS, EXAMPLES, SEE ALSO user-topic Installation, basics, settings, troubleshooting NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, topic sections, MESSAGES, FILES, SEE ALSO dev-tool A tool assembly NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, STRUCTURE, CONTRACTS, FLOW, DATA, DIAGNOSTICS, TESTS, SEE ALSO dev-component An architecture area or a project The same as dev-tool reference build.sh, test.sh, manifest.yml, settings files NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS, EXIT STATUS, ENVIRONMENT, FILES, EXAMPLES, SEE ALSO how-to One task NAME, SYNOPSIS, PREREQUISITES, STEPS, CHECK, SEE ALSO dev-topic Index and troubleshooting pages, this page NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, topic sections, SEE ALSO For a ribbon tool, REQUIREMENTS, RESULTS, MESSAGES and LIMITS replace the man-page INPUTS, OUTPUT, DIAGNOSTICS and BUGS. Other sections keep their man-page meaning, except these: Section What it holds NAME <title> - <what it does>, under 80 characters SYNOPSIS User page: the ribbon path. Developer page: a text block with source, assembly and entry point. REQUIREMENTS What the model must contain, as a table with names, units and rules RESULTS What a run changes and shows, and its Undo-list name MESSAGES Only messages whose meaning or fix the text does not make clear LIMITS Real limits, and traps that silently give a wrong result CONTRACTS Rules the code keeps, each with the test that checks it, if any RULES Write complete, short sentences, one idea each. Aim for 20 words or fewer. Keep the verbs and articles. Write "If a pattern is not valid, the command changes nothing", not "Bad pattern: no change". Use the names the reader sees: UI labels, parameters and messages, or code names on a developer page. Invent no labels or symbols. Define each term once, where it first appears, with its unit. Use the present tense, the active voice, and the imperative for steps. Use a table for items that readers scan. Each cell is still plain English. Put each fact in one place, and link to it. Describe current behavior only. Leave out dates, history, plans and the words below. Put <!-- lint: migration --> before a needed migration step. Give no line numbers. Name the file and the symbol. Show UI labels in bold, and messages, parameters and values in backticks, exactly as they appear. Write variable parts as <name>. Give each user tool page one or two screenshots. Until one exists, leave <!-- screenshot: <window or banner>, <state> -->. filler simply just easily easy basically actually really very "note that" please "in order to" "it is important" obviously "of course" various robust seamless leverage comprehensive powerful utilize via e.g. i.e. etc. history currently now (in time) new newly previously "no longer" formerly legacy (except in a code name) "has been" "was changed" "was renamed" "was removed" recently "before <month> <year>" process agent review wave lane epoch Desloppify campaign regression Aim for at most 600 words outside code on a tool page and 800 on an architecture page. The largest tools need more. CONTENT Choose facts for the reader's task, not for the code. A user page holds what a typical user acts on, including the traps that silently give a wrong result. Leave out rare edge cases and internal mechanics, such as check order, banner kinds and settings-file names. A developer page holds what a developer needs to change the code safely, and links to the user page for behavior. It copies no manifest.yml or signatures. CHECKS Facts. Check each claim against the code, by file and symbol, and copy labels and messages from it. Do not print the code inventory. Revit-only claims. Keep one only with a Revit test or the owner's confirmation. Second writer. Another writer checks the claims. Fix each finding. Reader test. Give a fresh reader only the page text and 3 or 4 realistic tasks. Ask for answers and for every sentence it read twice. Fix those sentences and any wrong answer. Fill only the gaps that a typical reader hits, not every gap the test finds. Build. The build fails on a source line reference or a DocFX warning. Markdown traps: A definition list needs : plus three spaces, and four-space continuation lines. In a table cell, a pipe in code shows a stray backslash. Link only to wiki pages, or DocFX reports InvalidFileLink. Check links against the generated heading IDs. SEE ALSO Writing documentation, Wiki Server

developer-guide/index.html.title: Developer Guide | dbtools
developer-guide/index.html.summary: Developer Guide This guide describes how dbtools is built, structured and tested, and how to develop its tools. Start with the Architecture Overview, which describes the components, startup and tool loading. Section Contents Architecture Components, startup, build and test pipelines, assembly loading, themes Projects The Core, App, Sandbox and Presentation projects Tools (Technical) Implementation of each tool Developing Creating tools, settings packs, hooks, warnings, Sandbox integration, testing Troubleshooting Common errors and the logs Documentation Page templates, writing rules, claim checks, screenshots Wiki Server How a push to kirsch33/dbtools-wiki updates the published site Requirements the .NET SDK pinned in global.json; build.sh and build.ps1 install it when it is missing; Python 3.10 or later on Linux and WSL; Desktop Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) or Revit 2027 to run the add-in. Building does not need Revit. Building ./build.sh # BuildAll: build, validate and publish both years ./build.sh BuildApp -y 2026 # product assemblies for one year ./build.sh AssembleDistributionCandidate -y 2026 pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 BuildAll # native Windows BuildAll, ValidateDistributionCandidate, PromoteToDist and BuildBundle always build every supported year; a -y that omits one fails. See Build Pipeline. Testing ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure # one tool, without Revit ./test.sh test --tool APP --scope local -y 2026 # in Revit, through the daemon ./test.sh test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SomeTestName" ./test.sh test --scope all Revit-hosted tests (the local scope) run on the dbtools-daemon fleet. See Test Pipeline for the design and Testing Tools for the options. Choosing checks The proof matches the change. Before a build, test, acceptance or release step, decide whether the change can make that step fail, and run only the steps that it can. Skip a step that the change cannot affect, and record the skipped step and the reason in the commit message, the report or the release record. A skipped step is not a passed step. Always run what produces or protects what users install: the build of what ships (./build.sh BuildAll from a fresh clone, with its Dev Mode preflight), its normal automated tests, and the release asset build and checksum steps. Run the expensive steps only for a change that can affect them: Revit-hosted tests, hosted jobs, long native passes and repeated full gates. For example, a change to how a window comes to the front cannot change Revit behavior, so it needs no Revit-hosted tests. While iterating, run focused tests on the changed code; ./test.sh test --changed-since REV selects the test owners that a change can affect. Run the complete suites of what a settled batch of changes can affect once for that batch, not after each edit. The pre-push hook selects its checks by the pushed paths; see Source checks. Writing documentation DocFX builds the wiki from wiki/. Run bash .github/scripts/build-docs.sh conceptual to build wiki/_site. See Wiki Server for publishing. Write developer and user pages in the style of Unix reference documentation (Debian and GNU manuals, man pages). State what a component is, what it does, how it works, how to use it and its limits. Put the main point first. Use plain declarative sentences in the present tense and the active voice; use the imperative in procedures. Use the names the code uses, one term per concept. Use lists for steps and parallel items, tables for tabular data, and code blocks for commands, paths and literal values. Document commands as a synopsis, options and examples. Describe the current behavior only. Leave out change history, status and verification notes, dates, issue numbers, and the vocabulary of the process that produced a change. Keep a history note only for a migration step or compatibility break the reader needs. Leave out filler, hedging and repeated summaries. State each real limitation once, where it applies. Verify every technical claim against the current code, scripts and configuration before you write or keep it. Documentation has the page templates and the rules that a script or a person can check. The same rules apply to source comments, CLI help and messages. A comment explains a reason, an invariant or a non-obvious API behavior, not what the code already says. CLI help uses man-page form: a synopsis, then one line per option with its default. An error message names what failed, the relevant value or path and, where useful, what to do.

developer-guide/projects/app.html.title: dbtools.App | dbtools
developer-guide/projects/app.html.summary: dbtools.App dbtools.App builds dbtools.dll, the Revit add-in entry and the App runtime. It targets net10.0-windows (DBT_RevitTargetFramework) for desktop Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. Project Item Value Project src/dbtools.App/dbtools.App.csproj Assembly dbtools.dll Target net10.0-windows Product references dbtools.Core, dbtools.Presentation Manifests Embedded in App for every tool Revit API references are compile-only and are never staged as product runtime files. DBT_RemoveForbiddenHostAssemblies removes RevitAPI, RevitAPIUI, AdWindows, UIFramework, System.Runtime and System.ObjectModel DLLs after copying. Deletion errors fail the build. RibbonNativeAccess reads Revit's internal ribbon panel and item wrappers. Product output stages App at the year root and the tool assemblies below Tools/. Responsibilities App owns: the public parameterless Revit entry (AddinEntry) and the daemon idle acknowledgement; the non-inlined startup and shutdown boundary, and the startup fallback diagnostics; lifecycle, Core hook composition, ribbon composition, the settings host and shutdown; the embedded tool manifests. The fourteen tool projects under src/Tools/ own their tool assemblies, including the Super Girt Tool (SGT), Settings and DialogSuppression. Each tool owner embeds its icons, raw views and manifest-declared design-time view models. Presentation owns the stable themes and compiled WPF controls. Source tree src/dbtools.App/ ├── Addin/ # Revit entry and installed-copy idle acknowledgement ├── Composition/ # DI and manifest-facing registration ├── Host/ # failure, test-run and window-owner boundaries ├── Lifecycle/ # publication, cleanup and lifecycle state ├── Logging/ # App logging-window integration ├── Ribbon/ # planning, Revit effects, state and startup styling ├── Runtime/ # App runtime, runtime initialization and local Revit task ownership ├── Settings/ # App settings host and integration ├── Shutdown/ # synchronous shutdown workflow └── Startup/ # entry boundary, preparation, startup ownership, background and deferred work, effects Startup AddinEntry has a public parameterless constructor for Revit. The first action of OnStartup checks DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_ROLE and the load context of the entry assembly. Idle copy: only a file-backed entry in AssemblyLoadContext.Default acknowledges the installed idle copy. It records the key dbtools-daemon.IdleAddin:<simple-name> (for App, dbtools-daemon.IdleAddin:dbtools) with the entry location as its value, and returns success without touching the ribbon, events or other startup work. Normal startup: every other context (ProductLoadContext, DevModeLoadContext, a null context and any other context) enters ToolWindowCallbackScope and the non-inlined AppStartupBoundary. Startup initializes the App runtime, validates themes, composes the ribbon, starts the Revit call gate and publishes deferred startup work. Startup parses the Revit year from ControlledApplication.VersionNumber. AppRuntimeInitializer passes it to AppRuntimeHostLifecycle.InitializeHost(ribbonTarget, revitYear). InitializeHost publishes the year to RevitInstanceIdentity before it creates logging or services; RevitInstanceIdentity accepts the same year again and rejects a different one. Logging, the per-year settings file and the container take the year from the InitializeHost argument, not from RevitInstanceIdentity. AppRuntimeInitializer then resolves the startup services, configures WindowStaticRuntime and builds the AppStartupContext. If initialization fails, it shuts down the runtime that it created and then resets the window runtime, but only when this attempt configured it. A rejected duplicate configuration leaves the incumbent window runtime in place. The report puts the initiating failure first. If entering the Revit API scope fails, AppLifecycleCoordinator records startup API context in the fallback log, shows the preparation message and returns failure before creating a runtime. Preparation runs ValidateTheme, CreateDeferredStartupRunner, ComposeRibbon, PublishInitialStartupEffects and StartBackgroundStartup in that order. A failed phase is logged as Startup phase {Phase} failed with the original exception, is presented with the theme, ribbon, startup effects, background startup or preparation message, and returns the captured handles for cleanup. A failure outside the phases is reported as phase TransferStartupOwnership with the preparation message. Startup state publication failures use the publication message whether registration fails before publication or observation registration fails after publication. Publication cleanup finishes before one presentation attempt. A rejected candidate is cleaned directly without publishing it over the incumbent lifecycle state. Deferred UI failures use the Deferred UI Startup safe-execution path. The lifecycle cleanup subscription and the deferred startup subscription each register their own Idling handler through a separate AppLifecycleIdlingRegistration. The optional Idling subscribe and unsubscribe pair of AppStartupConfiguration reaches both. Cleanup registers first, so a pending failed-startup cleanup gets the first Idling callback. The cleanup subscription attempts its handler removal once. Startup ownership captures the deferred subscription before it registers, so a deferred handler removal that fails, also during a failed registration, keeps the handler for the next cleanup to retry. Startup failure dialogs are suppressed while DBT_TEST_RUN_ID is active. A failed dialog callback is contained and recorded in the fallback log with the initiating failure first. App log templates identify their emitting owner with [EmittingType]; tool-module registration uses the AppToolModuleRegistrar bootstrap logger category. A registration failure names the tool, the manifest resource, the registration stage and the module type, or manifest-only for a manifest without a module. Failure cleanup runs synchronously at the Revit API boundary and combines the primary and cleanup failures. A startup, shutdown or ribbon-runtime failure that cannot reach the normal log is written by a BCL-only writer to Logs\dbtools.Fallback.log below AppPaths.BaseDir (default %APPDATA%\dbtools), so a missing Core or UI dependency does not hide the diagnostic. After a refused DBT_USER_DATA_DIR, AppFallbackFailureLog writes no file and its records reach Trace only. Shutdown OnShutdown uses the same load-context boundary as startup and runs lifecycle cleanup synchronously. An idle installed entry or an entry that refused DBT_USER_DATA_DIR returns success directly. Without a published lifecycle state, shutdown succeeds before opening a Revit API scope. While cleanup that another owner started is unfinished, shutdown fails and leaves the state published. Completed cleanup returns its recorded result, and shutdown clears only the publication that it cleaned. Each generation keeps the handles it acquires. AppStartupOwnership holds the background startup task state, the ribbon composition, the deferred and cleanup subscriptions, and the service root's RevitCallGateTask. AppRuntimeResources holds the AppRuntime. Shutdown releases these captured handles. AppLocalRevitTaskLifecycle.Shutdown(task, cancelPending) retires and disposes the captured task. Cleanup after a published background startup failure, startup replacement, or an abandoned builder cancels queued work. Normal shutdown drops queued work. AppRuntimeHostLifecycle.ShutdownHost(runtime) detaches the captured runtime from AppRuntimeAccessor only while it is current, then disposes it. Replacement cleanup and an abandoned startup builder release only their own handles. A replacement runtime stays published. A replacement task stays live. A lifecycle cleanup subscription that still holds a queued startup failure when it is disposed records that failure in the fallback log and throws only a handler-removal failure, so a replacement is not rejected for a stale fault. The App runtime host lifecycle (ShutdownHost) step runs before the Window static runtime contract step (WindowStaticRuntime.Reset, which also retires dispatcher operations). These steps and the cleanup summary are written to the fallback log after logging is disposed. The Revit task host step logs failures through the live logger. Composition AppRuntimeFactory builds the service root once from the ribbon target and the Revit year. AppServiceProviderFactory registers the Revit year once as an int singleton, then logging, settings (AppPaths.GetSettingsFile(revitYear)), UI ownership, Revit call gates, safe execution, command preflight, hooks, alerts and ribbon composition. It returns the concrete ServiceProvider. AppServiceRoot owns the provider: disposal stops the logger window host, disposes the provider and its singletons, then disposes logging. AppHostedComposition.EnsureRuntime(uiApplication, createControlledApplication) starts the App lifecycle with a headless failure presenter and an isolated ribbon target. When startup is needed, it asks the fixture for a UIControlledApplication wrapper of the daemon-provided UIApplication. Startup configures the static window runtime, publishes the App service root's call-gate task, attaches the application hooks and completes deferred UI startup. A change to AppPaths.BaseDir replaces the hosted lifecycle. ShutdownRuntime() releases the lifecycle that hosted composition started. CreateLoggingRuntime() uses the initialized year. BuildServiceProvider(logging, isolationName, configure) requires Core's concrete logging runtime and the published App call-gate task. It gives each provider a distinct ribbon prefix and applies configure after App registrations. The fixture provider borrows the task. The caller disposes the provider and logging runtime. AppToolModuleRegistrar asks Core's ToolModuleCatalog to discover the embedded manifest resources once. It instantiates the module owners, collects their settings, services and hooks in temporary registration state, validates module responsibilities and merges the state into the App container. Core's ToolAssemblyResolver loads the module, command, availability and icon owner of each manifest by explicit path from the product year's Tools/ directory, in the active owning load context. It checks the declared PE identity, rejects a loaded image with the same name from another path or identity, and probes no other directory. Manifest registration infers command-owned availability when availabilityType is omitted and rejects a redundant explicit command type. An explicit separate availability class keeps the existing resolution route. Synchronous command preflight reuses the executing command for its own availability check. Contextual edits and separate availability classes create one instance at validation. Settings uses its inferred command availability and remains available without an active document. ToolCommand.Execute and IsCommandAvailable enter the Presentation callback scope of the owning assembly. ExecutionContext flow is suppressed across callbacks, so host dispatchers and timers cannot keep a reference to an owning load context. Ribbon Ribbon planning builds each PushButtonData directly from a ToolRegistration: the file-backed Location of the command assembly, the command full name and the optional availability class full name. A button definition carries the logical tool internal name. RibbonTarget.GetItemName adds the target prefix for Revit. Grouped controls keep manifest order and use the same definitions. Settings, SGT and DialogSuppression use the same registration path as every other tool. RibbonControlPlanBuilder.Create turns the tool registrations into one RibbonPlan. Its panels follow the order Common, Structural, Testing, Services and Settings, then other panel names in ordinal order. Each RibbonPanelPlan lists its controls by order. At equal order, split buttons come first, then pulldown buttons, stacks and push buttons; push buttons with equal order keep their registry order. RibbonComposition creates the plan once from the registry's tool snapshot and passes the same plan to retained-panel discovery, retained-control validation, panel creation and control execution. RibbonCompositionState keeps the native PushButton of each registered tool for enabled-state changes. RibbonComposition owns ribbon creation, settings subscriptions and disposal. Compose returns that same owner after successful initialization. A duplicate composition throws InvalidOperationException: Ribbon controls are already composed for this process. App startup cannot continue. The rejected attempt preserves the incumbent ribbon state and subscriptions. A failed initialization rolls back its own panels and subscriptions and permits a retry before disposal. On a reload (Dev Mode), RibbonComposition finds the retained panels without changing them and validates every requested panel and button before it removes, creates or restores anything. A refused reload leaves the ribbon unchanged and throws InvalidOperationException with a message that ends Restart Revit to load this ribbon definition. Retained ribbon change Result Same assembly path and command class Button reused. Changed availability class on a retained button Applied. Cleared availability class Refused; restart Revit. Removed, reordered or retyped items or buttons Refused; restart Revit. Changed stack placement, membership or row boundaries, or an item added to a retained stack Refused; restart Revit. Changed assembly path or command class Refused; restart Revit. New panel items or grouped-button children after the retained items Appended. Tests Pure tests cover the idle gate (role and load-context decisions), ribbon planning, settings and startup state. They compile only the source needed for platform-neutral behavior, must not run Revit startup and must not load Revit-typed members. Local (Revit-hosted) tests reference the real App project. They cover entry behavior, ribbon composition, command availability, lifecycle cleanup and Revit window ownership. Hosted startup reads the Revit year through the App lifecycle. Fixtures that use the shared App runtime borrow its call-gate task. Revit-hosted tests take runtime ownership from the staged product tree. Tool project references stay compile references and do not add separate product images to the test dependency closure. Hosted inputs include the complete year root with Tools/ preserved; test assemblies, NUnit files and companions are separate inputs. The daemon's ProductLoadContext forwards product references to the same product instances that App uses. Release checks validate App's entry identity, embedded manifest ownership, command and availability owners, the stable Presentation resources, source-map freshness and the placement in the year tree. See Assembly Loading Contract, Architecture Overview and Test Pipeline.

developer-guide/projects/core.html.title: dbtools.Core | dbtools
developer-guide/projects/core.html.summary: dbtools.Core dbtools.Core is the shared infrastructure library of dbtools. It contains the Revit execution layer (call gates and run scopes), transaction management, safe execution, logging, settings, the tool module system and shared UI components. Property Value Assembly dbtools.Core.dll Targets Desktop net10.0-windows (Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027); portable net10.0 WPF Desktop target only (UseWPF=true) Nullable Enabled Responsibilities Revit execution: thread-safe Revit API access through call gates and run scopes. Transactions: transaction and sub-transaction handling with rollback on failure. Safe execution: central error handling with user notification and logging. Logging: Serilog-based structured logging with a UI sink. Settings: typed settings sections with persistence and validation. Tool modules: discovery, registration and lifecycle of tools. Shared UI: window support, alert dialogs, progress overlays and behaviors. Build Desktop builds compile the complete Core for one Revit year. Pure tests and the Sandbox use that same image. Revit references are compile-only. Portable builds ($(DBT_PortableTargetFramework)) compile only the explicit source list in dbtools.Core.csproj, without WPF, Revit, merging or content identity. Designer builds (DBT_IsDesignerBuild=true) exclude Revit sources so the XAML designer can load without the Revit SDK. _wpftmp builds (temporary projects during BAML compilation) exclude Revit and Tools sources except src/dbtools.Core/Revit/Execution/RunScope/AppRunScopeProfile.cs. A default desktop build writes its assembly to the artifact locations that the shared build props select. Revit-hosted test projects reference the evaluated Core TargetPath, not the product staging tree. Core composes the logging runtime. Its logger factory, logger abstractions and Serilog provider types bind through dbtools.Presentation, which stays in the stable load tier across Dev Mode generations. Presentation's SerilogStack coordinates the process-wide logger when generations overlap. Dependencies Reference Purpose dbtools.Manifest (project, desktop only) Portable manifest parser; merged privately with YamlDotNet dbtools.Presentation (project, desktop only) Stable WPF resources, controls, logger factory and provider types Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection (through Presentation) Dependency injection with a stable type identity Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions (portable target only) Logger abstractions for portable Core contracts without Presentation CommunityToolkit.Mvvm MVVM base classes CSharpFunctionalExtensions (desktop only) Public merged functional types shared by SGT and ERFT InternalsVisibleTo These assemblies see Core internals: runtime: dbtools, dbtools.GM, dbtools.SGT, dbtools.DialogSuppression, dbtools.FoundationTags; Core tests: dbtools.Core.Pure.Tests, dbtools.Core.Local.Tests, dbtools.Core.HostedTurns.Local.Tests, dbtools.Core.Portable.Pure.Tests; Presentation tests: dbtools.Presentation.Pure.Tests; App tests: dbtools.App.Pure.Tests, dbtools.App.Local.Tests; tool tests: dbtools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.Local.Tests, dbtools.DialogSuppression.Local.Tests, dbtools.ElevationTags.Local.Tests, dbtools.ERFT.Local.Tests, dbtools.FoundationTags.Local.Tests, dbtools.FramingJoins.Local.Tests, dbtools.GM.Local.Tests, dbtools.GM.HostedTurns.Local.Tests, dbtools.JoistGirderWeight.Local.Tests, dbtools.OrganizeFoundationTypes.Local.Tests, dbtools.RecordSet.Pure.Tests, dbtools.RecordSet.Local.Tests, dbtools.Settings.Pure.Tests, dbtools.SGT.Local.Tests, dbtools.TDV.Local.Tests, dbtools.VTC.Local.Tests. Directory structure dbtools.Core/ +-- Alert/{Body,Composition,DesignTime,Domain,Selection,ViewModels,Views,Workflow} +-- AppRuntime/{Domain,Runtime} # Runtime contracts and the static accessor +-- Failure # FailurePrecedence +-- Guarding # Guard and analyzer marker +-- Hashing # SHA-256 operations +-- Json # Strict camel-case enum converter +-- Logging/{Composition,DebugMode,Files,LoggerWindow,Retention,Runtime,Sinks} +-- Notifications/{Composition,Domain,NotificationBanner,Runtime} +-- Paths # AppPaths +-- Progress/{Aggregation,Overlay} +-- Regex # Shared regex construction +-- Revit/{Composition,Context,DocumentSession,Documents,Execution,Names,SharedParameters,Transactions} +-- RevitInstance/{Identity,RevitYear} +-- Ribbon # ProductRibbon +-- SafeExecution/{Domain,Runtime} +-- Settings/{Catalog,Composition,Domain,Persistence,RegexPattern,SettingsPack,State,Validation,Warnings} +-- TextFile # Text-file operations +-- Time # EasternTime +-- Tools/{Availability,Commands,Hooks,Manifest,Modules,Ribbon,Sandbox} +-- UI/{ColorPicker,Commanding,DesignTime,Dispatching,FilePicker,Theming,Windows} +-- Tests # Core test projects Tests Project Target Content dbtools.Core.Portable.Pure.Tests net10.0 Portable Core behavior that runs on Linux: Guard, strict JSON enums, safe-execution names and monotonic progress. References Core directly. dbtools.Core.Pure.Tests net10.0-windows Desktop Core and merged-owner behavior without Revit, including collectible composition activation, the progress overlay and the logger window dispatcher routing. dbtools.Core.Local.Tests net10.0-windows Revit-hosted fixtures. Has a test-only reference to dbtools.Presentation, which owns the overlay control, the tool window host and the window owner handles. dbtools.Core.HostedTurns.Local.Tests net10.0-windows Fixtures that need real native Revit turns (the RevitHostedTurns category). Core test projects use explicit <Compile> membership. Test files mirror the owner folders under Tests/; when a test file moves, update the compile links in the Pure and Local projects in the same change. Revit execution and transactions Revit Execution and Progress Overlay owns the design of run scopes, call gates, queued turns, ITransactionRunner, transaction groups and the progress overlay. Folder Content Revit/Execution/CallGate IRevitCallGate, InlineRevitCallGate, QueuedRevitCallGate, delegate admission, API-context admission (RevitCallGateApiContext) and the queued turn scheduler (RevitCallGateTask) Revit/Execution/RunScope IRevitRunScope, AppRunScope and AppRunScopeFactory Revit/Context RevitApplicationContext and ContextUnavailableException Revit/DocumentSession DocumentSessionKey, the typed identity of one open document (title, path and instance hash) with ordinal value equality; ToString returns its text, title\|path\|hash Revit/Documents DocumentChangeStamp tracks model changes per open document. Revit/Names ElementDisplayName formats a family and type, or the element name, with its ID as a suffix. Revit/Transactions ITransactionRunner, TransactionFailurePreprocessor, TransactionFailureException and ITransactionFailureDefinitionSource; under TransactionGroup/, ITransactionGroupService, IAtomicTransactionGroup and RevitTransactionGroups Revit/GroupPlacement GroupPlacementQuery detects members of groups placed more than once, including enclosing groups Revit/SharedParameters SharedParameterMigration, SharedParameterFamilyMigration, SharedParameterFamilyScan, SharedParameterFamilyRefusal, SharedParameterUseScan, SharedParameterUseQuery, SharedParameterUseQueryKey, SharedParameterUse, SharedParameterUseText, SharedParameterUseKind, SharedParameterUseDisposition, SharedParameterUseReport, SharedParameterRepairState, SharedParameterRepairSelection, SharedParameterRepairEligibility, SharedParameterRepairPlan, SharedParameterRepairReport, SharedParameterRepair, SharedParameterUseHandling, SharedParameterScheduleSnapshot, SharedParameterFilterSnapshot, SharedParameterScheduleField and SharedParameterFilterRule Revit/Composition RevitServiceCollectionExtensions: the Revit-scoped registrations Progress/Overlay, Progress/Aggregation IProgressOverlay, ProgressOverlay and MonotonicProgressAdapter ElementIdConverter.ToLong returns the full 64-bit element ID; use it for element identities, including the IDs in diagnostics. ToInt is a checked conversion for contracts that Revit defines as int, such as built-in category IDs. RevitTransactionContext.DeleteOnlyWarnings restricts warning deletion to the specified failure definitions. A caller can also filter by the warning record, including its description and failing element IDs. An unmatched warning rolls back the transaction. TransactionFailureException.BlockingFailureDescriptions includes the blocked warning's text. BlockingFailureRecords exposes the recorded severity, description, definition, and element IDs. Document change stamps DocumentChangeStamp.Get(document) returns the model-change count for one open document, or zero while tracking is detached. Each DocumentChanged event advances the count once. Reload Latest and Synchronize with Central also advance it because their changes may not appear in the event's element IDs. View activation and selection do not advance it. The stamp compares live Document wrappers by their value equality and removes a document's counter when Revit closes it. The application uses one shared DocumentChangeStamp. HookHost attaches its four document handlers during synchronous App startup and removes them during shutdown. AppRuntimeHostLifecycle also detaches those handlers when it cleans up the current runtime. Each registration starts a generation with fresh counters and invalidates cached document versions. The stamp retains documents and issues versions only while the handlers are attached. Shared parameter migration GroupPlacementQuery.IsInGroupPlacedMoreThanOnce(document, elementId) walks the element's group and every enclosing group. It checks GroupType.Groups.Size for all placed instances of each type, including nested instances. It returns false for an ungrouped element or a chain of group types placed once. SharedParameterMigration uses this check before grouped value writes. GroupPlacementQuery.CreateRunQuery(document) creates a query for a run whose group placements do not change.
