developer-guide/tools/common/gm-spec.htm.summary: Global Mapper architecture specification Overview Global Mapper (GM) collects Revit content, builds mapping intent, and executes reviewed replacement plans. This specification describes its state, execution, persistence, and lifetime contracts. Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. GM describes entry points and test surfaces. Architecture Composition and document scope App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory captures the launch UIDocument and Document and creates a QueuedModeless App run scope through GmSessionDocumentGate.CreateBoundScope. That helper binds the scope's concrete gate to the launch document before it returns the scope, so no consumer resolves an unbound gate. A binding failure disposes the new scope. The gate compares DocumentSessionKey values on each callback. The key uses the document hash code for session scoping. It does not guarantee collision-free identity. The persistence key is the nonblank document path, or the title|path|hash text of that captured session key for an unsaved document. Unsaved documents load saved data only under their captured session key. AddGm() registers the concrete GM gate without replacing shared IRevitCallGate registrations. Each feature registers its host-neutral services through a *ServiceCollectionExtensions class in its Composition folder and its Revit adapters through a *RevitServiceCollectionExtensions class in its Revit/Composition folder. AddGm() calls AddGmFeatureServices() in App/Composition and then each feature's Revit extension. It registers Mapping's IChangeWriter implementations before Shared Parameters adds its own. App registers only project state, UI state, session composition, and the gate. GM Revit readers, writers, family batches, transaction runners, and Commit Review consume the concrete gate. RevitMappingPlanExecutor rejects an invalid document or session-key mismatch before writers begin. RunCleanupAsync uses the underlying gate with CancellationToken.None so owned documents can close after authority or work cancellation ends. Commit Review uses the bound parent gate to create an InlineUi child scope through the same helper, bound to the expected document. It resolves apply services only after the helper returns. One outer Revit callback contains planning, modal review, apply, finalization, and refresh. During that modal session, forced-queue, off-thread, or second-callback work is refused. Apply-group finalization requested while painting runs at dispatcher ContextIdle after the paint frame exits. The owning Revit callback disposes the review and rolls back any unkept apply after the review dispatcher loop returns. Refresh follows that cleanup. AppSessionProjectionBuilder.CreateProjection receives the host-neutral SessionExecutionContext, the dialog context, the mapping session, the workspace (including a required IViewOps implementation), and feature services. It returns AppSessionProjection: the panes, the session's one MappingConflictViewModel, type creation, the shared-parameter loader, and the row refresh graph. Runtime and design-time composition use that conflict instance. SessionExecutionContext carries the session's executor, logger, error notifier, operation gate, workspace signals, row signals, live-plan update suppression, and origin-clear suppression. The runtime wraps that same session context in MappingDocumentExecutionContext, exposed as Session, with its ExpectedDocument. The bound gate carries the session authorization key. Host-neutral panes and rows receive the session execution context. Commit Review receives the document execution context. Authorization identity and persistence identity have separate consumers. WindowSessionServices supplies the attached owner and progress overlay. BannerNotifierFactory uses that owner. Before Attach, every overlay member, CancelRequested included, throws InvalidOperationException. Dispose is idempotent and terminal: overlay members and Attach then throw ObjectDisposedException. The owner provider outlives disposal, so a failure notification queued after the window closes still resolves its owner. GmWindowAttachment supplies feature dialogs with a late-bound getter for the attached window. Design-time composition uses explicit host-neutral collaborators, including DesignTimeViewOps. AppSessionBuilder constructs startup, initialization, Deep Scan, preference clearing, background prewarm, Family Mapping commands, pane lifecycle, disposal workflows, and the AppSessionRuntime with its OperationStateReaction and GmWindowPresentationProjector. It passes UIStateSession.Create and SessionWorkflows.Create the session's executor, logger, and error notifier, plus the operation gate for UI state, rather than the session execution context. PaneViewModelBuilder returns PaneComposition: the panes and the Family Mapping scan, row refresh, type creation, and row set. RowRefreshFactory builds one row collaboration graph per session and returns RowRefreshComposition: CrossPaneRowRefresh, RowRefreshCoreServices, CommitReviewRowServices, UIStateFactory, and OptionRenderingRefresh. App/Sessions/RowRefresh/CrossPaneRowRefresh sequences Usage rows, Family Mapping refresh, indicators, live-update suppression, row locks, and workspace events. Each cross-pane trigger is one named method on it: RefreshRowsAfterFilterChange, RefreshRowsAfterUsagePageActivationAsync, RebuildRowsAfterInitialLoad, RefreshRowsAfterUsagePublication, ScanFamiliesAsync, RebuildRowsAfterDeepScanAsync, RefreshRowsAfterSavedMappingClear, RefreshRowsAfterCommitAndContinueAsync, and RefreshRowsAfterCommitAndClose. It implements feature-owned ICommitReviewRowRefresh, IFamilyMappingCrossPaneCommands, and IDeepScanUsageRefresh. FilterRefreshWorkflow, StartupRowWorkflow, and PageActivationWorkflow call those triggers. App/Sessions owns session records and runtime lifetime. Composition owns construction. Feature implementations do not import dbtools.GM.App. FamilyMappingFactory returns FamilyMappingComposition: FamilyMappingViewModel, FamilyMappingScanWorkflow, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, and one MappingRowSet spanning family/type and supplied Usage rows. FamilyMappingScanStateApplier belongs to scan sequencing. The row builders and refresh owners receive the same row set. The factory shares one FamilyMappingState across these objects. FamilyMappingState.SelectedFamilyRow holds the selected family row. FamilyMappingViewModel.SelectedFamilyRow reads and writes it, raises one notification per change, and loads the row's views when the workspace is ready and the row is not null. FamilyMappingScanWorkflow and FamilyMappingScanStateApplier capture and restore the selection on the state. Public surface and resources GM production payload types default to internal. Manifest activation requires public GmToolModule and GmCommand. Public conflict projection values retain their public binding properties. Dependency objects, converters, selectors, and attached behaviors are stable public Presentation types. The design-time view models are internal with public binding/fragment properties. Sandbox and production consume the same raw resources and fragments. Compiled resource validation checks manifest logical names. Materials and Object Styles reuse UsageFamilyListStyle, UsageFamilyItemContainerStyle, and UsageFamilyRowTemplate from Presentation/Tools/GM/GmViewResources.xaml. Each pane supplies its own family list and selection. The shell supplies double-click navigation. The row supplies the context-menu apply command. Mapping options expose nullable SimilarityScore values. Presentation GmSimilarityBrushConverter owns the brush bands: 90–100 Success, 70–89 Secondary, 50–69 Warning, and 0–49 Muted. A null score uses Body. Alphabetical rendering retains ranking Score values but leaves SimilarityScore null. The converter resolves score brushes through the owning Window resource dictionary. Missing keys yield Gray. Detached elements use their own resource scope. Blank, disabled, separator, and Deep Scan template states use DynamicResource brushes. Source reference Paths below are relative to src/Tools/Common/GM/. Contract Source Launch and document gate App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory.cs, Revit/Documents/GmSessionDocumentGate.cs Session graph App/Composition/Revit/AppSessionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/AppSessionProjectionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/RowRefresh/RowRefreshFactory.cs Modeless lifetime App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSession.cs, App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate.cs State and names Domain/ProjectStates/ProjectStateStore.cs, Domain/ElementNames/ElementNamesCache.cs Persistence App/Persistence/StatePersistence.cs, App/Persistence/UIStateCache.cs, App/Sessions/UIStateLifecycle.cs Scan admission Features/DeepScan/DeepScanOrchestrator.cs, Features/DeepScan/Refresh/DeepScanRefreshWorkflow.cs Usage publication Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexLoader.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageMatchIndex.cs Options and similarity Features/Mapping/State/MappingOptionCache.cs, Features/Similarity/Naming/NamingSimilarity.cs Execution Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingPlanExecutor.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingApplyResultBuilder.cs, Features/Mapping/Revit/Execution/Batch/FamilyBatchExecutor.cs Review Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewApplyWorkflow.cs, Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewFinalizer.cs Intent identity Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentKey.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentStore.cs Data and contracts Domain and feature contracts Shared value language Domain/ owns the value language that several features share, and it imports no feature namespace. Domain/Mapping owns MappingKind and its extensions. Domain/MatchingOption owns MatchingOptionKind, MatchingOptionCandidate, and MatchingOptionSortMode. Domain/Categories owns CategoryOption and CategoryReference. Mapping keeps the WPF-bearing MappingRow and MappingOption presentation types and the intent, conflict, operation, plan, and execution behavior. Project state Domain/ProjectStates owns ProjectState, family/type records, reference index/values, project parameters, scan state, projection, and the scoped ProjectStateStore. The store imports no feature or App namespace. CurrentProjectState and CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identify the loaded snapshot and its category in one replacement operation. IProjectStateBuilder and ProjectStateBuildRequest are inward contracts. App/State/ProjectStateBuilder queries Families, Usage, Shared Parameters, and Previews and projects their results into those values. FamilyScanner and Commit Review verification count type instances in one document collector pass. They use the same placed instances as the mapping writers, including sheet-owned instances and view-owned instances hidden in their view. The snapshot derives family counts from those type counts. Family-only refresh retains loaded Usage and Shared Parameters sections and invalidates derived usage caches before preparing rows. A failed build preserves published state. Commit Review planning builds the selected category plus the families named by mappings and Purge selections. The planning state stays private to Commit Review. For mappings, planning can reuse the published state when no intent names a family or type. It can also reuse an all-category snapshot or a snapshot for the selected category. The snapshot's family and type records must hold every intent family and type. One name read confirms each of those elements still exists. A Purge selection always requires a fresh scan for unused status. A missing or deleted intent family or type requires a planning scan. Planning removes a deleted owner's type and parameter intents and reports a deleted type in a surviving family as a stale selection. CarryForwardInto supplies loaded sections and unchanged-family Deep Scan evidence to that planning state. Duplicate detection also stays unpublished. CarryDeepScanEvidenceInto supplies only unchanged-family evidence to its fresh full state. The scan service can publish a ProjectStateCategorySlice from current duplicate results without a Revit read. This is an owner rule (test ScanFamiliesWithCacheAsync_CategoryChangeAfterACurrentDuplicateScan_MakesNoRevitCall). The Families drawer filters its all-category rows in memory. A GM commit invalidates the duplicate results. Revit edits made while GM is open require a fresh scan to reach GM. The ProjectStateStore retains evidence across category-filtered state replacement. A rebuild restores it only when the family's type set and per-type instance counts remain unchanged. After commit, ReplaceProjectStateAfterCommit discards directly changed families and containing ancestors across all categories. Direct changes include mapped/owning families, families of mapped types, and material/object-style families found by AffectedFamilyResolver. Commit Review planning uses that same resolver. Its plan context owns planning identity and evidence. Discarding evidence removes scan state, type payloads, DeepScanResults, and fast parameter discovery together. Element names and categories Domain/ElementNames owns IElementNameQuery, ElementNamesCache, and ElementNameLookupKind. Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQuery implements the Revit adapter. App registers it with state/cache wiring. Categories registers curated-category services. ElementNamesCache exposes read-only family, type, style, material, and category name views. Each view reflects later merges and clears. Only the cache writes names: MergeNames, MergeFamilyAndTypeNames, name loading, Clear, and ClearFamilyAndTypeNames. A merged nonblank name inserts or overwrites the entry. A blank or omitted name keeps the cached entry. Strict name loading requires a nonblank cached name for every requested ID. The cache stores no blank name, so a missing name is queried again. Omitted/blank provider values stay unresolved. GetResolvedFamilyName prefers cache, then project-state family name, and throws if neither exists. GetCachedFamilyName uses the same order and returns null instead. GetCachedTypeName, GetCachedMaterialName, and GetCachedStyleName return the nonblank cached name or null. A name equal to its ID text is a name. Display getters retain explicit ID/unavailable-name fallbacks. Duplicate family and type names prefer the names captured with the detection, then cached names. A missing family, style, or material name falls back to a nonblank candidate name, then the ID text. A missing type name shows Type <id> (name unavailable). WorkspaceState.SelectedCategory is the single typed CategoryOption value exposed by IWorkspaceState. CategoryFilter derives its display label. Null and Id zero select every family. Other signed IDs select exactly that category, including negative built-in Revit IDs. Both IFamilyQuery methods use those rules. GetFamiliesAsync reuses state only when category identity matches, families exist, and all family names are nonblank. It still filters the reused result by the requested category. WorkspaceState.SortMode uses MatchingOptionSortMode through mutation, persistence, restoration, and option projection. CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identifies loaded state. FamilyMappingState.AppliedCategoryId identifies applied rows. Applying a different category resets category-scoped rows before application and records the category only after rows apply. Cancellation between state publication and row application therefore causes a reset on retry. Mapping intent, rows, and conflicts Features/Mapping/Domain owns immutable intent, conflict, operation, plan, and host-free execution values. It uses the shared kinds from Domain/ and does not import mutable Rows types. MappingIntentKey validates its nine-field shape through named factories and FromPersisted. It rejects invalid zero identities while retaining signed category IDs such as -2000011. MappingIntentStore stores a ParameterMappingIntentSnapshot for a Parameter key, a SharedParameterMappingIntentSnapshot for a SharedParameter key, and an ElementMappingIntentSnapshot for every other kind. An update with another snapshot type throws ArgumentException before it runs the callback or changes the store. Style and material source and target IDs are positive. AffectedFamilyResolver returns no families for a nonpositive ID. Commit Review planning fails an applied style mapping with a nonpositive source or target as an invalid mapping. The Rows package owns row-to-intent translation, projection, origin mutation, and family-apply behavior. MappingRowIntentProjection.ApplyTo assigns ApplySelection after it sets the target and origin. When the row refuses inclusion, ApplyTo writes the resulting selection back to the intent store. Only intents that can produce planned operations count as pending operations. An included type with a valid target or create name counts when its source resolves to an owner family. A family intent supplies the target family and type-parameter write policy. Signal-driven usage-linked family refreshes hold MappingUpdateSuppression while they project rows and refresh Apply indicators. FamilyMappingIntentRefreshRequested also reapplies accepted family intents to loaded type rows under suppression. Conflict/Rows owns row conflict matching. Detection consumes an immutable MappingSelectionSnapshot. MappingConflictWorkflow hydrates returned MappingIntentKey values into loaded rows. MappingConflictTarget defines three closed variants: a positive element selection, a type-parameter policy, or a display-only message. Resolution chooses an original side or an explicit MappingConflictBulkAction. Display labels and sentinel IDs do not encode executable policy. Duplicates implements Mapping-owned neutral selection/resolution contracts without exporting its own selection types. Mapping owns the session and document execution contexts, row signals, navigation values/lifetimes, MappingUpdateSuppression, and OriginClearSuppression. Mapping Domain/Planning owns nested-family, style, and type-reference plan language. Commit Review's CommitReviewDocumentEditBuilder owns mutable family-batch assembly. Mapping's neutral composition registers MappingIntentStore. Commit Review composition registers CommitReviewPlanVerifier. Revit/Composition registers mutation adapters, attached through AddGm. Shared Parameters implements Mapping's focused embed port and uses Mapping operation identities. Domain/Parameters/FamilyParameterDiscoveryResult carries normalized ScopedParameterName values, complete/partial state, and contextual read errors. ProjectStateStore.GetDeepScanParameterDiscoveryForFamily uses completed family scan state first, then DeepScanResults. Family Mapping uses that lookup for both scan availability and parameter names. Complete discovery supplies names. Partial discovery uses complete fast discovery when available, otherwise it clears the names. Family Mapping and Shared Parameters publish choices only from complete discovery. Their factories and consumers require IFamilyParameterQuery and ISharedParameterQuery. Shared Parameters also requires IAuthoringCategoryQuery. Duplicate parameter scoring requires complete discovery on both sides. Instance/Type suffixes are display labels. Parameter mappings retain scope and require equal source/target scope. Element identities Revit family, type, instance, material, style, view, and category IDs use long. Revit boundaries use ElementIdConverter.ToLong and FromLong. Saved-mapping and UI-state JSON accept integer-valued number tokens, including values in the 32-bit range. Family-document materials resolve by name rather than host numeric ID. Counts, indexes, depths, enum/order casts, synthetic duplicate group IDs, SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher sequence IDs, and MappingOption.StableStringId hashes use int. SharedParameterValueCopier rejects Map From values outside Int32 for Revit Integer storage. ElementId parameter destinations parse Map From text as long. Persistence and saved mappings Domain/Cache owns tool-wide cache results and metadata. Persistence adapters derive the GM root with AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("GM"). UI-state and saved-mapping stores create their directories when writing. App/Persistence owns document UI-state storage. App/Sessions/UIStateLifecycle sequences the session's startup restore and close persistence. It restores search text, sort mode, the similarity threshold, and the Applied Only, Hide Unscanned and Hide Unused checkboxes. It also loads the saved mappings. PaneStateProjector restores the Shared Parameters type, duplicate selections and duplicate exclusions. SharedParameterLoader restores the Shared Parameters category when it is available. The UI-state file retains expanded family IDs. At startup, family rows start collapsed. Scan refresh restores expansion within the open session. GM ignores legacy tab and Families category fields. StatePersistence requires both IUIStateCache and ISavedMappingStore in production. Design-time projection does not construct unused persistence. JSON writes flush a unique sibling temporary file and publish it atomically. Cancellation or I/O failure preserves the last good snapshot. Only confirmed missing files/directories count as absent. Access, sharing, invalid-path, and other I/O faults propagate. UI-state and Deep Scan snapshots are disposable caches: malformed, invalid, or old snapshots are discarded and logged. Saved mappings use strict nullable-ingress validation with contextual failures. A missing target marks a mapping as excluded. Excluded entries are saved alongside any last committed entry for the same key. Clearing an exclusion keeps the committed entry. Read errors leave the file intact. Cache results are immutable hit/miss values. Hits always contain data. Persistence and cache stores propagate unhandled failures to the operation boundary for logging. DeepScanCacheCoordinator retains warnings for hydration failures, key preparation failures, and optional cache writes. DocumentPersistenceCoordinator is a root-provider singleton shared by scoped StatePersistence and IUIStateCache instances. It owns the document gate, cache mutation gate, and separate UI-state/saved-mapping clear generations. IUIStateCache serializes asynchronous writes and document clears with the cache mutation gate. StatePersistence serializes document loads, clears, and saves and tracks separate UI-state/saved-mapping clear generations. An older open session cannot restore either snapshot after another window clears it. A freshly loaded window can persist new state. UIStateLifecycle attempts enabled close writes independently, retains failures in write order, and resets one-shot suppression even on failure. Confirmed clears drain before close persistence and disposal. PaneStateProjector supplies SavedAt. Saving preserves the supplied timestamp. Saved Mappings validates exact document identity and every persisted key before admission. Parameter mappings retain ScopedParameterName scope. The persistence port exposes load, save, and clear. MappingIntentStore owns merging and captures explicit Apply exclusions for close persistence. Commit Review constructs the restore workflow, merges persisted intent, and reapplies through row owners. Clearing saved mappings follows this order: Remove saved origins/selections from loaded rows. Clear mapping intent, duplicate intent, and the in-memory persisted list. Clear storage. Run the required App-bound refreshRowsAfterSavedMappingClear operation. CrossPaneRowRefresh rebuilds loaded Usage rows, refreshes Family Mapping rows, reconciles indicators under suppression, releases suppression, refreshes locks, and publishes cache status. Reapply calls Usage, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, Shared Parameters, and row locks directly. Option cache and similarity MappingOptionCache keys candidates by mapping kind, source ID, category, ordered target ID/name pairs, and source label. Category lookup does not fall back to general entries. Prewarm uses the same identity. Candidate snapshots use private read-only lists, so replacing entries cannot mutate earlier results. NamingSimilarity.Normalize and numeric-suffix stem comparison retain letters/digits in invariant lowercase. Numeric-suffix siblings with equal cleaned stems score 1.0 before Dice evaluation. Dice uses lowercased raw-name bigrams, including punctuation and whitespace, with multiplicities. Its score is twice the multiset intersection divided by the sum of raw lengths minus two. For a raw length below two, equal raw lengths score 1.0 only with equal nonempty cleaned stems. Other short-name pairs score zero. Each scoring pass owns its immutable name-profile cache. Deep Scan Deep Scan owns family scans, projection, usage resolution, feature cache, and refresh workflow. DeepScanAllProjectFamiliesAsync scans the loaded project family inventory. Deep Scan Unscanned scans the eligible zero-instance families across that inventory. DeepScanCacheCoordinator requires DeepScanCache, IFamilyParameterQuery, and IDeepScanUsageResolver. Successful usage resolution carries Resolution, which requires its style, material, and nested-family ID collections. Failed resolution carries FailureReason. Family scan StyleIds and MaterialIds contain element IDs. ProjectStateStore.InvalidateDeepScanUsageProjections invalidates cached projections, which recompute on the next read. A user scan collects a complete family batch and finishes cache preparation before one validated ApplyBatch admission. Usage refresh data is prepared before completed scan state publishes. Cancellation or required failure before admission preserves the prior projection. Host lookup completeness is separate for styles, materials, and families. An item failure marks only its domain incomplete and prevents partial singleton-name resolution or resolver-cache reuse. Other complete requested domains remain usable. Affected families retain warning diagnostics and incomplete usage. Unexpected collector/category traversal failures abort construction. Partial parameter discovery invalidates fast choices, is omitted from duplicate scoring, and removes prior reusable cache entries before admission. A later complete query can repopulate choices. Partial usage remains visible but cannot become reusable complete cache data. DeepScanCacheCoordinator removes prior reusable entries for incomplete parameter discovery or usage scans before admission. The first admitted close publishes closing state, cancels Mapping/startup, observes startup, and retains one terminal shutdown task. Repeated closes join that completion. The shutdown workflow independently attempts prewarm drain, option-rendering drain, confirmed preference-clear drain, session-operation cancel-and-drain, close persistence, and synchronous graph disposal, in that order. It then issues one terminal Close. Closed performs idempotent view-model cleanup and App run-scope disposal. Failures retain lifecycle order and do not skip later cleanup. Pane and scope collaborators remain alive until running work drains. Dev Mode retirement is synchronous and requires Idle for immediate collection. Commit Review reports Busy, so reload waits for Keep, Roll back, X, or cancellation followed by close. Revit shutdown can force ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll. Retirement diagnoses pending work, aborts owned dispatcher operations, cancels without draining, and skips close persistence with a log entry. It opens no dispatcher frame. The owning Revit callback rolls back any open apply group through the inline commit gate and disposes the review scope before returning, including when dispatcher shutdown interrupts the review. An existing normal-close task stops before its next stage when retirement takes over. DevModeStatus exposes Idle or Busy: <operations> in the root UI Automation ItemStatus. It includes name lookup, navigation, the Shared Parameters auto-zoom debounce, duplicate rebuilds, Type Mapping, Commit Review, cache posts, and pending page selection. App, Family Mapping, and Shared Parameters navigation use Mapping-owned NavigationLifetime leases. Leases start inside admitted callbacks or around awaited execution. The Shared Parameters auto-zoom debounce uses 200 ms and the lease token. Disposal cancels outside the lifetime lock and prevents later selection, activation, or zoom. Core alerts use observed nested modal loops and diagnose reload during a dialog. Refresh Cache RefreshCacheWorkflow drains background prewarm and reads the new inventory, duplicate detection and Usage snapshot. It publishes the inventory and duplicates before the Usage publication reaches its subscribers. Families restores the selected row and expanded details from the new rows. If the previous selection is unavailable, Families selects the first visible row. An empty view clears the selection. Shared Parameters rebuilds its definition groups, authoring tree and parameter use rows. A failed read keeps the previous inventory and rebuilds affected rows with Usage pending. Prewarm restarts after the action unless GM is closing. FamilyChangeMonitor records family, type and placement changes reported by Revit during the GM session. Deep Scan retention compares the fresh family inventory and discards evidence for changed families and scans that include changed nested families. Deep Scan also checks for changes during a read before publishing its results. Prewarm bypasses cached scans for families with changes reported during the session. Mapping execution RevitMappingPlanExecutor validates document identity and supplies document operations to MappingPlanExecutor. MappingPlanExecutor owns the stage loop, capture boundaries, and result builder. Result accounting The MappingApplyResult constructor validates and snapshots recorded operation results. Succeeded operations require positive affected counts. Skips require zero. Failed operations can retain counts for writes completed before failure. Root succeeded/failed/skipped and affected totals derive from one recorded-result snapshot. Caller collections cannot mutate the completed result. Family success requires changed work and a successful reload. Failed-rule totals and fatal operation diagnostics must agree. Exception-backed diagnostics retain the original exception internally. MappingApplyResultBuilder logs each exception reference once with operation context. Commit Review receives operation text, codes, IDs, and family context. When Revit refused a change, the operation text is Revit's own text, read by OperationErrorRevitReason: the blocking-failure descriptions (ITransactionFailureDefinitionSource.BlockingFailureDescriptions), else the message of a Revit API exception (Autodesk.Revit.Exceptions). A writer without its own error code adds the code RevitRejectedChange. Otherwise the text names the operation and points to the log. A count of failed nested instances adds the first failure's Revit text. A line-style group-edit failure keeps GroupEditCommitFailed and adds the group restriction. Exception types, messages, and stacks stay in logs. Writer exceptions are attributed to every unrecorded operation owned by that writer. Family cleanup always attempts close and retains close diagnostics after primary errors. Cancellation plus cleanup failures propagate primary-first through family-batch and outer writer containment. Skipped group-owned references produce Mapping warnings. An Edit Group restriction rejecting a line-style transaction at commit fails that pair. Successful sibling results retain their affected counts, but Commit Review rolls back an attempt with fatal mapping diagnostics. When an operation fails, Commit Review reports that failure and rolls back. Post-apply verification does not run, so it cannot replace the reason. Writer failures A writer exception after all owned operations are recorded is a workflow failure. The result builder logs writer/stage context once and rethrows the original exception with its stack. Recorded operations alone cannot produce a successful final result in this case. With unrecorded owned operations, the executor records their failures and continues to later writers. Population capture Replacement capture precedes the first mutation that can change its population. ApplyContext captures the original symbol populations, target occupancy and type-parameter source values before the writer loop. Host material references are captured at the fixed boundary after Host recreation and before Nested Families or Type Replacements, including plans with no Host operations. They refer to recreated element IDs without consuming values introduced by later type-parameter migration or family reloads. A family-scoped material mapping captures only material parameters on placed instances of its owner family. A captured parameter that already holds the planned target at write time adds no host write or count. Other changes to the captured value fail the operation. Each family document captures all applicable material, object-style and nested-symbol references before its operation loop. Missing sources are explicit capture results. An absent source in a traversed family is zero work with a non-fatal reason. A missing host source or an ambiguous family material name remains an error. Apply never discovers an incoming population. Family material capture includes writable type parameters and the per-type defaults of instance material parameters. Revit does not allow formulas on Material data type parameters. Formula-determined parameters are outside this material replacement population. Reference kinds are explicit. Blank type names are valid and match ordinally. Capture does not change FamilyManager.CurrentType. Transactional apply restores the captured type. Object-style capture identifies the actual subcategory parameter or boundary curves of each filled region. Family-owned execution uses BatchOperationSet keyed by MappingOperation.OperationId and FamilyBatchResult.ResultsByOperationId. Style and prepared-material payloads use the same IDs. Nested, style, material, and embed dispatch uses canonical operation types and direct appliers. Each applier receives a FamilyBatchApplyContext for its family-tree node: the apply context, host document, retained family document, root family ID, path summary and family identity. The family document is null after its retained document closes; an applier requires it only when it writes. Intermediate counts must be nonnegative, and succeeded plus failed documents cannot exceed attempted. Invalid producer output fails validation. Family document lifetime Family-owned batch execution discovers the complete applicable family tree and captures each original population before applying any family mutation. IFamilyDocumentService.DescribeRootFamilyAsync returns a FamilyDocumentReference (ID, name, identity and category key), and OpenRootFamilyDocumentAsync opens the edit document from that reference. The open rejects a modifiable host document and requires the family to match the reference identity and category. When the ID no longer resolves to a matching family after a reload, a unique match by name is used. FamilyBatchDocuments retains one edit document for each family identity through capture, apply, and reload. Discovery spans the whole commit. After discovery, documents with no applicable work in themselves or their descendants are closed before apply. Remaining documents close after their last root-batch use. Final cleanup closes anything left, including after cancellation. Each release closes in reverse open order and reports individual close failures. Discovery logs the peak and retained counts and reports progress per root. Cleanup uses the underlying Revit gate without requiring the launch document to remain active or the work token to remain uncanceled. EditFamily creates independent copies, so no captured element key is carried into a second edit session. Family element references use UniqueId within their retained document plus parameter identity. Family type references use explicit reference kind, family type name, and family parameter name. Built-in parameter identity uses the typed Revit enum without narrowing its underlying 64-bit value. Document-local ElementId values remain diagnostics and population indexes only. Missing keys produce a diagnostic and do not trigger a live rescan. Shared family identity and reload Shared nested families use a name/category identity. Nonshared copies include their embedding path. Discovery opens the project's shared definition when one exists, so a parent's stale embedded copy cannot become the original population for another root. If the same shared family is reached through several roots, applicable operation populations are merged and each normalized operation is applied once. An equivalent alias receives a merged notice. If its representative fails, the alias is reported as failed as well. Conflicting targets for the same source fail preflight. After a nested or root reload, the load allowlist selects FamilySource.Family only for shared identities changed by that target traversal. Unchanged shared children use FamilySource.Project, which preserves the target document's existing child instead of reloading a stale source copy. Parent material capture excludes shared-symbol projections: the child owns those values and only surviving writes count. Before reload, project-owned shared material projections are restored from the target document explicitly. Revit can otherwise propagate those type values even when the shared-family load callback selects Project. Nonshared symbol overrides remain part of the parent population. Family results Family-document success requires both changed work and a successful reload. A failed family traversal or reload marks every operation actually executed in that traversal as failed, including merged aliases. An affected count can show writes made before the failure. The original exception remains attached to the diagnostic for logging and review. Family-document attempt/success/failure counts include every examined root and child document, including zero-work captures. A reload or close failure keeps the completed affected counts and marks the affected document operation results failed. Material projection ownership A parent FamilySymbol's material type value is a projection of the child's authored FamilyType value. When that child has the same planned material operation, the child owns the write and its count. For nonshared children, root-only operations and traversal-depth leaves retain their parent-side references. Shared projections are always child-owned. Missing captured host references produce a nonfatal diagnostic. Line-style verification Line-style query snapshots retain curve IDs and per-source offered intersections, not Revit element wrappers or target sets per curve. A line-style apply performs one fresh discovery sweep, then verifies actual styles by reading the captured IDs. Complete original-source intersections are regrouped under the final source styles. Unexpected population splits or missing curves fail verification for the committed pairs. Their operation results retain the committed affected counts, and the writer returns the errors instead of throwing away those operation results. Commit Review and the subsequent accepted Usage refresh share this result. A rollback does not publish it. CommitReviewLineStyleLifecycle exports it once, and only while the session's query cache still holds the snapshot that was current when post-apply verification succeeded. Explicit Detect and Usage refresh boundaries invalidate prior snapshots. Object-style attribution identifies the family returned by LoadFamily, its retained name, and its ownership of original instances. Style availability depends on the family category and kind. Post-apply verification Verification runs only after an attempt in which no operation failed. It names each remaining source and each mismatched operation result by the plan's display labels, not by element ID. It reads symbol counts only for type, create-type and host operations, and style and material Usage only for material and object-style operations. It reads line-style Usage after every clean attempt, because that snapshot is the one CommitReviewLineStyleLifecycle hands to the post-commit Usage refresh. Commit Review checks operation identity and successful operation results for all replacement kinds, including runtime replacements created by Create Type. Symbol and line-style counts can be checked against incoming populations. Family material and object-style Usage count families while operation results count references. An overlapping successful target is therefore checked through its operation result and writer readback, not by equating those different quantities. Commit Review results and finalization Result Contract Completed Requires MappingApplyResult and derives success from Outcome Canceled Contains neither Mapping result nor failure prose WorkflowFailed Requires a nonblank reason. Can retain a rolled-back Mapping result for diagnostics Warnings can complete successfully and remain committable. Only positive succeeded operations without fatal diagnostics project applied or persistable intent. Such an operation with no matching intent entry logs a warning and is not saved. A matching entry without persisted state, such as one with PersistSelection off, is not saved and logs at Debug. Verification requires no planned type, host, style, or material source references to remain. Otherwise the verifier's report blocks mapping projection, and the attempt rolls back as Apply was rolled back. Nothing was changed. One Global Mapper: Apply session group stays open through modal review. Apply admits a reviewed plan only while CanApplyPlan is true: the plan has an operation, and validation found no nested-family replacement or type creation without a positive OwnerFamilyId. ApplyCommand checks it for availability and again when it runs. The first attempt clears it; Retry Apply is admitted by CanRetry. Apply and Retry Apply execute and verify inside an inner attempt group. Failure or cancellation rolls back the attempt and permits retry. Retry reuses the reviewed plan but constructs a new apply context and rereads the document. Keep + Continue and Keep + Close GM assimilate the session group into one Undo entry before recording mappings. Roll back, X's rollback answer, cancellation, and abnormal exit roll it back. X asks Keep or Roll back only while a successful attempt waits for Keep. After an attempt that kept nothing, X rolls the empty session group back without a prompt. An unknown rollback outcome propagates to the error banner rather than asserting that nothing was kept. Active-view refresh follows successful verification. A refresh warning does not disable Keep. After the review closes and its apply group is settled, RefreshAfterReviewAsync refreshes GM after any admitted attempt, including failed or rolled-back attempts. A kept apply still refreshes if disposing the review scope fails. The error report includes any cleanup and refresh failures. Forced retirement skips the refresh. GmCommitReviewWindowViewModel reports a plan or an attempt in three parts: Outcome, one card from CommitReviewOutcomeProjector: a title that states the result, for example Apply failed. Nothing was changed., one source → target: reason line per failed mapping (at most three, then a count), and the next step. A Revit rejection's next step says that Retry Apply runs the same plan and how to change the mapping. A rolled-back clean attempt lists the verifier's lines. Problems, one table: validation issues, operation failures and warnings, and plan warnings. Each row has a source, a target, a stage and a reason. The reason holds no diagnostic code. The row keeps its codes (Codes, for example HostParameterCopyWarning) and its operation id, and Copy Report prints both. DetailsText, one collapsed section with the operation summary, family changes, host replacements and nested families. It includes the Shared Parameters summary before Apply and the timing and stage summary after Apply. OperationRows is its per-operation table. The failure banner repeats the outcome title and its first line. Copy Report starts with the outcome and the problems. The raw view binds Outcome, Problems, DetailsText and the tables in Details. The problem reason wraps, and the grids scroll horizontally when the columns exceed the available width. Type replacements retain their selecting intent key, so acceptance records intent for its actual owner. Apply transactions log each Revit failure at Warning with definition ID and failing elements. Pre-commit issues retain their validation label. Family-document material replacement resolves source and target by material name. It reuses or creates the target material in the family and copies the project target’s shading color and transparency. The appearance, fill pattern, physical and thermal assets of the family material are outside this write. Errors retain planned operation ID and host source/target IDs. Family-document material IDs and affected elements are diagnostic details. Material receipts include the families changed by the host writer or reloaded with a material edit. Commit Review uses those receipts to scope allowances for incoming material chains and swaps. A family-scoped material mapping warns about project face paint and verifies unpainted source material usage. Report grouping uses the owning operation even when operations share a host pair or family documents assign different IDs. Reloaded family identity Family-owned apply retains the family ID returned by Revit reload. Accepted mappings use that identity, including existing saved and pending mappings for the same family. Rollback leaves mapping identities unchanged. MappingApplyResult.ReloadedFamilyIds snapshots changed root identities. Finalization remaps applied/persistable family keys and targets before merging. MappingIntentStore also remaps existing saved and pending intents, Apply exclusions, and usage links. One replaced identity must not retain a second saved mapping. Host replacement Each host replacement is atomic per instance. Placement and required facing, hand, and point-rotation transfer must finish before source deletion. Ordinary parameter copies use best-effort transfer. A failed replacement becomes an item error only after its subtransaction reports a completed rollback. If rollback throws or reports any other status, the primary and rollback failures escape together so the enclosing transaction aborts instead of committing an uncertain document state. ParameterValueTransfer reads the target after Parameter.Set returns false. It accepts the copy as a no-op only when its storage type and value exactly match the requested source value. It applies no numeric tolerance to Double values. A remaining mismatch becomes a nonfatal HostParameterCopyWarning with the source instance, parameter, and reason. Setter exceptions remain failures. These warnings appear only after the replacement subtransaction commits. A later required-state failure rolls back and retains the fatal replacement error. Commit Review preserves each distinct diagnostic, opens the operation diagnostics section, and reports Completed with Warnings. It counts nonfatal diagnostics. Within each diagnostic-code group, it includes distinct messages in first-seen order. Code groups sort by descending diagnostic count, then by code ignoring case. Host parameter transfer treats a writable instance Phase Created value as instance-owned even when the family symbol exposes the same built-in parameter ID. The type-bound rule excludes generated IfcGUID. Revit read scheduling GmSessionDocumentGate validates Action callbacks as synchronous before wrapping their launch-document check. It rejects async void before Core can see only the synchronous decorator. Generic results also undergo synchronous-result validation. Independent reads for one action start together. Startup waits for every family-category, shared-parameter-category, and parameter-group read to settle. Ordinary startup faults take priority over cancellation. Aggregate faults contribute their non-cancellation leaves recursively. A single ordinary fault keeps its identity and stack. Multiple ordinary faults form an aggregate in family-category, shared-parameter-category, then parameter-group order, regardless of completion order. Other exception wrappers keep their context. With cancellation alone, the first cancellation in that order keeps its token. Expanding a family with instances makes one Revit callback and opens no family document (owner rule; test ToggleFamilyRowCommand_ExpandingAFamilyWithInstancesReadsExamplesInOneRevitCallback). The expansion builds a missing usage index first, then runs its reads through IRevitCallBatch; the first failure propagates. The Views panel owns the views list. The views list is read for the selected row while the views panel shows and the workspace is ready, once per family until the next family scan or post-commit refresh. When the workspace becomes ready after startup or an operation, the selected row's list is read. A views-list double-click is one Revit call. Selected-type instance examples are read once through type selection. A duplicate scan reads the previews of each kind (line styles, object styles, materials) in one Revit callback (test DetectAsync_ReadsThePreviewsOfEachStyleAndMaterialKindInOneRevitCallback). Core's queued-turn policy determines which waiting calls share a callback. Testing See Global Mapper testing for fixture ownership, hidden-desktop dialog hosting, model baselines, and run commands. Limitations Family-tree discovery retains edit documents through capture and applicable writes, so peak open-document count grows with the discovered tree. Grouped curves are eligible only when each enclosing group type has one placed instance. Family-document material replacement resolves by name, not host numeric ID.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.title: Global Mapper (GM) | dbtools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper (GM) Overview Global Mapper finds duplicate or related Revit content, captures mapping intent, and previews and applies replacements through Commit Review. Its main window is modeless. Commit Review is modal and keeps a reversible apply group open until the user keeps or rolls back changes. The architecture specification defines state, capture, execution, and lifetime contracts. The user guide describes mapping workflows. Architecture Source and registration Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. The assembly and tool ID are dbtools.GM. manifest.yml registers: Surface Value Module dbtools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmToolModule Command and availability dbtools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmCommand Run profile QueuedModeless Ribbon Common panel, Global Mapper, order 30, icon key gm Main raw view dbtools.ToolViews.GM.GmWindow.xaml, Modeless Commit Review raw view dbtools.ToolViews.GM.GmCommitReviewWindow.xaml, Modal Sandbox uses internal design-time view models with public binding properties: dbtools.GM.App.DesignTime.GmWindowDesignTimeViewModel and dbtools.GM.Features.CommitReview.DesignTime.GmCommitReviewWindowDesignTimeViewModel. Ownership Owner Responsibility App/Composition Service registration, session and row graph construction App/Sessions Workspace implementations, cross-pane row refresh, UI-state restore and close persistence, attachment, close, shutdown, modeless lifetime App/Startup, App/Navigation Initialization, page activation, prewarm, pending navigation App/Persistence, App/State UI-state storage and feature-to-domain state construction Domain Project state and its family inventory, identity, element names, parameters, categories, workspace, cache and operation contracts Features/Categories Curated categories Features/Families Family inventory and document lifecycle Features/FamilyMapping Family/type rows, nested usage, scan, selection, and type creation Features/Mapping Intent, row-to-intent translation, conflicts, plans, and replacement execution Features/CommitReview Review planning, modal workflow, reports, verification, finalization, refresh port Features/DeepScan Family scanning, completeness, cache, hydration, refresh Features/Duplicates Detection, matching, selections, tree, and type mapping Features/Usage Indexing, options, matching, preview, selection, and usage rows Features/SharedParameters Authoring, formulas, parameter operations, rows, and tree Features/Similarity Name scoring and score presentation Features/Previews Material/style catalogs and preview values Features/SavedMappings Strict persistence envelope, clear, and reapply Features/ViewOperations View and element navigation Revit Tool-wide document and name adapters Feature packages own their local domain, planning, execution, Revit, views, and workflow where present. App composes cross-feature sequences through feature-owned ports. Features do not import App. GM identifiers spell out SharedParameter; none abbreviate it to SP. ICuratedCategoryQuery.GetCuratedFamilyCategoriesAsync returns the owner-selected Families categories, in this order: Detail Items, Generic Annotations, Generic Models, Structural Framing, Structural Columns, Structural Foundations, Structural Connections, Specialty Equipment, Mechanical Equipment, Doors, Windows, Furniture, Casework, and Title Blocks. Generic Annotations is always available. The others appear when the project has a loadable family in that category. IAuthoringCategoryQuery.GetFamilyCategoriesAsync supplies Shared Parameters with the categories of loadable families in the project, sorted by label. WPF presentation GmWindowPresenter loads App/Views/GmWindow.xaml through ToolWindowFactory. Its binding source is App/ViewModels/GmWindowViewModel. Commit Review binds to Features/CommitReview/ViewModels/GmCommitReviewWindowViewModel. The runtime and design-time view models expose raw fragment bytes for six feature panes. Stable GmRawViewConverter parses those fragments. OneTime fragment bindings use the nearest categoryTabs ancestor. The host assigns shell and raw-root DataContext synchronously before the first dispatcher pump, so the first DataBind/layout pass can materialize each pane. OneTime retains it across tab switches. Feature panes bind to their feature view models. Parent commands, category selection, and empty-state labels address the shell DataContext. Stable WPF registrations, controls, converters, selectors, attached behaviors, and shared resources live in src/dbtools.Presentation/Tools/GM/, namespace dbtools.Presentation.Tools.GM. Each raw view merges Presentation’s Resources/Theme.xaml and references stable dictionaries with versioned ResourceUri values. GmViewResources.xaml owns Mapping and Similarity styles without a second theme merge. Payload views have no code-behind, dependency properties, or implicit payload-type templates. Bindings use INotifyPropertyChanged sources or OneTime for immutable values. Raw templates use string keys with explicit fallbacks. GmViewXaml exposes embedded bytes for raw-XAML tests and hosted views. App Pure reads the GM assembly's fixed logical resources directly. Mapping target ComboBoxes use GmComboBoxDropDownCommandBehavior. It runs the selection command at Background priority when an open drop-down closes with a different logical item. It also runs the command when WPF changes a closed combo's selection through keyboard navigation or TextSearch. WPF uses Up and Down to select adjacent items while the drop-down is closed. For noneditable combos, Left and Right also select adjacent items, and Home and End select the first and last items. Page Up and Page Down navigate only while the drop-down item host is visible. Binding, refresh, and option-population changes outside those input routes do not run the command. The open command supplies lazy options when the user opens a target combo. Commit Review owns one Revit callback around planning, ShowDialog, finalization, and refresh. Core WindowOwnerModalityScope disables Revit and other top-level windows through that callback and restores only the windows it disabled. During planning, the GM owner remains available for its overlay and Cancel action. ShowDialog disables that owner while the review dialog is visible. ShowDialogCommitReviewDialogHost dims the owner (opacity 0.5, no hit testing) only for the dialog's lifetime, so planning never dims it. User close returns the session finalization. Forced retirement returns none. IsRetired is true for both outcomes and cannot distinguish them. Keep triggered from WPF Closing queues the final Close because WPF rejects reentrant Close there. The GM window, Duplicate Type Mapping and Commit Review use CenterOwner startup: WPF centers each window on its owner (Revit for GM, GM for the other two) and keeps it inside that monitor's work area. Duplicate Type Mapping uses a registered modeless shell owned by GM, with a taskbar entry. Commit Review has an explicit finalization decision and a cleanup close gate. Cleanup requests cancellation, waits for a safe rollback boundary, and propagates cancellation, timeout, or rollback failures. A failed cleanup leaves the review window open. Row refresh and owner closure follow successful cleanup. Design-time shared-parameter composition uses the production feature/projection graph with explicit host replacements, including NoopFamilyParameterQuery. Authoring receives a registered parameter-signature provider. Data and contracts The architecture specification defines project state, mapping intent, persistence, and execution results. Workflows Apply and family types A family’s Apply box reflects the checked type rows. Checking the family checks the types that have a valid target. Clearing it excludes every type. A mix shows as partly checked. The plan takes replacements from checked type intents. An unchecked type keeps its instances, and the source family stays loaded. Apply exclusions are part of Mapping Intent. The row projections and automatic matching preserve them. On close, GM saves explicit exclusions with their target. The saved-mapping store restores rows without a target as excluded and reports malformed data without discarding the file. Startup performance Startup logs Information-level elapsed time for five overlay steps. Before the overlay, it logs GM startup: "<step>" ended in <ms> ms. for the UI state load, the wait for first paint, and each of the three startup reads (family categories, shared parameter categories and shared parameter groups), also when a step fails. Usage indexing logs each catalog/index source duration and completion state. Failure or cancellation records the interrupted step and elapsed time, including queued Revit-call time. Overlay visibility is not the timing source. A family expansion builds a missing usage index first, because that build makes its own Revit calls. It then runs every other Revit read through IRevitCallBatch in one Revit callback: the source and target parameter names, the one-instance usage walk, the nested names and inline previews, the type sample and the instance values of its first instance. Gate calls made inside the callback run inline. A read that continues after the callback queues its later calls, and GmSessionDocumentCallBatch logs that at Debug. The expansion reads no views list; the Views panel reads it for the selected row. A views-list double-click calls IViewOps.ShowElementInViewAsync. Selecting a type updates the parameter examples from its first placed instance. A parameter-example read that GM cancels finishes without a window error. ViewOpsQuery checks a view-owned element only in the view group of its owner view: the primary view and its dependent views. Both the cross-view search of a navigation and the views list of a family use this rule. QueryElementsByParam walks the views in name order, stops at its cap, and reads the parameters of an element once when several views show it. Duplicate detection calls GetStylePreviewsAsync once for each style kind and GetMaterialPreviewsAsync once for materials. Each catalog batch runs in one Revit callback. Shared Parameters authoring builds project state once for all authoring categories. It batches parameter-name reads, type samples, and coverage reads, then builds each category's rows in memory. Evidence and group changes rebuild the rows under the session operation gate and progress overlay. Project state and Commit Review count placed family instances in one document collector pass. Both include sheet-owned instances. Parameter discovery prefers model-owned and visible view-owned instances before the remaining placements. Geometry scans discover owner IDs through a quick filter, then visit eligible owners with instances and apply Revit view visibility. Type IDs retain collector order and cache per project state. Style and material indexing share one capped sample and 25-instance chunks with separate geometry options. Family-dependent styles are visited once per usage build. Each option-building pass owns immutable name profiles and retains numeric-suffix and multiset-bigram scoring. Features/Usage/FamilyFastIndex/UsageFamilyFastIndexCollector records material and object-style evidence without Revit types. It keeps distinct paths, direct and nested usage flags, and maximum depth for each positive ID. UsageFamilyFastIndexBuilder reads a placed instance through Revit and supplies traversal contexts to the collector. Row refresh and UI dispatch App/Sessions/RowRefresh/CrossPaneRowRefresh owns every cross-pane row refresh trigger and its order: filter change, Usage page activation, startup, Usage publication, category change, Deep Scan, saved-mapping clear, and commit with Continue or Close. Each trigger is a named method that documents its order. FilterRefreshWorkflow, PageActivationWorkflow, and StartupRowWorkflow call these methods. Domain/ProjectStates/ProjectStateStore owns the family inventory: FamilyIds, the positive SymbolIds, FamilyInstanceCounts, and SymbolToFamily. A project-state replacement derives the inventory from the new state. A fresh family scan and a category snapshot restore replace it through ReplaceFamilyInventory. Name resolution, initialization, Deep Scan, and snapshot storage read the store when they run. The session operation gate, pending page selection, Duplicates pane rebuilds, Usage publication, option rendering, and Family Mapping inline previews dispatch UI work through the GM window's dispatcher, which WindowSessionServices provides after the window exists. They do not use the ambient application dispatcher or the default owner registry. A failed option-rendering refresh shows one "GM Option Rendering" error banner. A replacement refresh and the close drain do not report it again. A failed debounced Duplicates rebuild shows one "GM Duplicates Rebuild" error banner. Testing Pure tests mirror App, Domain, and Features owners. Test builders, external fakes, and assertions live in Tests/Support. Project-state and name-cache tests live under Tests/Domain. Duplicate projection tests live under Tests/Features/Duplicates. The root Revit name adapter mirrors its complete path at Tests/Integration/Revit/Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQueryTests.cs. CommitReviewPlanContextTests mirrors Features/CommitReview/Planning. Saved mappings, authoring, and usage matching also mirror their subjects. UsageFamilyFastIndexCollectorTests directly tests fast-index aggregation in the Pure suite. UsageFamilyFastIndexBuilderTests checks extraction from placed instances and missing-sample handling in Revit. Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSessionTests.cs launches the production session through its queued App run scope and GmWindowViewModelBuilder. It observes the raw view in the stable shell on the dispatcher. Normal-close tests overlap close requests and await shared completion, shutdown, one Closed event, cleanup, and scope disposal. Retirement tests wait for Idle, retire synchronously, and check collection without another dispatcher pump. ForcedRetirement_AfterApply_RollsBackTheOpenGroupAndReturnsWithoutHanging retires after a real apply and checks model restoration and group finalization before child-scope disposal in the same Revit turn. Revit-hosted Commit Review tests use testing/TestSupport/GM/Fakes/HiddenCommitReviewDialogHost in place of ShowDialog to satisfy hidden-desktop window ownership. Its dispatcher frame ends on retirement. IToolWindowSession.Closed does not complete after forced retirement, so awaiting that event would retain the Revit callback until timeout. A 60-second deadline retires a session left open and fails the test. Pure GM tests cover family duplicate Accept through type planning, Apply projection, signal-driven row refresh, pending-operation eligibility, and placement refusal. FamilyMetadataServiceTests covers the Revit placement types. GM Revit-hosted fixture models, named views, family symbols, line styles, materials, and expected production outcomes are required repository baselines. Missing baselines and false production results fail with the model path and running year. Fixture teardown and transaction-group finalization failures also fail and are aggregated with a primary test failure when both occur. GM Local tests enter the native callback through RevitHost for calls that finish in the current turn. The RevitTestBase gate refuses work that would wait for a later callback and names the test. dbtools.GM.HostedTurns.Local.Tests owns DeepScanOrchestratorPipelineTests and FamilyDeepScanTests. The pipeline and overlay cancellation tests use the queued Revit task for work after a file read or a dispatcher yield. They give each pipeline operation or cancellation scan a two-minute deadline. Both GM Local projects use the shared profile isolation setup. dbtools.GM.Pure.Tests.csproj contains owner-local fixtures and shared test support and references the desktop dbtools.GM.csproj. The production assembly grants the Pure assembly internal access. Revit references are compile-only; loading a Revit-typed member requires a Revit host. The repository wrappers run the GM checks. Run the ones that the change can affect (Choosing checks): ./build.sh BuildApp ./build.sh BuildTests ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 The Pure project targets net10.0-windows and requires Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App. Revit-hosted tests use the local scope through the daemon fleet. Limitations The session key uses the document hash code, which can collide. The specification describes family-document and line-style limits.

developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.title: dbtools.TDV | dbtools
developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.summary: dbtools.TDV NAME dbtools.TDV - transfer drafting views between a project and a library SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Common/TDV/ (manifest.yml) assembly dbtools.TDV entry TdvToolModule commands TdvImportCommand, TdvExportCommand DESCRIPTION WindowSession delegates library selection to LibrarySelectionDialog and opens the modal transfer window. TransferSession holds the source and destination for the window. STRUCTURE Path under the tool source Owner App/Composition/ TdvToolModule registers settings. AddTdv registers scoped services. App/Sessions/ WindowSessionDialogRunner handles close and retirement. Features/Library/ LibraryCatalog resolves paths. LibrarySelectionDialog builds the picker. LibraryDocumentService manages documents. Features/Transfer/Execution/ See TransferExecutor.ApplySelectionAsync and DestinationTransactionGroup (RunItemAsync, FinalizeAsync). Features/Transfer/Operations/DraftingView/ DraftingViewTypeResolver and DraftingViewWriter. Features/Preview/ PreviewExporter, PreviewImageExporter and PreviewCache. DraftingViewWriter.CollectViewElementIds compares Category.Name with the English keys in s_skipCategoryNames, so the check matches only those English names. See the same method for the Viewport type check and the ExtentElem substring check. CONTRACTS TransferExecutor.ApplySelectionAsync requires one continuous Revit API callback. TransferExecutorTests checks callback entry. DestinationTransactionGroup uses the requested document even when another document is active. EnsureOwns rejects any other document. DestinationTransactionGroup_BindsBeginItemAndFinalizeToOneNonActiveDocument checks the binding. Projection and execution trim names with TransferNameNormalizer. In TransferExecutorTests, DraftingViewReader_and_TransferCatalog_project_only_current_drafting_views_and_conflicts checks case-insensitive matching. Transfer_WhenDuplicateDestinationNamesAreSelected_FailsWithoutCreatingRenamedCopies and Transfer_WhenDestinationNameExistsAndReplaceFalse_ReportsConflictWithoutCreatingView check name rejection. See TransferExecutor.TransferSelectionItemAsync for validation and transaction order. For Retain Original, TransferExecutor.ResolveDestinationType lets EnsureDestType create a missing type. TransferExecutorTests checks that EnsureDestType creates a requested type and refuses a missing named type. TransferRunState counts and reports row successes after Committed. Transfer_DraftingView_From_GM_To_SGT checks success reporting after finalization. RunSelectionAsync checks Cancel before each view and after the final transaction group health check. The executor rolls back the group when it observes Cancel or when starting the group fails after it opens. Transfer_WhenReporterCancelsDuringFirstRow_RollsBackAndStops checks rollback with one view and with another view pending. TransferDestinationChangesTests checks window totals and unverified changes. TransferProjectorTests checks the conflict display and the display for rolled-back or unknown outcomes. FLOW LibrarySelectionWorkflow opens the picker even when no configured path is valid. LibrarySelectionDialog offers Browse for file in every case. When valid and invalid paths both exist, it reports the unavailable count. LibraryDialogOptions sets the initial size to 660 by 460 device-independent units. The alert owns the file picker. Canceling the file picker leaves the alert open. Before validating the choice, the workflow rejects the active model and its central path. A browsed path applies to one workflow. LibrarySelectionDialogTests and LibrarySelectionWorkflowTests check the selection routes. LibraryDocumentService checks the saved Revit year before opening. LibraryDocumentServiceTests checks year refusal and both open routes. Before releasing the library, LibraryTransferWorkflow.ReactivateHostDocument restores the project captured by the command if the active document changed. A preview export can activate the library, and Revit refuses to close the active document. ImportTransferWorkflow requests discard. ExportTransferWorkflow saves or synchronizes when TransferDestinationChanges.Any is true, including Unverified changes. It otherwise requests discard. TransferWorkflowTests checks these routes. On retirement, WindowSession defers library release until any active transfer ends. TdvWindowViewModelTransferTests checks the timing. TransferWorkflowTests checks release without queuing a call-gate operation. DATA The core.library pack binds Core.MasterLibrary to LibraryOptions. The Files list starts empty. Each LibraryFile entry has MainPath, FallbackPath and Alias. LibraryCatalog uses a valid fallback when the main path is missing or invalid. LibrarySettingsContext.Load skips fallback-only entries. LibrarySettingsContext flags entries with a main path and no valid path. The core.library.invalid warning reports those entries in Settings and leaves both transfer commands available. CachePaths defines the cache roots. PreviewImageExporter exports a PNG with a horizontal fit and a size setting of 1024 pixels. It takes the pane color from the PNG's upper-left pixel or from ColorOptions.BackgroundColor if the pixel is fully transparent. PreviewCache retains up to 32 paths and colors. It evicts the oldest inserted entry first. WindowSession.CleanupViewModel requests directory cleanup on close. PreviewCacheTests checks the limit and directory deletion. Workshared_library_sync_and_reopen_persists_changes_and_removes_local_workspace checks workspace removal after sync and discard closes. See LibraryDocumentService.TryDeleteWorkspaceForLocalPath for cleanup. DIAGNOSTICS Match transfer logs by RunId and read FinalizationOutcome. SaveAndCloseAsync_WhenSaveAndCloseBothFail_PreservesPrimaryThenClose checks the order of errors when library save and close both fail. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool TDV --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool TDV --scope local -y 2026 ./test.sh test --tool PRESENTATION --scope pure --fixture TdvPanZoomBehaviorTests TdvModelContext leases gm_test_model.rvt and sgt_test_model.rvt to hosted tests. Use BeginCase for isolation and CreateTemporaryWorksharedCentral for worksharing cases. TdvWindow.xaml uses TdvPanZoomBehavior for preview input. PreviewZoomBehavior resets the fit on image change and Zoom Extents. TdvPanZoomBehaviorTests checks wheel zoom and panning. PreviewExportOwnerTests checks the PNG, pane color and preservation of Revit's background colors. SEE ALSO Transfer Drafting Views, Revit Execution, Settings Packs, Feature Warnings, Model paths

developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft..title: dbtools.ERFT | dbtools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft..summary: dbtools.ERFT NAME dbtools.ERFT - plan and apply framing offset changes SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/ assembly dbtools.ERFT.dll module App/Composition/ErftToolModule.cs DESCRIPTION AdjustmentPlan holds column and beam offset changes for a floor or roof target. See Extreme Roof Framing Tool. STRUCTURE manifest.yml gives ErftNewCommand panel Testing and profile InlineUi. The sandboxWindows entry dbtools.ERFT.Main uses ErftWindowDesignTimeViewModel. ErftWindowDesignTimeViewModelTests checks that model's defaults. WindowSession.EnsureSession loads the embedded App/Views/ErftWindow.xaml and repeats the manifest dimensions. For Edit ERFT, see ErftContextualRibbonInjector.BuildButton. ErftCompositionContractsTests checks the hook registration. FindTargetTabs looks for Structural Columns, Structural Framing and Multi-Select, with Multi and Multi-Category as fallbacks. EvaluateSelection checks selected elements for structural column or framing category, a valid entity, Tag equal to ERFT and a nonblank SystemId. ContextualEditCommandType names ErftNewCommand. ErftWindowInteractionBehavior handles Escape and clicks outside grid rows. Model readers live in Features/Operations/. PreviewSceneBuilder prepares the preview scene, and PreviewProjector converts it for the shared presenter. CONTRACTS AddErft scopes AdjustmentPlanStore per run (ServiceCollectionExtensionsTests). SourceSelectionCollector.IsValidSourceSelection admits beams alone when one connects to a model column. SourceSelectionValidator checks copies of the beams (SourceSelectionValidatorTests). PlanPreparationBuilder.CompletePreparation builds the graph from selected members. For a resolved top level, ColumnReader adds the top offset to the level's ProjectElevation. This uses the datum of the location line read by BeamReader. FramingGraphBuilder uses a 1/2 in. distance in three dimensions. It checks the nearest column top first, then beam interiors and nearby directly supported ends. A supporting interior point must be more than 1/2 in. from both beam ends. The builder skips cycles and orders supports first (FramingGraphBuilderTests). TargetGeometryReader triangulates the target's solids and reads each face's generating elements. TargetGeometryBuilder accepts faces whose reported generators are the target or Revit Opening elements. It samples the outward normal at each triangle center and uses triangles with host normal Z below -1e-9. For a linked target, it maps the points and normals with GetTotalTransform (TargetGeometryBuilderTests). TargetSurfaceProjector projects vertically to the eligible surface nearest the member end. At equal distances, it uses the lower elevation. It accepts the closest edge of a triangle when the plan miss is within Application.VertexTolerance (TargetSurfaceProjectorTests). FramingGraphBuilder groups remaining free ends by beam ID, with one end per beam and every pair within 1/2 in. in three dimensions. AdjustmentEvaluator picks a shared splice target from rounded projected elevations. Up picks the highest, Down the lowest, and Nearest the first successful projection in group order. A failed projection still gives an error for that end. AdjustmentEvaluator uses the selected mode for projections. An end that follows a support or uses a shared target rounds its own change with Nearest. A follower uses the support elevation at the followed end. RoundingEvaluator treats a change with magnitude 0.000001 ft or less as zero. It normalizes whole and half steps within that distance (AdjustmentCalculationTests). ErftWindowViewModel.CanApply checks PendingCount > 0, zero row errors and valid tolerance. ErftWindowViewModelTests covers row errors and tolerance, including the 0.01 in custom minimum. During Apply, WindowSession.Interaction ignores apply and pick requests. ErftWindowViewModel.CanClose blocks closing. An expected Apply failure keeps the window open. WindowSessionTests checks these gates and the ShowModal overload that rethrows a thrown Apply exception. AdjustmentPlanExecutor rejects row errors and skips writes when nothing is pending (AdjustmentPlanExecutorTests). FLOW FramingAdjustmentWorkflow calls PlanPreparationBuilder.Prepare for launch and PrepareFromStoredPlan for edit. See EditReconstructionBuilder.TryCreatePlan for stored member resolution. FramingAdjustmentWorkflow.RunSession starts the Extreme Roof Framing Tool transaction group before preparation. On success it assimilates the group into one Undo entry before showing the success alert. Canceling or failing the session rolls back the group. WindowSession reuses the shell after Pick (WindowSessionTests). TargetRepickWorkflow.Repick preserves the plan if target resolution fails (TargetRepickWorkflowTests). MemberProfileExtractor passes ERFT Extract Member Profile, ERFT Extract Member Profile Bake and ERFT Extract Member Profile Cleanup to separate transactions per member type inside the session group. PlanPreparationBuilderTests checks temporary instance cleanup. AdjustmentWriter.ApplyAsync passes ERFT Apply Adjustments to the transaction runner. ApplyColumnAdjustment writes FAMILY_TOP_LEVEL_OFFSET_PARAM (FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests). ApplyBeamAdjustment writes STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END0_ELEVATION and STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END1_ELEVATION. DATA TargetGeometryReader.GetTargetDisplayName formats the target type and level. GetLevelName reads the footprint roof base level, extrusion roof constraint level or face roof level. It uses Element.LevelId if that parameter does not resolve a level. Lengths are in feet. Element IDs are long. Change the 1/4 in default in AdjustmentPlan.ToleranceFeet and TolerancePreset.Default (the ErftWindowViewModel.TryGetCurrentToleranceFeet fallback). Update "0.25" in ErftWindowViewModel._customToleranceText and ErftWindowDesignTimeViewModel.CustomToleranceText. SystemPlanRepository.Save sets SystemIdString and DataJson on the DataStorage entity. Save and Load reject duplicate system records with SystemRepository/DuplicateSystemRecords. AdjustmentWriter.TagElement sets Tag, SystemId, MemberRole, OriginalOffset and Timestamp. StoredPlanMapperTests checks the JSON shape and inclusion of every plan row.
