WallSystemWriter.Recreation.cs reads the live member and admits a matched bound arc only for the same family type. A matched spline, ellipse, unbound line, or other unsupported location fails with Update/LocationMissing. Recreation refuses each of these conditions. The source element or location is read-only. The source is pinned, grouped, assembled, owned by another user, or out of date with the central model. The source has a host other than its level, a host face, a parent or child component, or a dependent other than a verified stored duplicate Mark warning. The dependent-element refusal includes each dependent's ID, category, and class. Either end of the source allows a join, a framing member or a slanted structural column joins into it, or a column is attached to it at the base or top. SGT inspects framing and slanted-column ends within 0.01 ft of the source curve or inside the source model bounding box expanded by 0.01 ft. An unreadable framing end join identifies the framing element and end in the refusal. A missing join list is safe only when Revit reports that joining is disallowed at that framing end. For a nearby slanted-column end, SGT checks joins on both sides and looks up the attachment target when ColumnAttachment.IsValidColumn permits it. If the target remains unknown, a set attachment flag refuses recreation even when the join lookup fails, returns an empty list, or lists only other elements. SGT also refuses when reading the flag throws or the join lookup fails and Revit supplies no flag. Revit's ColumnAttachment API rejects beams as attachment targets for slanted columns. Revit models slanted-column beam relationships as joins. The source participates in a geometry join, coping, solid or void cut, structural connection handler, beam system, analytical association, or local or linked Copy/Monitor relationship. A tag, dimension, saved selection, displacement set, or per-element view setting refers to it. The source has extensible storage outside SGT or a parameter associated with a global parameter. Relationship checks cover the current model. References from other models through a link and external consumers of ElementId or UniqueId are outside these checks. The writer places a straight replacement through the normal placement writer. The system's Reference Level and the planned endpoints determine the replacement's level and end level offsets. The writer verifies the requested placement and refuses changes to the workset, phases, design option, structural type, hand flip, mirror state, Y/Z offsets, or opening member extensions. The remaining instance parameter comparison checks values that Revit exposes as writable. SGT looks up each shared parameter by its GUID and compares existing values, including hidden or read-only shared values. Other read-only fields stay outside the comparison except for the explicit placement constraints. Revit recalculates measurements such as Exact Weight. SGT writes the requested rotation, justification, facing, girt extensions, and tag identity. Revit's arc-only location values have no counterpart in the straight replacement. SGT skips ARC_ELEM_FIX_KEEP_CONCENTRIC (Keep Concentric), which holds the arc center during radius edits. It also skips CURVE_ELEM_ARC_RADIUS, CURVE_ELEM_ARC_RANGE, CURVE_ELEM_ARC_START_ANGLE, and CURVE_ELEM_ARC_END_ANGLE. These define the radius, sweep, and angular endpoints of an arc. SGT verifies stored duplicate Mark warning dependents in a subtransaction before placement. Each candidate must be a plain unnamed element with no category, type, or owner view. Deleting it must remove only that ID and exactly one stored duplicate Mark warning that names the source. SGT compares the warning records from Document.GetWarnings and the source's dependent IDs, then rolls back the probe. Deletion must remove the source member and may remove its verified warning dependents. Revit can keep a verified warning for the remaining members that share the Mark. The writer copies and verifies Mark, Comments, and IfcGUID after deletion. IfcGUID preserves the element's identity for IFC export. The writer registers the new UniqueId as the owner and reports Recreated with both element IDs and the reason. When Update recreates a matched member, its transaction deletes only the GeneralFailures.DuplicateValue warning for a replacement whose Mark other framing members also carry. SGT checks that the warning names Mark, identifies the replacement, and lists only marked framing members. Revit determines which Marks it treats as duplicates. The filter matches the localized Mark label in the native DuplicateValue message. Every other warning anywhere in the transaction rolls back Update. The failure reports Revit's warning text, the identified members or element IDs, and the members being recreated. Update without matched recreation keeps the default warning handling. A failed check or Revit write or commit failure rolls back Update. A warning rollback retains Core's TransactionFailureException as the cause. A failed stored-warning probe rollback reports Transaction/NotCommitted with the member ID and the probe failure. The session transaction group owns Undo. Layers. Domain uses no App, Features, Persistence, WPF or Revit API code. Features use no App code, and Placement uses no WallAnalysis code. The portable net10.0 build has no Revit API, WPF or Presentation reference, and build/MSBuild/Portable.targets excludes .cs files under App/, Revit/, Views/ and DesignTime/. Other code that uses them does not build. Nothing checks the Domain-to-Features, Domain-to-Persistence or Placement-to-WallAnalysis rules. Raw XAML. The XAML is embedded as dbtools.ToolViews.SGT.<file>, with no x:Class and no WPF-derived type in the payload. RawXamlTierContractTests checks every payload view. FLOW NewSessionWorkflow shows a prompt banner and calls WallTargetSelectionWorkflow.PickTarget. It asks for a linked wall (LinkedWallSelectionFilter), then, after Esc, for a host foundation wall (FoundationWallSelectionFilter). ContextualEditHook reads the selected system IDs instead, through ContextualEditTargetEvaluator. SgtWindowSession.Start begins the group and purges. WindowSessionBuilder composes the window, view model and SessionAnalysisOwner. PlanBuilder.BuildNewPlanAsync sets the framing mode, then runs WallAnalysisStep, PlanSeedingStep and admission. GirtElevationBuilder supplies whole 5'-0" intervals from the base through the framing band. For an edit, StartupAnalysisWorkflow rebuilds the plan with PlanBaselineMapper and ChangeReviewPlanBuilder, and AnalyzeEditPlanAsync analyzes a copy of it against the wall. A stored system that does not load falls back to a wall pick (FallBackToPick). Grid edits reach PlanStore through PlanSynchronizationCoordinator. A girt elevation edit applies to its row at cell commit or focus loss. Other girt cell edits apply to selected girts. SGT checks a type change for every selected girt before applying it. An opening row commit updates Center Along for the edited opening and other edited fields for the selected editable openings in the same plan write. Other plan writes read the committed opening while its row has a draft. OpeningAlong converts between wall start in the plan and the exterior left end in the grid and elevation. Opening row refresh keeps default names by opening key as it sorts rows. PlanSynchronizationCoordinator records Wall Offset, wall layer and Reference Level changes, grid edits, Bulk Apply, segment flyout edits, opening segment commands, and edits from PreviewEditingWorkflow. Each commit normalizes segments and stores the editable state before and after the write in UndoRedoHistory. MemberSegmentationReconciler repeats its pass until the opening and girt segments settle. It fails if they still change after eight passes. A failed recompute blocks the preview and refreshes the accepted plan. Anchor repair captures inner girt grids before merging rows. Recompute tries the saved grids within each inner end's solid span, starting with the closest to its opening edge. The grid line must leave 6" of span and clear the resolved jamb by the default gap. A gap override adjusts the end from that line. Recompute reports discarded grid ends and uses the opening edge for a split without a valid saved grid. Parent ends keep their anchors and gaps when a short pier is omitted. Inner-end drags and opening-edge snap offers are limited to the current solid span, including end spans bounded by the wall. The opening draft and native grid edit end before the refresh. A refresh that changes girt row identities runs on the dispatcher after the edit. Each replay checks the current plan version in the same PlanStore.Update that restores the editable state. If another write supersedes that version, SGT clears the stale history when a commit or replay encounters a version conflict. SGT keeps the newer plan and reports the refusal. After an accepted write with a notification failure, recovery reports the failure, clears the history, and refreshes the accepted plan. The recovered write completes the grid edit or replay. Only a recovery failure propagates from that path. An active opening draft or invalid field blocks replay against the current plan. The grids and preview refresh from the restored plan. A no-op leaves both stacks as they are. UIEdit validates input and renders the stored plan. RenderOnly renders the stored plan. PlanMutation normalizes the baseline from analysis or Change Review, which starts a fresh history. A merge records the openings it joins as bypassed, so recompute preserves the merged member. With Live Preview on, startup waits for the elevation refresh and paint inside the analysis progress overlay. With Live Preview off, startup keeps the current preview mode and finishes without waiting for paint. SGT logs one warning when the elevation takes longer than 10 seconds. Click Cancel to close SGT without changes. A preview failure opens the session with a blocked preview. A failed plan refresh stops and logs its error. Explicit refreshes propagate the failure to the calling workflow. Scheduled refreshes and standalone type-source warning updates queue error delivery to the SGT window's boundary at ContextIdle, below the progress paint frame's exit priorities. The session records the delivered failure and rolls back. After an edit startup, ChangeReviewWorkflow opens Change Review when ChangeReviewEvaluator reports NeedsAttention. Confirm analyzes the reviewed plan and saves only the decision ledger (SaveLedgerAsync). It publishes the draft, clears the window's Undo history and shows an information banner. Commands become available after the session processes the review or system retirement outcome. Opening measures and manual edits use OpeningAlong to convert between each wall's exterior left end and its plan start. ChangeReviewRowSuggestionBuilder infers spacing from the most frequent gaps of 6 inches or more at the start of the review. For a taller wall it uses that spacing to offer Add at the next whole intervals. When the accepted base changes, Move applies the draft rows' existing heights above the new base. Returning to Accept on the same wall restores the applied move. Add records each new row's chosen height above the accepted base and preserves it after Relink. ChangeReviewPlanBuilder calls GirtEndpointAnchorResolver on a copy for preflight at the new elevations. That leaves the original grid anchors available when the published draft goes through the same segmentation as ordinary edits. Segmentation splits spans at openings. Preflight offers Remove for rejected rows, including those above the accepted wall. Relink clears the applied move and derives a fresh suggestion from the new wall. Place, Update and Review Changes finish the active opening row before proceeding. A refused row commit preserves the draft and stops the command. Place and Update validate the input and stop if recompute would change the committed framing. SGT logs and displays a framing check exception once per plan version. Place and Update run preflight on the accepted plan, then call PlacementWorkflow, PlacementExecutor and WallSystemWriter. The writer places members, tags them and calls ISystemRepository.Save in one transaction. A successful write closes the window with a commit; a failed or canceled write closes it with a rollback. A refused preflight keeps the window open. For all SGT committed writes requested during progress painting, CommittedWrite queues the transaction at ContextIdle so it runs after the paint frame. Dispatcher refusal or abort reports TransactionNotCommitted with the transaction name when the caller's token has not been canceled. FinalizeSession releases the preview and window, then assimilates or rolls back the group. The UI state saves in the background. Reference Level ReferenceLevelReader reads the host levels and the wall's base constraint. It uses Level.ProjectElevation for the wall, link transforms and framing curves. A level's datum elevation is its internal Z minus the host project base point Z. For a linked wall, ReferenceLevelRule.FindWallLevel matches the transformed constraint within 0.01 ft, preferring the same normalized name. Without a match, it uses the nearest host level at or below the wall base within the SGT length tolerance, or the nearest one above it. The edit flow uses IsEditMode to disable the picker and retains the stored system level. A missing system level blocks Update. For a new system, ReferenceLevelRule.Choose uses a live project pick or ranks datum-named levels. Names match adjacent normalized tokens. Decimal level numbers stay together. Names with a mezzanine marker do not rank as datums. The rank order is finish floor, level one, ground, then level zero. Heights within 0.01 ft of 0 or 100 ft come first, followed by name rank, lower datum elevation and ordinal UniqueId. Without a named datum, the rule tries 0 ft, then 100 ft, then the wall level. A wall uses its own level if that level names another datum or lies more than 8 ft above or below the datum. ReferenceLevelElevation converts between the system level and the plan band base for the grids, Change Review, and preview tooltips. Changing the selection in a new system refreshes the displayed elevations without changing plan coordinates. A missing system level leaves the elevation cells read-only with a missing-level header. Place and Update use the system's Reference Level for every new member. FamilyInstanceMutator seeds horizontal curves on the level plane, then sets the end offsets to the planned internal Z coordinates. It creates vertical jambs on their final world curves and sets INSTANCE_REFERENCE_LEVEL_PARAM after regeneration. PlacedSystemRecorder checks the level and both curve endpoints of every new member. Update leaves the Reference Level of existing members in place. DATA Item Value System storage One DataStorage per system, named dbtools_SGT_System_<SystemId> (GUID without hyphens), schema dbtools_SGT_SystemV2, GUID 87a71e39-0771-4e55-8575-084c51b2facc. DataJson holds the format v4 SystemData envelope with Placed, the decision ledger and settings. SettingsData.ReferenceLevelUniqueId is required. Project pick dbtools_SGT_Project is the project DataStorage and schema name. For multiple rows, ProjectReferenceLevelStorage uses the live pick from the lowest ordinal storage UniqueId. A separate transaction after framing merges duplicate rows and clears stale picks. Place also saves a changed selection. A failure adds a warning to the placement outcome. Member tag Schema dbtools_SGT, GUID 4a265d21-dc7d-4f58-a135-6620d53056a1, with Tag (SGT), SystemId, MemberRole (girt, head, sill, jamb_left, jamb_right) and ConfigJson. Framing mode WallFramingMode.Standard for a linked wall, with the wall bottom as base. Foundation for a host foundation wall, with the wall top as base and a 20'-0" band. The JSON field is placementMode. Rules MemberRules: AutoSeedSpacing 5'-0", MinimumLength 6". UI state %APPDATA%\dbtools\Cache\SGT\ui-state.json: panel expansion, opening column widths and Bulk Edit fields. It never gates the model commit. Revit element IDs are long in the plan, storage and placement records. The schemas use vendor input dbtools. Revit stores the vendor ID in uppercase. PurgeUnsupportedAsync removes earlier system formats, including v3, and strips their SGT tags from framing. It keeps the framing elements and the project pick. Its result counts retired system IDs for the startup warning. Schema names compare without case when identifying storage owned by SGT. DIAGNOSTICS SGT log messages use prefixes such as [SGT], [SGT.Preflight] and [SGT.Place.Cutback]. A plan rejection is a SpecFailure with the text [SpecFail/<area>/<rule>] <detail> (SpecFailureCodes). A UI error shows <action>: [SGT.UI.<area>.<name>] <detail> (UserErrorCodes). DiagnosticsPreflightLogger records analysis outcomes. The orientation warning counts girt families and opening role/family groups with failed or missing orientation results for eligible types. Wall geometry build messages log at Debug. Per-segment preview cutbacks log at Trace, which the application log file omits. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool SGT # pure: portable and Windows projects ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 Project Covers dbtools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests Domain, feature decisions and storage mapping, on net10.0 dbtools.SGT.Pure.Tests Window lifecycle, view models, flyouts, UI state and synchronization dbtools.SGT.Local.Tests Wall analysis, opening detection, model writes, storage, preview parity and the real window session The Local tests open SGT/sgt_test_model.rvt (Model paths). Without the model, they fail. SEE ALSO Hooks, Sandbox Integration, Revit Execution

developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | dbtools
developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting This page lists common build, runtime and tool errors, and how to read the dbtools logs. For a reported failure, read the logs in %APPDATA%\dbtools\Logs\ first. Build Choosing a build command Build one project or test project with plain MSBuild: dotnet build path/to/project.csproj -c Release This computes content versions, restores only the selected year and stages the project's runtime inputs. It does not validate or publish a distribution. ./build.sh BuildAll builds, validates and publishes the complete distribution for every supported year, including the Dev Mode preflight and manifest checks. Use ./build.sh BuildTests or a selected-test target to compile the test projects. See Build Pipeline. Python 3.10 or later is required Python 3.10 or later is required. Install it with: sudo apt-get install python3 On Linux and WSL, build/DotNet/sdk.sh uses Python to verify and install the pinned SDK when the private SDK root is incomplete; test.sh also uses it for test discovery. Install Python and rerun the command: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y python3 bash build/DotNet/sdk.sh On Windows, build.ps1 installs and verifies the SDK without Python. dbtools-daemon.Protocol package missing or mismatched BuildAll requires the dbtools-daemon.Protocol package version pinned in build/Distribution/protocol-package-lock.json, with the SHA-256 recorded there. The Validation Runner loads the package after the build tasks verify it. If the package is missing or its bytes differ from the lock, obtain the pinned package and update the lock. sourceKind is github-release for a published release, or local-candidate for an approved local candidate with its candidate-<version> tag, daemon commit, and copies of the bundle README and SHA256SUMS. Do not point the build at a daemon checkout or bypass the check. BuildAll does not need the daemon CLI or an installed Revit. The DIST suite and Revit-hosted tests use the daemon CLI. Dev Mode preflight fails ValidateDistributionCandidate runs the Dev Mode policy on each year and prints: Revit <year> Dev Mode preflight: <n> failures, <m> warnings; outcome=<x> Both years must pass. Every collectible-boundary warning (CollectibleThreadStatic, CollectibleAssemblyLoadContextType) counts as a failure. A failed policy, boundary, graph, identity or candidate-byte check needs a source fix and a new build. Unsupported Revit year The supported desktop years are Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027; the distribution and reference metadata use the year keys 2026 and 2027. A build or candidate for any other year is rejected; there is no fallback framework. Revit backup files in test models Revit writes backup copies (*.0001.rvt, *.00001.rvt) when it saves a model. Under testing/RevitTestModels/ these files are ignored by Git. The build does not delete them; remove them by hand when you no longer need them. Runtime Tool assembly fails to load InvalidOperationException: Failed to load tool assembly 'dbtools.GM' from the declared Tools path '<path>' in ALC rooted at 'dbtools'. Related errors from ToolAssemblyResolver: Tool assembly '<name>' was not found at the declared Tools path '<path>'. Tool assembly path '<path>' declares simple name '<x>', expected '<name>'. Tool assembly '<name>' is already loaded from '<path>', but the declared Tools path is '<path>'. App loads each tool from Tools/<name>.dll beside dbtools.dll. Check that the year directory has the complete product tree (see Assembly Loading Contract) and that the manifest's assembly name matches the file. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll. "Assembly already loaded" during Dev Mode reload Revit shows a popup about an assembly that is already loaded during or after BuildAll, while the dbtools-daemon Dev Mode driver watches the distribution. Causes: The driver watches the multi-year root .artifacts/dist/Release instead of one year directory. A reload starts while promotion replaces the files. dbtools code loaded or resolved a dbtools.* assembly or type outside the driver's collectible AssemblyLoadContext (for example through an AppDomain-wide scan or Assembly.Load), so the context cannot unload. Point the driver directly at one year directory, .artifacts/dist/Release/2026 or .artifacts/dist/Release/2027, never at a copy, and publish with ./build.sh BuildAll. Promotion keeps each unchanged file as the same file (a hard link), so Windows Defender does not scan it again. A copied directory is a set of new files that Defender scans again, which can add tens of seconds to each Dev Mode inspection. Theme validation Startup validates the theme with ThemeValidator.ValidateOrThrow; a failure stops startup. In a Revit-hosted test run, read the daemon job's startup failure output instead of waiting for a dialog. Theme dictionary merge failed InvalidOperationException: Theme dictionary merge failed at '/dbtools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Brushes.Light.xaml'. A resource dictionary did not load: a missing assembly reference, a broken StaticResource chain or invalid XAML. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll and check that the year directory contains dbtools.Presentation.dll from the same build. Theme resource freeze failed InvalidOperationException: Theme resource freeze failed for key '<key>' in '<source>'. A Freezable resource (brush, geometry) cannot be frozen, usually because it has a binding or a dynamic reference. Make its values static. Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch: expected 7 dictionaries but found 6 in '<root>'. InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch at index <i>: expected '<uri>' but found '<uri>'. Resources/Theme.xaml must merge these dictionaries in this order: Tokens.xaml, the brushes of the current color theme (Brushes.Dark.xaml or Brushes.Light.xaml), Converters.xaml, Controls.xaml, DataGrid.xaml, Menus.xaml and Components.xaml. See Theme System. Revit API context errors ContextUnavailableException: No UIApplication in current gate scope. InvalidOperationException: ActiveUIDocument is null. Code used the Revit API outside a valid API context, for example from a modeless window without the call gate, after the document closed, or during shutdown. Run Revit API work through IRevitCallGate.RunAsync, check that a document is open, and handle cancellation when a document closes. WPF Dispatcher errors InvalidOperationException: No WPF Dispatcher is available (Application.Current is null and no Revit window dispatcher could be resolved). InvalidOperationException: WPF Dispatcher is shutting down. UI work ran during early startup or late shutdown, when no dispatcher is available. Check for a dispatcher and for Dispatcher.HasShutdownStarted before UI work. Use WpfDispatcher.Post for queued work and observe its task. Use WpfDispatcher.Invoke only when the caller must wait for the UI action. See the dispatcher operation retirement contract for generation shutdown behavior. Unhandled UI exception from a window command A WPF command that calls ISafeExecutor.RunAsync and lets the exception propagate into an AsyncRelayCommand raises a Dispatcher unhandled exception, which the Dev Mode driver host can also show. In window commands, use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync: it logs and notifies but does not rethrow. Use RunAsync where the caller must receive the exception. XamlParseException on a read-only binding System.Windows.Markup.XamlParseException: A TwoWay or OneWayToSource binding cannot work on the read-only property '<name>' ... Run.Text binds TwoWay by default. Binding it to a get-only property fails when the window loads. Set Mode=OneWay (or OneTime for an immutable value), or bind a TextBlock.Text instead. Contextual ribbon layout changes A contextual ribbon injector that modifies Revit's contextual tabs eagerly (for example the Multi-Select tab) or inserts at index 0 shifts the native buttons. Inject only when the selection contains matching elements, append panels and buttons with Add, and remove them when the selection no longer matches. Core's ContextualRibbonInjector follows these rules. Other startup and manifest errors Message Cause AppRuntime not initialized. Code ran before App startup completed or after shutdown Manifest '<id>' is missing required 'panel' field. (and other missing required messages) Invalid manifest.yml Tool module type '<type>' not found in assembly '<assembly>'. The manifest module type or assembly name is wrong Tools Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) TransferException carries a TransferErrorCode: Code Meaning Action DestinationTypeMissing The destination has no matching drafting view type Create the view type in the destination SourceTypeNameUnavailable The source view type name cannot be read Check that the source is a valid drafting view CreateViewFailed The destination view could not be created Check write access and view limits CopyElementsFailed The view elements could not be copied Check the elements and the target view OverridesFailed The view overrides could not be copied Some overrides cannot be transferred View Template Comparer (VTC): raw XAML resource not found System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Embedded tool XAML resource 'dbtools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml' was not found. The VTC alert body templates are an EmbeddedResource with the logical name dbtools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml, read with ToolWindowXaml.ReadEmbeddedResource. Check the item and its LogicalName in dbtools.VTC.csproj. The shared VTC dictionaries are in src/dbtools.Presentation/Tools/VTC. Logs Log files Logs are written to %APPDATA%\dbtools\Logs\. File names use Eastern time: dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>.log dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>-manual-<ManualTimestamp>.log The second form is written after Start New Log File in the logger window. The first line of each file names the Revit year, the instance id and the Revit process id, so a log can be matched to its Revit process. Example: dbtools-2026-ABC123-20260124-143022345-a1b2c3d4.log. Startup cleans up old files: at most 50 files across all instances, at most 14 days old, and at most 100 MB in total while more than one file remains (the newest file is kept even if it alone is larger). Failures that occur before logging starts are written to %APPDATA%\dbtools\Logs\dbtools.Fallback.log. When DBT_USER_DATA_DIR names a directory, the log files and dbtools.Fallback.log are in Logs\ below that directory. A refused value writes no file; the startup failure goes to Trace and to the startup failure dialog, which DBT_TEST_RUN_ID suppresses. Debug mode Debug mode lowers the minimum log level from Information to Debug, shows the logger window and flushes the log buffer every 120 ms instead of 600 ms. It is off at every startup and is not saved. It turns on when: you enable it in the Settings window or open the logger window; you click Details on an Error banner. This opens the logger window and turns on Debug Mode. An Error-level log entry by itself does not open the window. Closing the logger window turns debug mode off. Logger window The title is dbtools Log - Revit <Year> [<InstanceId>]. The window is a modeless utility window. The logger host applies pin mode changes centrally: a change that keeps the owner mode only updates Topmost, and a change of owner mode closes and recreates the window. Code must not change the owner of the live window directly. The window provides: the columns Source, Time, Level, Message and Duration. Source is narrow and shows the first namespace segment after dbtools and the type name, for example JoistGirderWeight · AutoUpdateTask. A name that does not fit is still and shortened in the middle, keeping the start of the tool and the end of the type name (Joist…AutoUpdateTask). While the pointer is over the row, or the row is selected, the full name scrolls as a ticker: it holds at its start, scrolls left and repeats after a gap. It returns to its start when the pointer leaves or the selection moves. With Windows animation effects off, names never scroll. Rows have no tooltips; message text without its markers: a leading [Tag] shows as a chip, and the execution phase, the elapsed time and the correlation ID leave the text. Duration shows the elapsed time of a timed entry, for example 460 ms, 5.6 s or 1 min 45 s; a details pane (the toolbar info button, a double-click on an entry, or Show Details in the context menu). Opening it scrolls the selected entry into view. It shows every value of the selected entry: time with milliseconds, level, full source, message, tag, phase, duration, correlation ID, the logged text and the exception. Copy details copies these values; the start row of a finished operation is hidden: its finish row shows the duration. A start row stays until its operation finishes, and a search shows every matching start row. Show Start Rows in the context menu shows every start row; level filters for INFO, WARN, ERROR and DEBUG, and a text search that matches the logged text and the displayed text; Copy All and Export, which save every retained entry in arrival order regardless of the filters, with the logged text unchanged. Export writes dbtools-log_<yyyyMMdd_hhmmss><AM|PM>.txt; auto-scroll, which follows new entries. Scrolling up pauses it until you scroll back to the bottom or until a new entry arrives after 15 s idle; turning it off keeps it off; Start New Log File (in the danger menu), which starts a new file, clears the window and logs a confirmation with the same instance ID. If closing the previous file fails, the new file stays active and a warning is logged. Correlation IDs and execution phases ISafeExecutor gives every operation a GUID correlation ID and logs its phases: ["Start"] "GM Apply" starting (CorrelationId=...) ["Complete"] "GM Apply" completed in 1234ms (CorrelationId=...) The log file and exports keep this text. The logger window shows GM Apply completed with 1.2 s in Duration, and keeps the phase and correlation ID in the details pane. Phase Level Meaning Start Information The operation started Complete Information The operation finished Cancel Warning The operation was canceled Error Error The operation failed Search for the correlation ID to find every entry of one operation and its duration. Reporting a problem Include: the log file from %APPDATA%\dbtools\Logs\, or a logger window export; the Revit version (year and build number); the dbtools version; the correlation ID of the failed operation; the steps to reproduce; a screenshot of any error dialog.

index.html.title: dbtools documentation | dbtools
index.html.summary: dbtools documentation dbtools is a set of tools for Autodesk Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027, mainly for structural engineering workflows. It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11 and installs for the current user. Sections Section Audience Contents User guide Revit users Installation, getting started and one page per tool. Developer guide Contributors Architecture, creating a new tool and troubleshooting. API reference Contributors Reference generated from the XML documentation comments. Tools Tool Purpose Global Mapper Bulk replacement of families, types, styles and materials; duplicate detection; shared parameters. Super Girt Tool Girt, header, sill and jamb placement on walls. Combined Foundation Tags Data and positions for combined pier and footing tags. Transfer Drafting Views Copy of drafting views between a project and a library. View Template Comparer Comparison and merge of view templates. The user guide lists all tools. Requirements Item Requirement Revit Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) or Revit 2027, desktop Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Account Standard user. The installer needs no administrator rights. Architecture dbtools.dll is the Revit entry point. It loads dbtools.Core (shared infrastructure and the tool registry), dbtools.Presentation (WPF resources and controls) and one assembly per tool from the Tools folder. The architecture overview describes the layers. Source: https://github.com/kirsch33/dbtools. Report problems on the issue tracker.

user-guide/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | dbtools
user-guide/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started NAME getting started - the dbtools ribbon, settings, banners and logs SYNOPSIS dbtools > Settings DESCRIPTION This page describes the parts that all tools share. RIBBON The tab has four panels: dbtools Common, dbtools Structural, dbtools Testing and dbtools Settings. This guide names a panel by its last word, such as dbtools > Structural. The user guide lists the tools on each panel. A tool button needs an open model. Only Settings works without one. A tool raises a settings warning when its settings are not valid, or when the model lacks something that the tool needs. Then the Settings button shows a warning icon, the dbtools tab is highlighted, and the buttons that need the missing item are disabled. Open Settings to read and fix the warning. SETTINGS Click Settings to open dbtools - Settings. dbtools saves settings for each Windows user and each Revit year. Settings that you make in Revit 2026 do not apply in Revit 2027. General starts open. Use a link on the left to open a section and move to its heading. A gold dot marks a section with active warnings. Settings opens those sections and scrolls to the first warning. A blue dot marks a section with unsaved pack edits. Option in General Default Effect Theme The Revit theme Dark or Light for every dbtools window. A choice shows at once. Save Settings keeps it; if you close the window without Save Settings, the saved theme returns. Common tools On Shows the dbtools Common panel. Structural tools On Shows the dbtools Structural panel. Testing tools On Shows the dbtools Testing panel. Background services On Controls background services, including Dialog Suppression. Clear this option to stop all services. Clear Enable Dialog Suppression in its pack to stop only that service. Debug Mode Off Opens the log window and adds Debug entries to the log. It applies at once and lasts until Revit closes. A cleared panel option hides the panel and stops its tools from auto-updating. Each tool's auto-update option controls whether it runs while its panel is enabled. Common Settings, Structural Settings, Testing Settings and Services Settings hold the settings packs of the tools. Some packs have an auto-update option, such as Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. It runs the tool each time you open or switch to a view. Button Effect Validate Checks the unsaved settings, opens sections with active warnings, and scrolls to the first warning card. It saves nothing. Save Settings Saves all changes and closes the window. A banner confirms the save. Text at the bottom of Settings tells when the changes apply. Reset All… Resets every setting at once, after you confirm. Reset to defaults on a pack Resets that pack at once, after you confirm. A pack that differs from its defaults shows Modified; otherwise the button is unavailable. Unsaved marks pack edits made since the last save. If you close the window without Save Settings, dbtools discards your changes without a prompt. BANNERS A tool shows its result in a banner at the top of its window or of the Revit window. Most banners close by themselves after 3 to 10 seconds, and an error stays longest. While the pointer is over the banners, no banner closes. A long message has a Details button, which opens the log window with the full text. An unexpected window error always has Details, even when its message is short. With more than three banners, the last row shows +<n> more. Click it to show all banners. LOGS dbtools writes one log file for each Revit session to %APPDATA%\dbtools\Logs\, named dbtools-<year>-*.log. A failure from before the log starts goes to dbtools.Fallback.log in the same folder. For a problem report, send the newest log. An unexpected window error shows an Error banner. Click Details to open the log window and turn on Debug Mode. Logging an error by itself does not open the log window. Debug Mode stays on until you clear it or Revit closes. In the log window, double-click an entry to see its details. Click Copy details to copy them, or Export to save all entries to a file. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Could not load settings. The settings file may be corrupt or inaccessible. Reset Settings keeps a copy of the settings file in %APPDATA%\dbtools\ and resets the settings. The banner names the copy. Close Settings closes only the settings window. Close closes only the message. SEE ALSO User guide, Installation

user-guide/index.html.title: User guide | dbtools
user-guide/index.html.summary: User guide NAME user guide - install dbtools and use its tools in Revit SYNOPSIS Installation, Getting started DESCRIPTION dbtools is an add-in for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. The tables list its tools by ribbon panel. TOOLS Common Page Use Global Mapper Replace content in bulk, find duplicates and add shared parameters. Transfer Drafting Views Copy drafting views to a library with Export To Library, and back with Import From Library. Elevation Tags Align spot elevation tags with Align Elevation Tags, and set their symbol text with Set Elevation Symbol Text. Structural Page Use Super Girt Tool Place girts and opening framing on a wall. Combined Foundation Tags Update combined foundation tags with Update Combined Foundation Tags, and move them with Move Combined Tags. Organize Foundation Types Organize foundation types for tagging. Analytical Snap To Level Move the ends of analytical members to a level. Allow Join and Disallow Join Allow or disallow joins at both ends of framing. Update Joist Girder Weights Estimate the weight of each joist girder. Testing The Testing tools are experimental. Page Use View Template Comparer Compare and merge view template settings. Record Set Package Revit models with their linked files. Extreme Roof Framing Tool Fit columns and beams to floor and roof slopes with Extreme Roof Framing. Services Dialog Suppression runs when Background services and Enable Dialog Suppression are on. Under Settings > Services Settings, use Dialog text patterns to choose which dialog text to match. A match suppresses a dialog that supports a result override. SEE ALSO Developer guide

user-guide/installation.html.title: Installation | dbtools
user-guide/installation.html.summary: Installation NAME installation - install, update and remove dbtools SYNOPSIS dbtools-Setup-<version>.exe dbtools-Setup-<version>.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES DESCRIPTION dbtools runs in desktop Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027, on 64-bit Windows 10 or later. Setup installs it for one Windows user and needs no administrator rights. Download dbtools-Setup-<version>.exe from the releases page. INSTALLING Close Revit. Run Setup as the Windows user who uses Revit. Setup installs into the %APPDATA% folder of that user only. On Revit versions, select the Revit years. Setup selects each compatible Revit on this computer. It disables each other year: Revit 2026 - update to 2026.5 or later: update Revit, then run Setup again. Revit <year> - not detected: that Revit year is not installed. Go to the next page. If dbtools is installed, Setup asks An existing dbtools.bundle was found. Replace it with this version? Click Yes. On Ready to install, check Product, Revit and Location. Click Install. The last page shows dbtools is installed. Open install folder opens %APPDATA%\dbtools. Start Revit. If the dbtools tab does not show, read the logs. UPDATING To update, run Setup of the version that you want. Setup replaces the whole bundle folder, so it deletes files that you added there. It keeps your settings and logs. dbtools does not check for updates. UNINSTALLING Close Revit. In Windows Settings > Apps, find dbtools and click Uninstall. The uninstaller deletes the bundle folder, and keeps your settings and logs in %APPDATA%\dbtools\. SILENT INSTALLATION Setup accepts the standard Inno Setup switches, such as /VERYSILENT and /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES. A silent install selects every compatible Revit year and replaces an installed version without a prompt. Run it in the Windows session of the Revit user. Setup writes a log during installation. Exit code Meaning 0 dbtools is installed. 10 Setup could not activate the copied files. Another code Setup did not install, for example because Revit is running or no compatible Revit is installed. The Setup log gives the reason. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Close Revit and run Setup again to install dbtools. Revit runs in your Windows session. Close it. Select at least one installed Revit version. For Revit 2026, install update 2026.5 or later. No Revit year is selected. dbtools could not be installed The last Setup page gives the reason and the path of the Setup log. It also tells whether your previous version is still installed. Close each program that uses a file in the dbtools folders, and run Setup again. A dbtools dialog when Revit starts, such as dbtools theme failed to load: dbtools could not start. Run Setup again. If the dialog shows again, send the log. FILES Path Contents %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\dbtools.bundle\ The add-in. Revit loads it at start. Contents\dbtools\<version>\<year>\ holds the files for one Revit year. %APPDATA%\dbtools\ The uninstaller, your settings, the logs in Logs\ and the tool caches in Cache\ SEE ALSO Getting started, User guide

user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.title: Analytical Snap To Level | dbtools
user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.summary: Analytical Snap To Level NAME Analytical Snap To Level - move the ends of analytical members to a level SYNOPSIS dbtools > Structural > Analytical Snap To Level DESCRIPTION The tool moves the end points of the selected analytical members to the elevation of one level. It changes only the curve of each analytical member. The plan position (X and Y) of the end points does not change. Select the analytical members. The button is enabled when any element is selected. Click Analytical Snap To Level. In Select Target Level, select a level. Each level shows as <name> (Elev: <elevation>), with the elevation in feet. The lowest level is first. Read the Snap to Level Complete result in Analytical Snap To Level. Click OK. REQUIREMENTS The tool skips a selected element that fails a rule, and reports the reason. Item Rule Skip reason Element An analytical member, not the physical beam or column not an analytical member Structural role Beam or Column, not another role such as Girder role not supported Curve A straight line. A curved member keeps its shape. not straight Length After the snap, the member is not shorter than Revit allows. An almost vertical beam fails this rule. would collapse The role sets which end points move: Role What moves Beam Both end points. The member becomes horizontal. Column Only the end point nearer the level. If both are equally near, the start point moves. RESULTS The completion window counts the processed and skipped elements. It shows one line for each skip reason: <reason>: <count> (element IDs <id>, <id>, and <n> more) It lists up to 10 IDs for each reason, and adds and <n> more for the rest. For not an analytical member, it shows only the count. The processed count includes members that were at the level already. Each run is one Undo step: dbtools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level. An error undoes the whole run. A skip does not. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do No target level selected. You closed the level window without a level, or the model has no levels. Nothing changes. LIMITS All selected members snap to the one level that you select. To use more levels, run the tool once for each level. To snap to an elevation without a level, add a level there. A sloped beam loses its slope. SEE ALSO Allow Join and Disallow Join, Getting started, dbtools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel

user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.title: Elevation Tags | dbtools
user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.summary: Elevation Tags NAME Elevation Tags - align spot elevation text with its leader, and set symbol text SYNOPSIS dbtools > Common > Align Elevation Tags dbtools > Common > Set Elevation Symbol Text DESCRIPTION Align Elevation Tags moves the text of each matching spot elevation in the active view beside its leader end, at the same gap for short and long text. It works in floor, structural and ceiling plans. A spot elevation is aligned when all of these are true: A pattern in Tag name patterns matches one of these names: the spot type, its family, the symbol type or the symbol family. It has a leader. The elevation base of its type is not Relative. Text Location Position of the text Above Leader, Below Leader Over the shoulder, on the side of the leader toward the point that the spot measures. A level leader puts the text below the leader. In-line with Leader Centered on the leader line, past the leader end. Align gives Above Leader and Below Leader the same position. This keeps the text off the symbol text of the DB Elevation Tag symbols. Set Elevation Symbol Text gives the selected spot elevations a symbol with other text. Enter the text, such as T.O. FTG., at Symbol text: and click Apply. The command copies the symbol family and the spot type, names each copy <original name> - <text>, and moves only the selected spots to the copy. The symbol type keeps its name. The same text again uses the same copies. The text must be on one line, without \ / : * ? " < > | { } [ ] ; ` ~. REQUIREMENTS Item Rule Symbol family For Set Elevation Symbol Text: an editable spot elevation symbol family with exactly one text element. SETTINGS Open dbtools > Settings, expand Common Settings and find Elevation Tags. Auto Update Elevation Tags runs Align, without a banner, each time you open or switch to a supported plan view. It is on by default. Tag name patterns holds up to 3 .NET regular expressions. Align and Alignment preview match the spot type and family names and the annotation symbol type and family names. Both ignore case. The default is: ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete|Steel|Wall) Label$ Alignment preview shows the offsets for the selected type in paper inches. The arrow buttons choose the type. A positive Along leader moves the text along the shoulder, away from the leader end. A positive Perpendicular moves it away from the leader line, or up for In-line with Leader. The next Align run uses the saved values. The preview draws the type with a downward and an upward leader. When you set an offset, a dashed outline shows the original text position. The only caption below the drawing is the type's Text Location in Revit. RESULTS Align ends with a banner, such as Aligned 12 elevation tag(s). A tag that is already in place does not count. Each run that moves tags, also an automatic run, is one Undo step: dbtools - Align spot elevations. Set Elevation Symbol Text is one Undo step: dbtools - Set elevation symbol text. It deletes a copy that it made when the change leaves the copy unused. A failure changes nothing. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do No spot elevation tags matched Tag name patterns. Check Elevation Tags settings. Compare the patterns with the type and symbol names. No matching elevation tags needed changes. Spot elevations without a leader are skipped. Each matching spot is in place, has no leader, or uses the Relative base. Symbol family '<name>' contains <n> plain text elements. Exactly one is required. Edit the symbol family so that it has one text element. Elevation Tags Disabled (a settings warning) Auto-update could not start, so Align and auto-update are off. Click Clear on the warning in Settings. LIMITS Align does not change spots in linked models. The placement suits a symbol that draws its text above its origin, as the DB Elevation Tag symbols do. With another symbol, the elevation text can cover the symbol text. The offsets are stored by spot type name, for every project. A renamed type or a copy from Set Elevation Symbol Text has no saved offsets unless its new name already has an entry. Align and Alignment preview include a copy when its annotation symbol type name matches a pattern. EXAMPLES To also align the spot types whose names start with Acme Spot, click + Add Pattern, enter this pattern and click Save Settings: ^Acme Spot SEE ALSO Getting started, dbtools.ElevationTags

user-guide/tools/erft.html.title: Extreme Roof Framing Tool | dbtools
user-guide/tools/erft.html.summary: Extreme Roof Framing Tool NAME Extreme Roof Framing Tool - set column and beam offsets to the underside of a floor or roof SYNOPSIS dbtools > dbtools Testing > Extreme Roof Framing To edit an adjustment, select its members, then click Edit ERFT on the contextual Modify tab. DESCRIPTION ERFT raises or lowers column tops and beam ends to fit a floor or roof. It writes Top Offset on columns and Start Level Offset and End Level Offset on beams. ERFT saves the adjustment for Edit ERFT. Click Extreme Roof Framing. Select a linked floor or roof. To pick one in the host model, press Esc. Select the columns and beams, then click Finish. Check the Columns and Beams tables, then click Apply. The target label shows the type and level. A linked target also shows the link name. ERFT projects vertically to downward-facing surfaces generated by the floor, roof or its modeled openings and uses the one nearest the member end. At equal distances, it uses the lower one. An end just beyond an edge can use the edge elevation within Revit's vertex tolerance. Member end Target elevation Column top The nearest underside elevation at the column's plan position. Beam end near a selected column top The adjusted top of the nearest column. Beam end near another selected beam's interior The adjusted location line of the supporting beam at that plan position. Beam end near a directly supported beam end The support elevation at the followed end. Other beam end The nearest underside elevation for that end. For beam ends, ERFT checks supports in the order shown. It uses a fixed 1/2 in. distance in three dimensions. A beam interior support point must also be more than 1/2 in. from either end of the supporting beam. Free ends from different beams can share a splice target when every pair is within 1/2 in. ERFT chooses among their rounded projected elevations. Up picks the highest, Down the lowest, and Nearest the first projecting end in beam ID order. ERFT rounds each end's change in steps of Tolerance: and adds it to the current offset. Up and Down apply where an end projects to the underside, including when choosing a shared splice target. An end that uses a support or a shared target rounds its own change with Nearest. A change of 0.000001 ft or less in either direction counts as zero. OPTIONS Control Effect Pick Selects another target and calculates again. Tolerance: 1/16", 1/8", 1/4" (default), 1/2", 1" or Custom. A custom value is in inches and at least 0.01. Use a decimal point. Nearest, Up, Down Round a projected change. At 1/4", -0.1 in. becomes 0 with Up and -0.25 in. with Down. Status Pending (will change), No Change (the rounded change is 0) or Error. Point to an Error cell to see the reason. Apply On when the tolerance is valid, a row is Pending and no row has Error. REQUIREMENTS Item Rule Column A structural column in the host model, placed at a point. Beam Straight structural framing in the host model, not a brace. Material ERFT leaves out a member whose structural material name has the word concrete, in any capitalization. Selection At least one column, or a beam with an end within 1/2 in. of a model column top in three dimensions. Target A floor or roof. RESULTS A beam that follows another beam end shows the followed end below its offset. Error rows show the current offsets. If a follower's support has no adjusted elevation, the tooltip names the followed end and its support. Apply writes the offsets and marks each changed member. On success the window closes and Revit records one Undo step, Extreme Roof Framing Tool. An expected failure rolls back the writes and shows Apply failed: with the reason. The window stays open. Canceling the tool rolls back the session. Edit ERFT restores the target, tolerance and rounding of the adjustment. It reads the current offsets and calculates again. If the selection holds more than one adjustment, select one in Select ERFT System. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do 3D Preview is unavailable: <reason> The message gives the preview failure. Apply depends on the adjustment plan and tolerance. LIMITS A beam can use only selected members as supports. A column in the model can qualify a beams-only selection. Select that column to use its adjusted elevation as a support. SEE ALSO Getting started, dbtools.ERFT

user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.title: Combined Foundation Tags | dbtools
user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.summary: Combined Foundation Tags Combined Foundation Tags prepares and positions the combined pier and footing tags (family DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag). It has two commands: Update Combined Foundation Tags computes the data that the combined tag displays and writes it to shared parameters on piers and footings. Move Combined Tags moves combined tags to a corner of the footing they tag. The tool does not place tags. Place the tags with Revit's tag commands. Synopsis Ribbon: dbtools > Structural > the foundation tags split button. The split button also contains Organize Foundation Types. Command Effect Update Combined Foundation Tags Writes Foundation Pier Top on piers, and Associated Pier and Associated Pier Elevation on footings, in the active view. Move Combined Tags Moves each matching tag in the active view to the corner of its footing that the tag's name specifies. Both commands are enabled when a view is active and process the active view only. Both are disabled while the shared-parameter prerequisites are not met (see Prerequisites). Prerequisites The update command needs three project parameters, bound as instance parameters and identified by GUID: Parameter Type Category Group Associated Pier Text Structural Foundations Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation Length Structural Foundations Identity Data Foundation Pier Top Length Structural Columns Constraints The required GUIDs come from the DB Structural group in the DB shared parameter file. A project parameter with a required name and another GUID can report GUID_MISMATCH. dbtools checks the parameters when the active model changes. If a parameter is missing, has another GUID, has the wrong data type, is bound as a type parameter, or is bound to the wrong category, or a loaded family defines one of these names with another GUID, dbtools activates the warning Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. The warning disables Update Combined Foundation Tags, Move Combined Tags and Organize Foundation Types, and the Settings button shows the warning icon. This check shows no banner. Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags also check the parameters each time they run, for example when you run one before the check on a model change has finished. In a family document they refuse to run. When a parameter fails, the command does not run. It activates the warning and shows one message, Required shared parameters need repair, that lists each failing parameter with its status and problem: Repair runs Install/Repair, as in Settings, including the prompt about schedule fields and view filters (see Schedule fields and view filters). After a successful repair, a banner confirms it and lists what changed; run the command again. Cancel changes nothing, and the warning stays. To repair the parameters in Settings: Open dbtools > Settings and expand Structural Settings. The Combined Foundation Tags pack lists each required parameter of the active project: its name and status, then its data type, category and group. A parameter that is not OK also shows its problem. All text wraps to the window width. Click Install/Repair under the list. The pack reads the active document when it opens. Without an open project, it shows No project open in place of the list; when a family is the active document, it shows A family is active. Install/Repair is then unavailable. The Settings window blocks Revit while it is open: close it, open or switch to the project, and open Settings again. Install/Repair needs an active project. It loads the definitions from the embedded shared parameter file, binds them to the required categories as instance parameters, and clears the warning. It keeps any other categories bound to these parameters and their values, and whether values can vary between group instances. If a parameter that already has the required GUID is bound as a type parameter (WRONG_BINDING_TYPE), Install/Repair changes it to an instance parameter and copies the value of each type to every instance of that type. If it is not bound to its required category (WRONG_CATEGORY), Install/Repair adds the category and keeps every value, including different values in instances of one group. For a parameter with another GUID (GUID_MISMATCH), Install/Repair replaces the parameter with the company definition and keeps: every category the old parameter was bound to, plus the required category, as instance categories; the old parameter group, and whether values can vary between group instances; every value: an element value stays on the same element, and the value of a type parameter is copied to every instance of that type. The company definition replaces the old parameter's visibility, description, user-modifiable and hide-when-no-value settings. The status message and the banner name each replaced parameter, the values kept, and each setting that changed. Install/Repair changes nothing and keeps the warning when it cannot keep every value: the old parameter has another data type, for example Area where Length is required; the parameter with the required GUID has another data type (WRONG_DATA_TYPE); Install/Repair cannot change the data type of a shared parameter, so delete that parameter in Manage > Project Parameters, which deletes its values, and run Install/Repair again; a value cannot be written to its element, for example because Revit blocks the change; a rebar container overrides the old parameter; Associated Pier Elevation or Foundation Pier Top (Length) has values on members of a group that is placed more than once. Revit changes such a value only in group edit mode, and it does not let a Length parameter vary between group instances, so dbtools cannot write it. Values of Associated Pier (Text) in such groups are kept; a type parameter has a value on a type that has no instances; a parameter with the required name and another GUID holds values next to the parameter that has the required GUID (DUPLICATE_NAME); more than one parameter has the required name and none has the required GUID. The message names the parameter and the reason. It lists up to 10 values that could not be kept. For a project parameter, it shows the family and type or the element name, followed by the ID. The dbtools log lists every affected value. Correct the cause and run Install/Repair again. A duplicate of a parameter that already has the required GUID (DUPLICATE_NAME) is deleted only when no element or type has a value for it; the status message names each deleted duplicate. A global parameter with one of these names is not a project parameter; Install/Repair leaves it alone. Status values include MISSING, GUID_MISMATCH, FAMILY_GUID_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_NAME, WRONG_DATA_TYPE, UNBOUND, WRONG_BINDING_TYPE and WRONG_CATEGORY. Families with another GUID A loaded family keeps its own copy of a shared parameter: a family parameter, or a label that shows the parameter. When a family uses one of these names with another GUID, its labels and formulas keep looking for that GUID. Revit also removes a deleted shared parameter from the labels of the families that use it, so a tag then shows nothing. Install/Repair therefore changes the families first and deletes the parameter with the other GUID only when no family uses it any more. When a project has a parameter with one of these names and another GUID, Install/Repair opens each family of the project to check it; in a project with many families this takes a while. For each family parameter with the name and another GUID, it: replaces the parameter in the family with the one from the DB shared parameter file, as an instance or type parameter as before, in the same group; keeps every formula, dimension label and label that uses the parameter, and every value of each family type; reloads the family into the project, then gives every element and type its value back and checks each one. When the company parameter is already bound, the status is FAMILY_GUID_MISMATCH and names the families whose types or elements show the parameter. A label that shows the parameter directly does not show in the status; Install/Repair finds it. Install/Repair changes the families in the project only. The family files in your library still use the other GUID; when you load such a file again, the problem comes back. Replace the parameter in the file too. Install/Repair changes nothing, keeps the warning, and names the family when: a label uses the parameter directly, as added through Edit Label > Add Parameter in a tag or title block family. dbtools cannot change a label. In Revit 2027 the message has one line per label: its detail group, the position of the parameter in the label, and its prefix, suffix, sample text, spaces before, line break before and non-breaking spaces, so you can add the company parameter with the same settings. Revit 2026 cannot tell which label it is. Open the family, select the label (in a detail group, use Edit Group first), click Edit Label, replace the parameter with the one from the DB shared parameter file, and load the family into the project again; a nested family uses the parameter, or the family is a shared family nested in another family; the family defines the parameter as a type parameter in Structural Foundations or Structural Columns, where the project binds it as an instance parameter; the family defines it with another data type; an element has one value for the family parameter and another for the project parameter; the family is in-place or cannot be edited, and it defines the parameter, or dbtools cannot tell whether it does. When its elements show the parameter and the project parameter could explain that, dbtools checks, without a change, whether the elements still show it without the project parameter; a value cannot be written back after the reload, for example because a formula computes it or the element is in a group placed more than once. Invalid parameter bindings When an add-in undoes a change to Values can vary by group instance of an existing parameter, Revit can leave the parameter bindings of the model in an invalid state until the model is reopened. dbtools does not leave this state, but it cannot read the parameters while it lasts. It then shows one message and changes nothing: Revit's parameter bindings for this model are in an invalid state; save, close and reopen the model, then try again. Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags show it as a warning banner and do not run. Settings shows it under Status not available in place of the parameter list, and Install/Repair shows it as its result. The check on a model change activates the warning Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. Save, close and reopen the model. dbtools checks the parameters again when the reopened model becomes active. Schedule fields and view filters When Install/Repair deletes a parameter (a replaced parameter or an empty duplicate), Revit also removes every schedule field that uses it and, from any view filter that uses it, the rules that go with it. This includes a field in an embedded schedule and a combined parameter field that includes the parameter. Revit removes a combined parameter field whole. Install/Repair cannot keep these fields or add them again. You must add the company parameter to those schedules by hand. A change of binding (WRONG_BINDING_TYPE or WRONG_CATEGORY) keeps the schedule fields. Revit removes each rule set of an affected view filter that has a rule on the deleted parameter, with every rule in that set. The filter keeps its categories and its other rule sets, so it can select other elements than before. A filter with no rules left applies to all elements of its categories. Install/Repair cannot keep or restore the removed rules. Before you continue, record whether each filter uses AND or OR and whether any rule is inverted. The rule list does not show this logic. After the repair, add every listed rule to each filter by hand, including rules that use other parameters. The list shows only the rules that Revit removes. The parameter list shows a warning marker, for example "Used in 2 schedules" or "Used in 1 view filter", below each parameter that Install/Repair would delete while a schedule or view filter uses it. Below the marker, each line names a schedule and the field heading, or a view filter, rule parameter and rule. Install/Repair cannot see the formula of a calculated field, so a calculated field that uses the parameter is not listed; check calculated fields after the repair. When the repair would remove schedule fields or view filter rules, Install/Repair (the pack button or Repair in a command's message) asks before Revit deletes them. The prompt lists each schedule, field and parameter, and each view filter, rule parameter, rule and deleted parameter. It tells you to record each filter's logic before you continue: Cancel changes nothing. The parameters, values, bindings, schedules and view filters stay as they are, and the warning stays. Continue checks the project again. If the list changes and still contains fields or rules to remove, Install/Repair asks again before applying the repair. The status message and banner list the fields and rules that Revit removes. If a later value check fails, Install/Repair reports the refusal and rolls back the repair. After you continue, open each listed schedule and add the company parameter again, with its formatting, sorting, grouping, filters and conditional formatting. Open each listed view filter and add every listed rule with the parameter named for that rule. Use the AND/OR logic and inverted rules that you recorded before the repair. Update Combined Foundation Tags Usage Open a plan view that shows the piers and footings. Run Update Combined Foundation Tags. Read the banner. Floor and ceiling plans are eligible for automatic updates when Auto Update Combined Foundation Tags is on and the prerequisite warning is inactive. What it does The command considers the family instances visible in the active view. A family instance is a pier when its family name matches a pier pattern. It is a footing when its family name matches a footing pattern (see Settings). For each pier, it computes Foundation Pier Top = the Top Offset parameter (0 if absent) plus the elevation of the level in the Top Level parameter, and writes it to the pier. For each footing, it finds the nearest pier within 2 ft in plan (X and Y). It writes the pier type's Type Mark to Associated Pier. When a computed top is available, it writes the top to Associated Pier Elevation. With no pier within 2 ft, the updater clears Associated Pier and Associated Pier Elevation where the bindings allow it. For a member of a group placed more than once, the updater compares each parameter before writing it. This includes nested groups whose enclosing group is placed more than once. Equal values need no write and do not count as skipped. A changed parameter is written if it varies between group instances, such as Associated Pier when that setting is enabled. A changed parameter that does not vary is skipped. Other parameters and elements still update in the same run. A group placed once still works. Revit changes non-varying values in repeated groups only in group edit mode. Length parameters cannot vary between group instances, and the Revit API cannot enter group edit mode. The updater keeps the parameter's existing variance setting. When a repeated group blocks the write to Foundation Pier Top, the footing can still use the computed top. If the pier has an unconnected Top Level, the footing can still get the pier type's Type Mark. A value is written only when it differs. Lengths are compared after rounding to two decimals. Clearing Associated Pier Elevation requires a shared parameter with Hide when no value. If Revit refuses the clear, the updater counts the footing as skipped. The detail entry includes the footing ID and parameter name. If the matched pier has an unconnected Top Level and the footing has a stored elevation, the updater keeps it and counts the footing as skipped. Result The banner reads Updated N element(s); M failed/skipped. or No elements modified. An element is counted as skipped when a pier lacks a valid Top Level, a footing or pier has no location point, a parameter is missing or read-only, or a length cannot be cleared. An element also counts as skipped when a changed parameter does not vary between instances of its repeated group. It enters the Skipped selection set and can also enter Modified if another parameter changes. Each run logs up to ten failure details at Warning across piers, footings and repeated groups. A separate warning gives the full skipped count and up to ten element IDs. For repeated groups, the banner adds N skipped: in groups placed more than once (Revit allows these values only in group edit mode). Outcome Banner At least one element modified Stays open. Has Select Modified, and Select Skipped when some elements were skipped. Nothing modified, some skipped Warning that closes after 8 seconds. No buttons. Nothing modified or skipped Info that closes after 5 seconds. When every value is already current, the updater creates no selection sets and changes nothing. The manual result is an Info message. The buttons select the elements of the run that just finished. They work only while the model that ran the update is active. Each run also creates selection sets named dbtools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (<timestamp>) and dbtools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (<timestamp>) when the respective list is not empty. The timestamp is in Eastern time. A second run in the same second adds a suffix such as (2). When the updater creates a set, it keeps up to five sets with the prefix dbtools - FoundationTags - across both kinds. It deletes sets outside the five highest element IDs. Move Combined Tags Usage Open a plan view with combined tags. Run Move Combined Tags. What it does The command examines the independent tags in the active view. It moves a tag when: the tag points to a Structural Foundations family instance; the tag's family or type name matches a tag family pattern; and the tag's name is a corner name. The corner name is Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right or Bottom Left (case-insensitive). If the tag has no name, the command reads its type name. The command uses the view orientation to choose the footing corner. It moves the tag head to that corner and keeps its elevation. Result The banner reads Moved N; skipped M of K candidate tags. A candidate is skipped when the corner name is not valid, the tagged element is not a family instance with a location point, or it has no geometry. When no candidate exists, the banner says why: Message Cause No tags were found in the active view. No independent tags in the view. No tags in the active view are currently tagging structural foundation elements. The view's tags tag other categories. No tags matched the patterns in Tags to move. Check Combined Foundation Tags settings. Sample rejected tag families/types: <list> Tags tag foundations, but no tag family pattern matches. Settings Open dbtools > Settings and select the Combined Foundation Tags pack. Setting Default Used by Auto Update Combined Foundation Tags On Update (floor and ceiling plan activation) Tags to move ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ Move Piers to update ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ Update Footings to update ^(?:Footing\|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ Update Each pattern list holds up to 3 regular expressions. Matching is case-insensitive. An empty list uses the default. An invalid expression is skipped and logged. When no valid pier or footing pattern exists, the update does nothing. When no valid tag pattern exists, the move does nothing. Limitations Both commands work on the active view only. Only family instances that are visible in the active view are updated. The nearest-pier search is 2D and has a fixed 2 ft radius. Piers and footings are recognized by family name only. Families with other names need a matching pattern. The corner a tag moves to is taken from its name. A tag with another name is skipped. Install/Repair cannot change a label that uses a required parameter with another GUID directly, or the family files in your library. See Families with another GUID.

user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.title: Allow Join and Disallow Join | dbtools
user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.summary: Allow Join and Disallow Join NAME Allow Join, Disallow Join - allow or disallow joins at both ends of framing SYNOPSIS dbtools > Structural > Allow Join or Disallow Join DESCRIPTION The two commands share one split button. Allow Join allows joins at both ends of each selected Structural Framing family instance, such as a beam. Disallow Join disallows joins at both ends. Select the framing. The commands are enabled when the selection holds at least one Structural Framing element. On the split button, click Allow Join or Disallow Join. Read the banner. RESULTS A run changes the selected Structural Framing family instances. It ignores other elements, such as structural columns, and does not report them. The banner shows Allowed joins on <n> element(s). or Disallowed joins on <n> element(s). The count <n> includes elements that had that join state already. Each run is one Undo step: dbtools - Allow Join Selected or dbtools - Disallow Join Selected. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Failed to apply allow join operation for element <id>. Revit refused the change for that element. The run stops and changes nothing. The message says disallow for Disallow Join. Find the element with Manage > Select by ID. LIMITS A command always sets both ends of each element. It cannot set one end only. SEE ALSO Analytical Snap To Level, Getting started, dbtools.FramingJoins

user-guide/tools/gm.html.title: Global Mapper | dbtools
user-guide/tools/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper Global Mapper (GM) replaces project content in bulk. You map a source (a family, a type, a line style, an object style, a material or a parameter) to a target, review the plan, and apply every mapping in one operation. GM also finds likely duplicates, ranks replacement candidates by name and property similarity, and adds shared parameters to families and categories. Synopsis Ribbon: dbtools > Common > Global Mapper. GM opens as a modeless window and needs an open, active project. It works on the active document only. Linked files are not changed. GM opens on the Families tab with only Generic Annotations checked. It restores Search, sort mode, Threshold, Hide Unused, Hide Unscanned, and Applied Only for the project. It restores the Shared Parameters category and type when available, duplicate selections and exclusions, and saved mappings. Family rows start collapsed. Tab Purpose Duplicates Finds likely duplicate elements and lets you choose which one to keep. Families Maps families and their types, parameters, object styles and materials to other families. Line Styles Replaces line styles. Object Styles Replaces Detail Items object styles. Materials Replaces materials. Shared Parameters Adds shared parameters to families and categories, or maps existing parameters to them. The Shared Parameters tab needs a Revit shared parameter file with at least one group. Without one, GM disables the tab and explains why. Startup waits for all category and parameter-group reads to finish. If a read fails while another is canceled, GM reports the failure. Startup clears the loading state after the reads finish. Usage Open a tab. Choose the source rows to change and the target for each. A target can be chosen by hand or by the similarity ranking. Check Apply on each mapping to include in this run. Click Review Plan. GM opens Commit Review as a modal window and shows the plan. The model is not changed until you click Apply there. If the plan has nothing to apply, GM shows the reason in a banner and does not open Commit Review. Click Apply. Then choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back (see Commit Review). Save the project before a bulk change. Header controls These controls apply to the current tab. Control Effect Search: Filters rows by name. Threshold: Slider from 0 to 100%. Sets the minimum similarity for automatic target selection. Sort mode (Similarity / A-Z) Orders target lists by similarity, with colored scores, or alphabetically with no scores. One setting covers the top-level and nested target lists. Hide Unused Hides elements with no instances in the project. Hide Unscanned Hides unscanned rows. Shown on the Families and Shared Parameters tabs only. Applied Only Shows rows with Apply on, including rows linked from other tabs. Not shown on Duplicates, which has its own status filter. Inspector Pane, Preview Panel, Views Panel, SP Authoring Pane Show or hide those panes.
