Refresh Cache Rebuilds Duplicates, Families, the three Usage tabs and Shared Parameters from the current project. Keeps saved mapping choices and Deep Scan results for unchanged families. Clear... menu Clear Saved Mappings, Clear Saved UI State, Clear Deep Scan Cache (see Saved state). Mapping Conflicts Opens the conflict list. Shown when conflicts exist. Auto-Resolve All resolves them in the order: Duplicates, Tab Defaults, Family Overrides, Manual. The status line at the bottom left shows the loading state, the number of visible rows and the number of applied and conflicting rows of the current tab. A grid shows Loading... while data loads and a No ... message when a loaded result is empty. Similarity and threshold GM scores each target against its source. Scores use the same theme roles in every pane: 90–100 Success, 70–89 Secondary, 50–69 Warning, and 0–49 Muted. Options without a score use Body. At a threshold, an unchanged row selects the highest-scoring target at or above it. If no target qualifies, the row stays empty. A manual target choice stays when you change the threshold. Opening a list and closing it without picking another entry keeps the current selection. Use Apply to include a mapping with a valid target. Clear Apply to exclude a mapping and keep its target. GM remembers that choice when you change the threshold or category, change the parent target, or refresh or rescan the project. On the Duplicates tab, the threshold controls which keep-target candidates appear for each source row. Duplicates tab The tab scans automatically when you open it. Deep scan Some family details, such as embedded parameters and nested families, need a deep scan. A deep scan opens the family document. It is always started by you; GM does not scan when you expand a row. A deep scan is needed to: unlock the expanded details of a family with no instances (Scan required); read embedded definitions, such as nested family graphs, that a placed instance does not expose. Moving an instance keeps its family’s Deep Scan results. Refresh Cache checks the family definition and the number of placed instances of each type before reusing a result. For a family with instances, GM reads Object Styles and Materials from one placed instance. Materials also include the placed shared components inside it. When planning a material replacement, GM checks one placed instance of each type for the source. During Apply, nested children are eligible when the parent contains the source material by name or one of its categories or subcategories takes that material from project Object Styles. GM checks eligible shared children already loaded in the project against their current definition. Action Effect Scan Family (in the expanded details) Always runs a fresh deep scan. A complete result replaces the cache entry. An incomplete result removes the previous reusable entry. Deep Scan Unscanned (top-bar icon, Families tab) Scans eligible unscanned families with no instances across the project, after confirmation. Clear Deep Scan Cache Checks saved and loaded results. If the cache is empty, GM reports that without asking for confirmation. After you confirm a clear, GM deletes the results and refreshes the display. The progress overlay shows the project read, the number of families scanned, cache preparation, and the display refresh. Select Cancel while GM scans families to stop after the current family. GM discards the run's results and skips opening the next family. If cancellation reaches GM after it writes the cache and before it applies the scan, the cache keeps its changes. The display keeps its previous results. Results are cached across sessions. At startup GM restores cached results for eligible families with no instances. The restore is strict: if the cache entry does not resolve in the current document (for example a missing or ambiguous style or material), GM logs a warning and leaves the family unscanned. No banner appears. If you clear the cache while the restore runs, the cleared families stay unscanned until you scan them again. If Revit reports an error while GM reads a family parameter, GM keeps the names it read as diagnostics and marks parameter discovery incomplete. Those names are not offered as mapping choices and are not used for duplicate scoring. GM also removes the older reusable cache entry for that family. A separate successful read of the host can still fill the mapping choices. Otherwise, scan again after you fix the reported problem. If GM cannot fully resolve nested-family or material usage during a scan, it keeps the extracted details and warnings visible as a partial result, and does not cache or restore the family as complete. Scan again after you fix the reported references. A malformed or incomplete cache entry is deleted and needs a new scan. The cache is disposable and is not migrated between formats. Saved state GM saves your mappings and window state for each project, by its file path. Each unsaved document has its own state, so unsaved documents with the same title do not share state. On reopen, saved targets are restored with Apply off. An explicit exclusion is saved with its target and stays in effect until you check Apply again. Menu item (Clear...) Effect Clear Saved Mappings Removes the mapping and duplicate selections for this document. The mappings do not return from an older saved file or from an open GM window. Clear Saved UI State Removes saved UI state for the document, including search, sort, threshold and filters. The next GM window starts with default settings. An open window does not write its older state back when it closes. Clear Deep Scan Cache Checks for results before asking for confirmation. A confirmed clear removes deep-scan data and the DS badges. When GM asks for confirmation, select Cancel to keep the saved data. A completed clear shows a success banner, for example Cleared saved mappings for this document. A failed clear shows an error banner titled with the action, for example GM Clear Saved Mappings, and no success banner. If GM cannot write the saved mappings, it logs the failure and shows an error banner, and your mappings may not persist. A saved row with no target restores as excluded. An exclusion is saved separately from the last committed mapping for that row. An invalid saved-mappings file produces an error banner and stays on disk. GM flags a saved target that is unavailable so you can choose it again. A Shared Parameters Map From choice stays pending while its source is unavailable. If a later scan finds the source, GM restores the choice and its Apply setting. A style target must belong to the scope of its source (Line Styles or Object Styles). Each of the Materials, Line Styles and Object Styles tabs lists only its own kind of element. When a family and a project tab map the same Material or Object Style source, the family uses its own mapping. Clearing Apply on a family row excludes the source in that family from the project mapping. A shared nested family also keeps its own mapping or Apply exclusion when a parent maps the same source. If the child has no choice of its own and the project mapping reaches it, the project mapping handles the shared document. GM reports the skipped child on the parent mapping. A family Material mapping updates writable material parameters on its placed instances. Project face paint stays in place and appears as a warning. Result Commit Review While GM builds the plan, its overlay names the current step. Review Plan then opens Commit Review centered on the GM window. Revit is blocked and the GM window is dimmed while it is open. The window shows: the planned operations, by section (Plan Overview, Planned Operations, Host Replacements, Family Changes, Nested Families, Shared Parameters, Validation Issues); sections that do not apply are hidden; after apply, Commit Results, Stage Summary (succeeded, failed and skipped counts per stage, with affected references, family and timing context) and Family Breakdown; an Operation Results table with a status for each operation (Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped), its operation id, stage and timing. Failed operations are summarized per mapping rule, with the source and target display names rather than element ids. The status bar shows the apply phase before the commit and the Applied, Skipped and Failed counts after it. Right-click a report table for Copy Selected or Copy All. Copy Report copies the whole report. Failed in the rules summary counts failed mapping rules. One rule can run across many families. Use the Families line (Planned / Attempted / Failed) and the Failed Operations row, which adds up the per-family failures. Apply and keep Apply runs the plan as one operation. The changes stay provisional while Commit Review shows the results. The commit continues after a failed operation: failures are recorded and the remaining operations run. The progress overlay shows on Commit Review, and its Cancel button requests cancellation at once. After a run in which no operation failed, GM checks that no references to a source remain. After a failed operation it does not check: the failure is the reason. Outcome What you can do Every operation succeeded and verification found no remaining source Choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back. An operation failed, verification found a remaining source, or the apply was canceled GM rolls the attempt back. Nothing is kept. Inspect the errors and choose Retry Apply to run the reviewed plan against the current model. Succeeded with nonfatal warnings Labeled Completed with Warnings. The Operation Warnings section lists each distinct instance, parameter and reason. Review it before you keep the changes. Keep remains available when verification succeeds. Keep + Continue records the mappings and returns to GM. GM refreshes the mapped data in place and restores the expanded row context. Types created with Create appear in the refreshed rows. Deep Scan results stay for families the commit did not change. Scan a changed family again to restore its details. Keep + Close GM records the mappings and closes GM. Roll back restores the model and creates no undo entry. A kept apply is one undo entry named Global Mapper: Apply. Press Ctrl+Z to revert it. If Revit closes Commit Review during shutdown, GM rolls back any apply you have yet to keep. Do not leave Commit Review open after Apply. Choose Keep or Roll back first. Closing the window with the X: during apply, requests cancellation and cleanup, then closes. If the cleanup fails, the window stays open and shows the error; after a successful apply, asks whether to keep or roll back, with Roll back as the default; after an apply that kept nothing (failed or canceled), closes without asking. After any apply, GM re-reads the affected rows and counts from the model, whether the apply was kept or rolled back. A banner reports the outcome: A successful apply shows a green banner with the Applied, Failed and Skipped counts. If the apply or the plan has warnings, the banner is a warning banner that ends with Warnings: <n>. A failed apply shows a red banner that starts with Apply failed. Nothing was changed. and names the first failed mapping and its reason, for example DB WWF / Wire Mesh → DB Rebar Horizontal Mat / DB Rebar Horizontal Mat: Can't change type of "DB Rebar Horizontal Mat : DB Rebar Horizontal Mat" from line based to non-line based or vice-versa. When Revit refuses a change, the reason is Revit's own text. Commit Review stays open. A canceled apply shows Apply was canceled. Nothing was changed. If an apply seems to stall near 90%, Revit is still processing one operation. Click Cancel once and wait. GM cancels and cleans up when that operation ends. If it does not recover, report it with the newest dbtools log. How replacement batches behave Line styles, host materials, family materials, family object styles, types, host symbols and nested-family replacements use each mapping's original source population. A swap A to B and B to A exchanges the populations. A chain A to B and B to C leaves the original A population on B and the original B population on C. References moved by an earlier mapping do not become a later mapping's source. A shared nested family can appear under several selected roots. GM combines its applicable mappings and changes each original reference once. Later family reloads keep the result. Equivalent duplicate mappings get a merged notice. Conflicting targets for the same family source need your attention. A source that is absent from a traversed family is zero work, not a failed mapping. When a family reload cannot complete, every family operation that ran in that traversal is shown as failed, including equivalent shared-family aliases. The report keeps the affected count for writes completed before the failure and shows the reason. GM rolls the whole apply back, and you can choose Retry Apply. A failed operation can report writes that succeeded before it failed. Those counts are diagnostics, and the rollback discards the writes. If one half of a swap fails, the successful half could leave both populations on one target. For that reason GM rolls back the whole apply. Unchanged shared children stay on the project version during another family's reload. Shared children that the current traversal changed are reloaded from the edited family document. The family-document counts in Commit Review include the examined root and nested family documents, including documents where a source has no references. A parent-only material mapping leaves a shared child's material defaults unchanged. Map the child itself, or include it in the traversal, to change those defaults. Messages GM reports results and problems in banners with the title Global Mapper. While Commit Review is open, its banners show on the Commit Review window. Message Meaning Apply completed. Applied: <n>, Failed: <n>, Skipped: <n>. Family documents attempted: <n>, family document failures: <n>. The apply finished. The banner adds Warnings: <n>. when operations or the plan reported warnings. Apply failed. Nothing was changed. <source> → <target>: <reason> An operation failed, and GM rolled the attempt back. The reason is Revit's own text when Revit refused the change. Change that mapping, or choose Retry Apply for a failure that a retry can fix. Apply failed. Nothing was changed. <error> The apply stopped with an error. Commit Review stays open. Apply was rolled back. Nothing was changed. <kind> with remaining references: <names>. Every operation succeeded, but the check after the apply found a remaining source reference. <operation> failed. The dbtools log has the cause. An operation failed without a Revit reason, for example ReplaceType failed. The dbtools log has the cause. or Failed to change instance type. The dbtools log has the cause. Read the newest dbtools log. Apply was canceled. Nothing was changed. You canceled the apply. Keep is unavailable: the last apply kept no changes. Retry Apply or close Commit Review. Keep was chosen after an apply that was rolled back. No conflicts to resolve. Auto-Resolve All found no conflicts. No auto-resolvable conflicts were found. The remaining conflicts need a manual choice. No unscanned (0-instance) families are eligible for deep scan. The project has no family eligible for Deep Scan Unscanned. Deep scan cache is empty. Clear Deep Scan Cache found no saved or loaded results. Deep scan cache cleared. Clear Deep Scan Cache finished. Cleared saved mappings for this document. Clear Saved Mappings finished. Cleared saved UI state. Next open will use defaults. Clear Saved UI State finished. Map From source parameter '<name>' is not available. A Shared Parameters Map From source is missing from the current options. The choice and its Apply setting wait for the source to return. Configure a Revit shared parameter file that has at least one group to use this tab. The Shared Parameters tab is disabled. Set a shared parameter file in Revit. No operations selected. Tip: check the Apply column on families, or map materials/styles on the Usage tabs. Review Plan found nothing to apply. Commit Review does not open. Commit Review could not build the plan: <reason> Review Plan failed. The banner title is GM Commit Review. Commit Review does not open. The plan selects more than one GUID for shared parameter '<name>' (<GUID>, <GUID>). Pick one definition for this name. Review Plan found mappings to different definitions with the same name. Use one definition for all mappings with that name. Shared parameter '<name>' with GUID <GUID> is missing from the current shared parameter file. Review Plan, By parameter, or Apply could not find the selected definition in the current file. Load the file that contains it, or select a definition from the current file again. More than one shared parameter definition matches '<name>'. Select the definition again. Review Plan, By parameter, or Apply found several definitions for a selection by name. Select the intended definition from its SP Group. Apply the repair on its own: clear the other mappings, or apply them first. Review Plan found a repair and other mappings. Commit Review does not open. "<name>" already exists in this project with another GUID. Repair it in By parameter first. A bind or embed would add a second GUID for the name. Repair the parameter first. At plan time, Commit Review shows Shared parameter GUID conflicts prevent Apply. The project changed after Review Plan. Review the plan again. The repair scan at apply found a change since the review. Nothing changed. Binding "<name>" as a type parameter could change values that loaded families hold. Bind it as an instance parameter. Loaded families define the parameter and the project does not bind it. GM cannot add a category to the type binding of "<name>" and prove that every value stays. Add the category in Manage > Project Parameters. The parameter has a type binding. Manual shared parameter repair remains: <text> An operation warning after a repair. Fix the named use by hand. Inline texts: Deep scan to unlock details for families without instances (row tooltip): the family has no instances and no deep scan. Run Scan Family. Parameter scanning is unavailable; parameter mapping is disabled. and No mappable parameters detected for this family. (Parameters detail tab). line-style targets pending Usage indexing (Duplicates row): wait until indexing ends. Scan the families first. (By parameter repair table): the scan did not finish, or Revit did not open every editable family. Click Scan families. No families in the shown categories. (By parameter family table): no family of the shown categories can take the parameter. Check Show all categories. When an action fails unexpectedly, GM shows an error banner titled with the action, for example GM Duplicate Type Mapping, GM Deep Scan or GM Clear Saved Mappings, followed by the error text. Retry it, and read the dbtools log if it fails again. If Refresh Cache cannot read the fresh project data, affected Usage rows return to their pending state. Saved mapping choices are kept. Review Plan is disabled when no operation is selected or a blocking conflict exists. Checking a family checks each type with a valid target. You can also check individual types. If the target list is empty, the category has no other family. If some instances were not replaced, open the family and check that every type is mapped. Limitations GM changes the active document only. Line style and object style scopes are limited as described above: curves in multi-instance groups are not restyled, and the Object Styles tab covers Detail Items subcategories only. Commit time grows with the number of elements and families. A few dozen changes finish at once; thousands can take minutes. The progress overlay shows the state. Revit 2027 repairs annotation labels when the internal API is available and every check passes. A failed check leaves a hand-fix row with its reason. Revit 2026 does not let dbtools read annotation labels. An annotation family that contains an old GUID keeps the binding move closed until the family no longer contains it. A repair changes the families loaded in the project, not the family files on disk. A family loaded again from an old file brings the old GUID back. A repair moves uses only to the company definition with the same name. To move values between two names, use Map From. GM does not repair these cases. The row shows the reason and has no tick: The project already binds the company GUID. More than one other GUID with the name has a project parameter. A combined parameter schedule field, a schedule with a calculated field (Revit counts a percentage field as one), or a schedule filter value that GM cannot carry. A view filter rule or evaluator that GM cannot carry and verify. A non-editable nested family that dbtools cannot inspect, in a family that uses the old GUID directly (not as a family parameter). GM moves a family parameter even when its family has a non-editable nested family. If a hidden use keeps the old GUID after the reload, GM refuses the move and rolls the attempt back. A schedule field that shows totals, a minimum or a maximum that the company parameter's field cannot show refuses the binding move at apply. By parameter has no Formula source. Write formulas in By family.

user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.title: Update Joist Girder Weights | dbtools
user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.summary: Update Joist Girder Weights NAME Update Joist Girder Weights - estimate the weight of each joist girder and write it to Wt SYNOPSIS dbtools > Structural > Update Joist Girder Weights DESCRIPTION The tool estimates the self-weight of each joist girder in the model, in pounds per foot (lb/ft). It writes the estimate to the girder's Wt parameter and changes nothing else. A joist girder is a Structural Framing element whose family name matches Family/type name. By default, these are the families G Joist Girder, BG Joist Girder, VG Joist Girder and Vulcraft Joist Girder. The estimate uses four values of the girder: Length, Depth, Number of Joists and the point load. The point load is the load, in kips, at each panel point where a joist bears on the girder. The tool works on the whole model. It skips a girder with a missing or invalid value. REQUIREMENTS For each value, the tool tries each listed name on the girder, then on its type, and uses the first value found. Value Parameters Rule Number of Joists Number of Joists, SpaceNum, Number of Equal Spaces Must be more than 1. Enter the number of equal spaces, not of joists. Length Cut Length, Length Must be more than 0. Depth Depth Must be more than 0. Point load Parameters that match the load patterns See Loads. Weight Wt An editable Number parameter. The tool writes lb/ft here. Text values for the first three must be plain numbers. Length and Depth are in feet. A parameter of type Length works in any display units. In a Number or text parameter, enter 48 in. as 4. Loads A populated total load sets the point load, including an explicit zero. Otherwise, the tool adds the dead and live loads if both groups have inputs and at least one group has a value. The load patterns in SETTINGS find each kind by parameter name. The tool skips the girder when two usable inputs of one kind have values, when a Force load is negative, or when no usable load exists. The tool reads Revit Force parameters and converts their values to kips. It also reads nonnegative loads from Text parameters. A plain number means kips. Text accepts k, kip, kips, lb, lbs, lbf, pound, pounds, or kN. Use a decimal point and optional commas for thousands. Examples include 10, 10 kips, 10,000 lb, and 45 kN. The tool ignores matching parameters of other types, including Yes/No, Number, and Family Type. It also ignores invalid load text. If no load resolves, the skip message names each ignored match and its reason and shows any invalid text. The tool ignores a blank total. A dead or live load group with only blank Force or Text inputs counts as zero if the other group has a value. A Dead Load of 2 kips and a blank Live Load give 2 kips. An instance load input takes precedence over a type input with the same name, even when blank. SETTINGS Open dbtools > Settings, expand Structural Settings and find Joist Girder Weights. Auto Update Joist Girder Weights runs the tool, without a banner, each time you open or switch to a view. It is on by default. It can slow view changes in a large model. To see what it skips, run the tool from the ribbon. The four patterns are .NET regular expressions. By default, the load patterns match DL, LL, and names that contain Dead Load, Live Load, Point Load or Total Load. Family/type name ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ Total Load (?:Point\s*Load|Total\s*Load) Dead Load (?:^DL$|Dead\s*Load) Live Load (?:^LL$|Live\s*Load) RESULTS A run from the ribbon ends with a banner like this: Candidates: 12 Updated: 10 Skipped: 2 Sample skipped element(s): - Element 412345: Depth must be > 0. - Element 412377: Number of joists must be > 1. Candidates is the number of joist girders found. The banner lists up to 5 skipped girders, with the first problem of each. Find each girder with Manage > Select by ID, fix it, and run the tool again. Each run that changes values is one Undo step: Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Required writable Double parameter 'Wt' not found. Add Wt as an editable Number parameter. Missing required input for 'Point Load'. … The tool lists missing or blank loads and explains which matching parameters it ignored. Supply a total or a dead and live pair with at least one value. Use Force or Text parameters. Ambiguous <kind> Load inputs: … More than one parameter of that kind has a value, including any explicit zero. Clear all but one. Joist Girder Weights Disabled (a warning in Settings) A saved pattern is not valid, so the tool is off. Correct the pattern and click Save Settings. Auto-update failed; disabled for this document session. Auto-update stays off until you reopen the model. LIMITS The weight is an estimate from a fixed formula, not from SJI or manufacturer tables. Make Wt an instance parameter. A type parameter gives all girders of that type one value. A Wt with units, such as Length, shows a wrong value. EXAMPLES To also use the family Acme Girder, set Family/type name to this value and click Save Settings: ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$|^Acme Girder$ SEE ALSO Getting started, dbtools.JoistGirderWeight

user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.title: Organize Foundation Types | dbtools
user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.summary: Organize Foundation Types Organize Foundation Types renames pier, footing and pile cap types by their dimensions, assigns sequential type marks, and merges eligible types of the same size. It changes types and keeps placed instances in position. Synopsis Ribbon: dbtools > Structural > the foundation tags split button (with Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags). The command processes the whole model. It is disabled while the Combined Foundation Tags Disabled warning is active (see Combined Foundation Tags). Usage Save the model. Run Organize Foundation Types. If a processed type has a Type Mark, choose Overwrite Existing Marks or Preserve Existing Marks. Choose Cancel, or close the question, to stop without changing the model. Read the Organize Foundation Types result dialog. When no processed type has a Type Mark, the command runs without asking. Choice Effect Overwrite Existing Marks Regenerates the Type Mark of each retained type. Preserve Existing Marks Keeps every existing Type Mark. Assigns new marks only to types with blank marks and skips every existing mark when choosing a new one. Keeps equal-size types with different marks separate. Cancel or close Stops the command without changing the model. Processed types The tool processes types of these families (exact names, case-sensitive): Family Category Dimension parameters Mark prefix Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Types of other families are not processed. Naming and marks Each type is renamed as <dimensions> (<mark>). Dimensions are formatted in feet and fractional inches. Family Name format Example Foundation Pier <b>x<h> (<mark>) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Foundation Pier - Round <d> DIA. (<mark>) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) Pile Cap-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 4'-0"x4'-0"x2'-0" (CAP-4.0) Types are processed in ascending order of size, and marks are assigned in that order: piers: section area b x h, then b and h when areas match; round piers: diameter; footings and pile caps: width, then length, then thickness. Pier and round pier marks are P-1, P-2, ... and RP-1, RP-2, .... Footing and pile cap marks are <prefix>-<w>.<n>, where <w> is the width in whole feet (rounded down) and <n> counts from 0 within that width: F-3.0, F-3.1, CAP-4.0. Preserve Existing Marks reserves every existing mark before assigning new ones. Overwrite Existing Marks assigns new marks in size order and reserves old marks when a type is skipped. If a skipped type keeps a mark already assigned in this run, the result dialog names the duplicate. Merging The tool compares exact stored dimensions within each family. A merge requires every dimension to have a value. Overwrite Existing Marks groups all types of the same size. Preserve Existing Marks keeps different marks separate. In Preserve, a blank type joins a marked group if the size has one distinct mark. Otherwise, blank types of that size form their own group and receive a new mark. In Preserve Existing Marks, the marked type with the lowest element ID is the merge target when the group has marked types. In other groups, the type with the lowest element ID is the target. The tool reassigns instances and deletes duplicate types before renaming the target. Result The run is one undo entry. The result dialog shows the number of types renamed, duplicates merged and types skipped: Organized pier and footing types. • N types renamed • N duplicates merged • N types skipped When types are skipped, the first line reads Organized pier and footing types with skipped types. and the dialog adds up to 5 lines <type id>: <reason>. A type is skipped when Revit rejects its change, for example when the new name already exists. The remaining types are still processed. If a merged type cannot be deleted, the command fails and changes nothing. If a skipped type retains a mark assigned to another type during the run, the dialog adds Duplicate Type Marks. It shows the count and lists up to five examples with the shared mark and both type IDs. Press Ctrl+Z to undo the whole run. Limitations The tool changes the type name, the Type Mark parameter, and the type of merged instances. If the tool must assign a mark and Type Mark is missing, read-only, or uses storage other than text, it skips the whole type. The tool skips a type with a missing or unreadable dimension. The skip details identify the dimension parameter. Linked models are not processed. A stale name on another type in the same family can block a rename. This includes equal-size types with different marks in Preserve Existing Marks. The skipped type keeps its name and mark. Run the tool again once the name is free. If two types hold each other's proposed names, rename one manually to an unused name before rerunning the tool. Different stored dimensions can round to the same text in a type name. The tool keeps these types separate to preserve the exact size of placed foundations. If their marks also match, Revit can reject one of the renames.

user-guide/tools/recordset.html.title: Record Set | dbtools
user-guide/tools/recordset.html.summary: Record Set NAME Record Set - copy Revit host models and their linked files into one package folder SYNOPSIS dbtools > Testing > Record Set DESCRIPTION Record Set copies host RVT files and their file-based links into a target folder. Then it changes the links in the copied hosts to point to the copies. It copies the files as saved on disk, and changes no source file. Click Target Folder... and choose the target folder. Click Add Revit File... and choose host RVT files. With hosts in the list, the button is Add host. In Host Models, set Discipline and Building for each host. Choose < Add new… > to type a name. Read the Preview tree and the Preview Messages. Right-click a DWG in the tree to set its CAD handling. Click Execute. Preview shows the files and folders in the copy plan, including any Xref folders the plan copies. Preview Messages lists files excluded by policy. Execute is available when the preview is up to date, the footer shows Root Allowed, and no message has the severity Block. OPTIONS The Options menu above the preview: Item Effect Manage Disciplines..., Manage Buildings... Add, rename or delete names. A rename or a delete also applies to the hosts and links. Auto-discover CAD Xrefs Find the Xrefs of each DWG, also nested ones, with AutoCAD Core Console. Copy each Xref file into the folder of the DWG copy. Allow CAD repath With discovery, point each Xref in the DWG copies at its copy, with a relative path such as .\Grid.dwg. Both CAD options start on only when Core Console is found. Without discovery, Record Set copies the folders xrefs, xref, refs, ref, external, dwg and cad that are beside the DWG to the same place beside the DWG copy. Names and options last until the window closes. The context menu of a DWG link in the tree: Item Effect CAD: Keep Xrefs The default. Copy the DWG and its Xrefs as the Options menu sets. CAD: Bind All Bind every Xref into the DWG copy, with Core Console. It drops the Xrefs added with Add Xref... from the plan. Bind Type > Bind or Insert For CAD: Bind All, Bind sets AutoCAD BINDTYPE 0 and Insert sets 1. Add Xref... Add a DWG Xref by hand. It is copied beside the DWG copy. REQUIREMENTS Item Rule Target folder Must be in \\fileserver\Projects, a root built into the tool. Otherwise Root shows Blocked. Free space At Execute, the target drive must keep 10 GiB free after the copy. AutoCAD Core Console Needed for discovery, repath and Bind All. Record Set uses the ACCORECONSOLE environment variable, then PATH, then the newest AutoCAD or DWG TrueView. The footer shows the path in ACAD. RESULTS <target>\<building>\<discipline>\<host>.rvt <target>\<building>\<discipline>\Linked Files\<link> a link of one host <target>\Common Linked Files\<link> a link of two or more hosts The default building - and an empty discipline add no folder. A link is common when its full path appears two or more times, even in one host. When two different source files would get one target path, the second gets <name> (2).<ext>, and so on. Execute copies the files, does the CAD work, and then changes the links in the host copies. A copy replaces an existing file in the target and keeps the source timestamps. After a successful run, an alert shows Status: ok and the manifest path. A failed run logs the error and shows an Error banner with Details. Click Details to open the logger window and enable Debug Mode. Record Set adds no Undo step. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Policy denied host file: <name>, and the other Policy denied … messages The file is not copied. The tool excludes .dwl, .dwl2, .tmp, .bak, .lnk and .exe files, and names that match *backup*.rvt, *.old or ~$*. Xref <name> in <dwg> not found: <stored path> The file is not at its stored path or in the DWG folder. The DWG copy keeps the stored path. CAD Xref discovery failed for <name>: <error>. Using fallback. Record Set copies the Xref folders as without discovery, and changes no Xref path. Bind All blocked for <dwg>: … A Block. Every direct and nested Xref must exist and must not be excluded. Fix the Xref, or choose CAD: Keep Xrefs. Total size <bytes> exceeds limit., Total plan item count <n> exceeds limit. A Block. The plan is over 80 GiB or 10,000 items. Put fewer hosts in each package. FILES <target>\.recordset.lock exists while a run is active <target>\.recordset_sentinel marks a Record Set target <target>\_recordset_manifests\<run>.json the run ID, counts and status (ok or failed) LIMITS A failed run does not undo its work. Read the log and the manifest before you run again. If a run stops without removing .recordset.lock, the next run at that target fails. Delete the lock only when no Execute runs on that target. Execute cannot be canceled. Record Set does not copy the links of linked models. Without discovery, or without Allow CAD repath, the DWG copies keep their stored Xref paths. An absolute path still points to the source. Links with a path relative to a Revit library location are not copied or changed. SEE ALSO Getting started, dbtools.RecordSet

user-guide/tools/sgt.html.title: Super Girt Tool | dbtools
user-guide/tools/sgt.html.summary: Super Girt Tool NAME Super Girt Tool - place girts, headers, sills and jambs on one wall SYNOPSIS dbtools > Structural > Super Girt Tool To change a placed system, select one of its members, then click Modify | Structural Framing > Super Girt > Edit SGT Wall. DESCRIPTION Super Girt Tool (SGT) frames one straight wall with horizontal girts. At each opening, it can add a header, a sill and two jambs. It stores the configuration with the members for later edits. The framing band is the height range for girts. It runs from the bottom to the top of a linked wall. On a host foundation wall, it runs from the foundation top to 20'-0" above it. SGT ignores openings in a host foundation wall. SGT shows member elevations from the system's Reference Level. Click Super Girt Tool and pick a straight wall in a linked model. Press Esc at that prompt to pick a straight foundation wall in the host. SGT opens the window and analyzes the wall. It adds girt rows at the base and at each 5'-0" interval within the framing band. With Live Preview on, the progress overlay stays open until the Elevation preview is ready. With Live Preview off, startup keeps the current view and finishes without waiting for the preview. Click Cancel to close SGT without changes. If the preview fails, the window stays open and reports the error. Change the rows and openings. The preview shows the result. Click Place. SGT places the members and closes the window. OPTIONS Type a length as decimal feet (7.5), feet and inches (7'-6 1/2") or inches (18"). A number without a mark is in feet. Layer The exterior face of this wall layer sets the framing line for any wall Location Line setting. The default is the most-exterior structural layer. If none exists, SGT chooses the thickest non-finish layer, or the thickest layer when all are finishes. Ties favor the exterior layer. Offset The distance from the selected layer's exterior face to the framing line. A positive value moves the line toward the exterior. The default orientation seats the section at this plane and keeps the steel on the interior side. The back of an angle girt's long leg sits flat on this plane and faces the exterior. Its short leg is at the bottom and points toward the interior. The toes of a channel jamb point away from the opening. Reference Level Choose the Revit level for a new system. Place and Update use that level for every new girt, header, sill, and jamb in the system. After placement, the picker shows the system's level and is disabled. To change it, delete the system and place it again. The list shows host levels from highest to lowest. Dropdown heights measure from the project base point. A level whose type uses the Survey Point elevation base can show a different height in its level head. The list marks the initial selection and wall base level. When you change the selection and click Place, SGT remembers the pick for new systems in that project. Walls on another datum or more than 8'-0" from the project datum use their own level by default. Changing the picker refreshes the elevation numbers in both grids. The framing geometry stays in place. Girts Each row is one girt at one Elevation, with a Girt Type. When you choose a type of another family, SGT replaces Rotation, Y Justification, Z Justification and Flip with the defaults of that family. To add a row, type an elevation next to Add Girt and click it. The editable Elevation column and the Add Girt input measure from the system's Reference Level. The column names that level, for example Elevation from FFE. Openings On a linked wall, SGT detects doors, windows and wall openings. A linked wall without openings is valid and starts with an empty Openings grid. Add Opening adds one by hand. Center Along is the distance from the wall's left end in the exterior view to the opening center. The grid lists openings from left to right in that view. An opening keeps its default name when it moves to a different position in the grid. The Left Jamb, Right Jamb, Header and Sill boxes turn each member on or off. Bottom Elevation measures from the system's Reference Level and sets the sill and lower jamb ends. Height sets the distance to the header and upper jamb ends. Add Opening places the new opening's left edge at the wall's left end. A girt is split at each opening that it crosses. Click the chevron of a split row to edit each segment. Double-click a row to open Bulk Edit for that row and the other selected rows. To change one column across several rows, select the rows in that grid and commit the edit in one selected row. Elevation in Girts and Center Along in Openings affect only the edited row. A girt elevation applies when you commit the cell or leave the field. When you edit several openings, their changes apply when you commit the row. Held and unframed openings are read-only. Commit or cancel the current opening row before adding, duplicating or deleting rows. The default gap between a jamb face and the end of a header, sill or girt is 1/2". Each jamb extends to the nearest girt that reaches it above and below the opening. At an end with no such girt, the jamb extends to the wall limit. Extend a jamb past its default end to split the added length at girts it crosses. At each split, the two jamb ends clear the girt faces by 1/2". SGT leaves the jamb in one piece at the joint when either member ends at the other. If the next jamb piece would be shorter than 6", the jamb ends 1/2" before the girt face. The preview reports a shortened extension and uses the selected target to recalculate the end when the girt changes. Preview The preview has an Elevation, a Section and a 3D mode. Elevation shows the wall from the exterior, so the wall start is at the right. Left Jamb and Right Jamb are left and right in this view. The horizontal dimension of the selected opening shows Center Along from the wall's left end. In Elevation, drag a member's end handle to a grid line, an opening edge, a wall edge or another member. A drag that ends elsewhere changes nothing. Double-click an end handle to type the gap at that end. An inner end of a split girt can move within the solid span between two opening edges or between an opening and a wall end. A grid must leave at least 6" of span and clear the adjacent jamb flange by 1/2" at the grid line. A typed gap adjusts the end from that line. Changes to wall or opening geometry or framing, grids, girt elevations or extents, or jamb types, orientations or extents can make a saved grid unsuitable. SGT reports when it drops the grid and uses the opening edge and its gap for the split. A short outer pier keeps its anchor and gap so it can return when there is room. Undo and Redo apply to Wall Offset, wall layer, committed grid edits, Bulk Apply, segment flyout edits, opening segment commands, and preview edits. Each action takes one step, even when it changes several rows. Commit or cancel an active opening row and fix invalid fields before using Undo or Redo. Running wall analysis or clicking Confirm in Change Review starts a new draft and clears both stacks. If another plan write supersedes the recorded state, SGT keeps the newer plan. It clears stale history when you try to apply or replay an edit. If SGT recovers from an error after a plan write, it keeps the accepted plan, clears the history, and keeps the window open. Complete or remove blank girt rows and fix invalid grid fields before changing Wall Offset or the wall layer. If a grid edit blocks the change, SGT keeps the rows and restores the accepted wall value. REQUIREMENTS Item Rule Wall A straight, vertical wall in a loaded link, or a straight, vertical host wall whose type has the function Foundation. Girt types Structural Framing types of editable families: C and MC channels, Z shapes, angles and HSS. Opening types Channels and HSS only. Girt end gaps Each girt end with a gap needs an extension parameter that can hold the gap value. SGT knows a shape by the Structural Section Shape, Section Shape or Shape parameter, or by names such as C10X15.3, C Shapes or HSS. It skips a family or type whose name contains joist, girder or truss. SGT prefers C Shapes : C10X15.3 as the default girt type. If that type is not eligible, SGT selects another eligible type. SGT uses a sample type to find default settings for a family. Square and rectangular HSS use separate samples. SGT checks the geometry of each type and solves that type directly if the family settings do not seat it. SGT measures visible steel solids and excludes solids with materials identified as non-steel. It also measures solids with unassigned or unrecognized materials. If every visible solid is excluded, the diagnostic lists the materials and their classes. RESULTS Place creates and tags the members. SGT writes the end gaps of each girt to its Start Extension and End Extension, as negative values. Place and Update check the extension limits for all girt segments before writing any members. Place, Update, and Review Changes commit the active opening row before continuing. A refused edit leaves the grid open for correction. For an edited system, Update writes existing members with a changed curve or instance settings. It creates missing members and deletes extra members. It can also replace a matched member whose location is a bound arc with the straight member from the plan. The member must be editable, have the same family type, and have no tags, hosted elements, joins, or other model relationships. A matched spline, ellipse, unbound line, or other unsupported location stops Update with Update/LocationMissing. SGT places the replacement on the system's Reference Level. It copies Mark, Comments, and IfcGUID, which preserves the member's IFC export identity. It checks that Y/Z offsets, opening member extensions, shared parameter values, and other editable instance values outside SGT's placement settings match. Revit recalculates values such as Exact Weight. Update rolls back if a required value would change or Revit refuses a write. SGT can remove a stored duplicate Mark warning when it verifies that the warning belongs to the source member. When Update recreates a matched member, any Revit warning in the transaction also rolls it back. The only exception is a duplicate Mark warning that names the replacement and the other framing members that share its Mark. The failure reports Revit's warning text and identifies the affected members. Update without matched recreation uses the normal warning handling. Update Summary lists Moved, Recreated, or Deleted for each change. A replaced member has both element IDs and the reason on its Recreated row. Delete System deletes the members and the configuration. Cancel or closing the window rolls back the session. Change Review Change Review opens when you edit a system whose wall or openings changed in the model. Review Changes opens it at any time. Opening Start and End measure from the wall's left end in the exterior view. When you accept a wall with a different base elevation, Move offers to keep each existing girt at the same height above the new base. Rows on the spacing grid follow the grid. Rows at custom heights keep those heights. The suggestion lists old and new elevations relative to the accepted base. After Move, Remove is available for any row above the new top. Keep or Ignore pauses the move. Return to Accept on the same wall to restore it. If SGT infers spacing and the wall is taller, Add offers the next whole intervals after any move. SGT uses the girt gaps at the start of the review and ignores gaps under 6 inches. Rows added during the review keep their chosen height above the accepted base, including after Relink. Decision Effect Accept Use the changed geometry from the model. Keep Keep the geometry of the last placement, or the values that you typed. Ignore Leave the framing as placed. Change Review asks again next time. Confirm saves the decisions and clears the window's Undo history. An information banner confirms the result. Click Update to apply the framing changes. Relink moves the system to another wall and offers a fresh Move if that wall changes the base elevation. Deconstruct removes the SGT data and keeps the members as plain framing. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do [SpecFail/Calibration/NoEligibleFamilies] No eligible structural framing families found … No loaded family meets the REQUIREMENTS. Load one, such as C Shapes. Profile warmup failed for <n> family types; … SGT cannot read the section of these types, so you cannot select them. [SpecFail/Writer/ExtensionCalibrationMissing] SGT needs Start and End Extension calibration for this girt type. Select an eligible girt type and try again. [SpecFail/Writer/ExtensionParamMissing] The girt type lacks the extension parameter for an end with a gap. Use another type, or set that gap to 0. [SpecFail/Writer/ExtensionParamReadOnly] The extension parameter has a fixed value that differs from the required value. Use another girt type or change the gap. [SpecFail/Writer/NoLevels] Place and Update require a level in the host project. [SpecFail/Writer/ReferenceLevelMissing] The host level is unavailable. For Place, reopen SGT and select an available level. For Update, delete the system and place it again. [SpecFail/Writer/ReferenceLevelSetFailed] Revit could not create the framing on the required Reference Level with the requested level offsets. SGT rolls back the write. [SpecFail/Writer/LocationMismatch] Revit placed a member with endpoints or direction that differ from the plan. SGT rolls back the write. [SpecFail/Update/ReferenceLevelChanged] The system's Reference Level was set at placement. Delete the system and place it again to change its level. The project Reference Level pick could not be updated. SGT saved the framing and its Reference Level. The warning gives the reason the project pick could not be saved. Removed SGT data for <n> systems. The old systems' members stay in the model as plain framing. Placing again on those walls can overlap the existing framing. <action>: [<code>] <detail> An action failed. The detail gives the reason. LIMITS An opening splits each girt that crosses it, even with all four members off. To run a girt across, drag the girt's handle at one edge of the opening to the other edge. SGT joins the two pieces into one girt. SGT leaves out a girt piece shorter than 6", with no message. Update overwrites any Start Extension or End Extension value that you type on an SGT girt. If you move or resize a detected opening, its Source becomes Manual, and SGT stops following the opening in the link. A second Super Girt Tool run on a wall places a second system. To change a system, use Edit SGT Wall. A copy of an SGT member keeps its SGT tag, so Delete System deletes it too. If Place or Update fails, the window closes and all changes of the session are lost. SEE ALSO Getting started, dbtools.SGT

user-guide/tools/tdv.html.title: Transfer Drafting Views | dbtools
user-guide/tools/tdv.html.summary: Transfer Drafting Views NAME Transfer Drafting Views - copy drafting views between the model and a library file SYNOPSIS dbtools > dbtools Common > Import From Library dbtools > dbtools Common > Export To Library DESCRIPTION Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) works with a library: a Revit model (.rvt) that holds standard drafting views. An import copies views from a library (the source) into the active model (the destination). An export copies views from the active model into a library. Run a command to open Select Library File. Select a listed file or click Browse for file. In the Transfer Drafting Views window, check the views to copy. Fix each name conflict, then click Transfer Selected. Each click is one transfer. Click Accept and Transfer More or Close Tool in the result. The picker opens even when no saved library is usable. It explains the empty list and offers Browse for file. When valid and invalid paths both exist, it lists the valid files and reports the unavailable count. Cancel the file picker to return to Select Library File. TDV opens the chosen library in the background. Choose an accessible .rvt file from the current Revit version. The active model and its workshared central file cannot serve as the library. A browsed file applies to one transfer window. Add the path in Library Files to use it from the list on later runs. The preview fits the selected view to the pane and matches the exported background. A transparent image corner uses the Revit canvas color. Use the mouse wheel to zoom and drag with the left button to pan. Zoom Extents fits the whole view again. OPTIONS Control Effect View Type: Shows only the source views of one type. Search views Shows the views whose name contains the text, or its letters in the same order. Import? or Export? Includes the row in the transfer. View Name The destination name. Click it to change it. Replace Replaces the destination drafting view with the same name. View Type The destination view type. Retain Original uses the type name of the source view. A checked row has a conflict in these cases: Its name is blank. Another checked row has the same name. The destination has a drafting view with that name, and Replace is off. The check ignores case and leading or trailing spaces. SETTINGS Open dbtools > Settings and select Common on the left. In Library Files, click Add Library File… to choose a file. Select a main file to edit its Alias or choose Set Fallback Path…. TDV uses the fallback when the main file is unavailable. A path is valid when the file exists, ends in .rvt, and was saved in the Revit version that runs. TDV opens no other file, so it never upgrades a library. The list marks any other path Unavailable. When Revit starts, when Settings opens and when you click Save Settings, TDV checks the saved paths. One entry with no valid path turns on the warning Library Paths Invalid. The warning leaves both commands available. Fix or remove the entry, then click Save Settings. Validate Libraries shows the result. RESULTS For each checked view, TDV makes a drafting view or reuses a matching view when Replace is on. It assigns the selected view type and copies the scale, the writable VIEW_DESCRIPTION parameter, the elements and their graphic overrides. Both clearing an existing view and copying into it skip the categories Title Blocks, Viewports, Views, Schedules and Guide Grids. If a view fails, TDV undoes only that view and continues. Per-View Issues in the result shows its code. Cancel on the progress bar undoes the Transfer Selected run, up to the end of the last view. Each import transfer is one Undo step, Transfer Drafting Views. Before closing the library, TDV reactivates your saved project if Revit switched documents. Import closes the library without saving. When the export window closes, TDV saves the library if any transfer added or replaced a view. It also saves if it cannot confirm a commit or rollback. For a workshared library, TDV synchronizes with central and relinquishes all elements. The synchronization comment gives the window's totals. TDV reports save, synchronization and close failures. If TDV cannot reactivate your project, switch back to it in Revit. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do The open document cannot be selected as its own library file. Choose another file. The active model's central file also counts as the open document. The selected library file cannot be used. <reason>. Read the reason and choose an available .rvt file from the current Revit version. DestinationTypeMissing The named type is not in the destination, or Retain Original could not make it. CopyElementsFailed Revit could not copy an element. TDV copies nothing from that view. LIMITS A copied element whose type name exists in the destination uses the destination type. If the destination has no type with the Retain Original name, TDV duplicates the alphabetically first destination drafting view type and gives it that name. The type keeps the properties of the duplicated type. SEE ALSO Getting started, dbtools.TDV

user-guide/tools/vtc.html.title: View Template Comparer | dbtools
user-guide/tools/vtc.html.summary: View Template Comparer View Template Comparer (VTC) compares two view templates in the open project, side by side. For each differing setting you choose which template's value to keep. VTC then writes the result to one of the templates or to a new merged template. It can also save templates to a library and load them back. Synopsis Ribbon: dbtools > Testing > View Template Comparer. The Testing panel is shown when Testing tools is on in the settings (the default). If the project has no view templates, the command shows No view templates found in the document. Usage Select the Left and Right templates. The Swap button exchanges them. Click a value cell in the Settings Comparison tree to choose which side wins for that row. The Inspector has Use Left, Use Right and a clear button for the selected row. For a category row, use Edit Left or Edit Right (in the Inspector, from the row, or from the context menu Edit Override...) to stage a local graphic-override edit. A staged edit is marked Edited. Review the selected rows and eligible staged edits in the Preview tab. Click Process and choose the target. Comparison tree The tree has these top-level groups: Display Settings, Template Parameters, Model Categories, Annotation Categories, Analytical Model Categories, Imported Categories, Filter Overrides, Revit Links and Worksets. Design Options are not listed because Revit exposes document options, not template-specific option visibility. Control Effect Search box Filters rows by name. Filter Limits the rows by configuration (see below). Select Left / Select Right Selects all differing rows shown by the current search and filter, taking the value from that side. Wipe Clears all selections and conflict state. Filters are kept. Reset Resets the search, the view filter and the conflict filter. Expand/collapse button Expands or collapses all groups. Show: All, Conflicts, Success After Process, shows all rows, only rows that failed to apply, or only rows that applied. Context menu Select from Left (with children), Select from Right (with children), Clear selection (with children), Edit Override..., and for Revit links Open Revit Link Settings... and Copy Revit Link Settings To.... A category row or a Filter Overrides row is configured in a template when that template hides it or overrides any of its graphics. A Template Parameters row is configured when the template includes the parameter. The Filter modes are: Configured (default): rows configured in either template. Configured in Left and Configured in Right: rows configured in that template. Rows that are not category, filter-override or template-parameter rows are always shown. Select Left and Select Right select every differing row that the filter and search show. Under Configured in Left, Select Left can therefore select a row that both templates hide when only Right overrides its graphics. Processing that row to the right template keeps it hidden and clears those overrides. Template parameters and display settings Template Parameters show each parameter's inclusion state and, when Revit exposes a writable value, its number, whole number, text or element value. VTC applies a value only when the selected side includes the parameter and the snapshot contains the value. A shared parameter with a captured GUID matches by GUID and data spec. Other parameters with captured identity match by unique name and data spec. Revit ignores the spec version suffix. Older snapshots without parameter identity or value data resolve by unique name and apply only the inclusion state. Element values map by name and kind when project IDs differ. A missing or ambiguous required match is a row conflict. Display Settings include category-kind visibility, View Display Model, background, depth cueing, sketchy lines, shadow and sunlight intensity, plan view range, color-fill schemes, point-cloud overrides and coordination-model overrides. View-range levels, color-fill schemes, line styles and graphics patterns are matched by name when project IDs differ. A missing or ambiguous match is a conflict. VTC matches a silhouette style by its name, kind and category across projects. Revit checks whether the style is valid for the target view. Filter Overrides include each filter's enabled state. Filter Order applies after all filter rows. The target must contain the same filters as the selected order. VTC removes and re-adds them in source order, restores visibility, graphic overrides and enabled state, then checks the order by filter name. Process Process applies the selected rows and the eligible staged edits in one batch. A staged edit is eligible when its row has a selected side and that side is the edited side, or when its row is not in the current comparison. An edit on a visible row with no selected side, or with the other side selected, is not applied. The dialog asks Apply changes to: Option Effect Overwrite <Left name> Writes the selected values into the Left template. Overwrite <Right name> Writes the selected values into the Right template. Create Merged Template Creates a new template named in Template Name:. The name is required. A merged template starts as a copy of the Left template. Settings outside the selected changes keep their Left values. Use Swap to choose the other base. For a row that has a selected side, the target takes that side's captured value. An absent category row resets visibility and graphic overrides. An absent filter row removes that filter. An absent workset or Revit-link row resets that setting to its default. An absent template-parameter row excludes that parameter. A missing optional display member is uncaptured, so VTC skips it. A display setting unsupported by the target view type is a row conflict. VTC always applies the template-parameter inclusion state. It writes a parameter value only when the selected side includes the parameter and the snapshot contains that value. VTC reports a setting it cannot apply as a conflict and continues with other rows. If a category supports graphics changes but refuses the requested visibility, VTC keeps the graphics changes and reports the visibility conflict. An unexpected failure rolls back the batch. Overwriting a template makes one Undo entry. Create Merged Template makes one Undo entry named Create Merged View Template. Imported categories Imported categories (DWG, DXF and other imports) appear under their own Imported Categories group. They use the same compare, edit, preview and process flow as other categories. Revit links Revit link settings appear under Revit Links, grouped by link. Type-level and instance-level link targets are listed separately. VTC lists only the settings that the running Revit version lets add-ins both read and write: Visibility Mode, Linked View, Filters, Nested Links, Object Styles, Color Fill, View Range, Phase, Phase Filter, Detail Level, Discipline. Line Weights appears in live comparisons in Revit 2027. If its new value differs from Visibility Mode, VTC sets Visibility Mode to Custom. VTC applies the supported settings individually. VTC matches links between the two templates by link name and target kind. If two links of the same kind have the same name, VTC stops with an error. Action Effect Open Revit Link Settings... Opens Native Revit Link Settings for one link target. The window always lists all supported settings of that target, even if you opened it from one row. Apply to Template writes the selected settings; it is one undo entry. Copy Revit Link Settings To... Copies the supported settings to other link targets. Linked View is matched by name and view type. Phase and Phase Filter are matched by name in the target linked model. If a name is unavailable because the linked document is unloaded, the raw ID is reused only when source and target reference the same linked model. Otherwise, the copy fails for that target. The copy is one undo entry. A target that cannot accept the settings is reported and the others are copied. Any other failure leaves every target unchanged. Loading a saved template from the library remaps Linked View by name and view type. VTC checks for a unique match even when that row's displayed value already matches the target. It remaps Phase and Phase Filter by name. A missing or ambiguous name is a row conflict. A linked-element ID without a saved name is refused because VTC cannot prove that it identifies the same linked element. When only one template contains the link row, VTC uses that template. When both do and you have not selected a side, VTC asks which template to use. Library The Library tab saves template snapshots to disk and applies them back to a template. Save Template > Left Template, Right Template or Merged Template. An optional name field sets the saved name. When blank, the source template name is used. Load applies the selected saved template to the side chosen in Load to:. It first asks for confirmation, because it overwrites the template's settings in Revit. A delete button removes the selected saved template, and a refresh button reloads the list. VTC stores snapshots under %APPDATA%\dbtools\Cache\VTC\ and creates the folder on the first save. Saved names ignore case and surrounding spaces. Saving under an existing name asks Replace saved template 'X'?. A save without confirmation leaves an existing file in place, including a file another Revit session creates at the same time. VTC accepts snapshots without optional values and rejects missing required data or malformed values. Library Load applies captured rows that differ from the target. It reports the number of applied settings and names rows with conflicts. An expected conflict leaves the other rows eligible for apply. If VTC cannot rebuild the comparison after applying the settings, one warning gives the apply result and the reason the comparison failed. If a save or delete succeeds but the list cannot refresh, VTC shows a warning that names the template. A save or delete that fails shows an error. Result Process, Apply to Template and Copy Revit Link Settings To... each make one undo entry. VTC reports each result in an alert titled View Template Comparer. When Process reports conflicts, use Show: Conflicts to see those rows. Show: Success includes applied rows whose values now match, subject to the current comparison filter. Messages Message Meaning No view templates found in the document. The project has no view templates. VTC does not open. Select two templates to compare first. Left or Right is not selected. Select at least one setting or make a local override edit before processing. Process has nothing to apply. Created merged template '<name>'. <n> operations completed. Create Merged Template finished with no conflict. Applied changes to '<name>'. <n> operations completed. Overwrite finished with no conflict. ... <n> operations succeeded and <n> conflicts were reported. Some rows failed to apply. Use Show: Conflicts. ... No operations succeeded and <n> conflicts were reported. No row was applied. Pending edits cleared because the template pairing changed. Changing Left or Right discarded staged edits. Pending edits cleared because the comparison was rebuilt. Refreshing the comparison discarded staged edits. Pending edits cleared during selection wipe. Wipe discarded staged edits. No category override data is available on the <Left/Right> side for this row. The row cannot be edited on that side. This Revit link exists on both Left and Right. Choose which template should <action>. Choose the template for a link command. Select a specific Revit link row or setting to open. Open Revit Link Settings... needs a link row. No supported Revit link settings were found for this node. The row has no supported link setting. No other Revit link targets are available to copy settings to. Copy Revit Link Settings To... has no target. Applied <n> Revit link settings to <name>. Apply to Template finished. A warning adds the number of settings that could not be applied. Copied Revit link settings from '<source>' to <n> target(s). The copy finished. A warning lists the failed targets. Revit link key '<key>' is ambiguous. Link names must resolve uniquely per target kind and setting. Two links have the same name. Rename one of them. Saved template '<name>' to cache., Saved merged template '<name>' to cache. The library save finished. Replace saved template '<name>'? A saved template has this name. Replace overwrites it. Apply saved template '<saved>' to '<template>'? This will overwrite the current template settings in Revit. Confirm Load. Applied '<saved>' to <template>. <n> settings applied. Load finished. If any rows conflict, the message gives the count and names those rows. No captured settings in '<saved>' differed from <template>. Load found no captured change to write. Deleted saved template '<name>'. The delete finished. Failed to save template: <reason>, Failed to load template: <reason>, Failed to delete template '<name>': <reason> The library action failed. The message gives the reason. ... but the displayed saved-template list could not refresh. The save or delete succeeded; click the refresh button. Limitations VTC compares templates in the open project. It does not compare templates across projects, except through the library. Link settings that Revit does not let add-ins read and write are not shown. VTC cannot apply a background of type None because Revit exposes no public setter for that value. Coordination-model reference-level overrides are not enumerated by the public API used by VTC. Design-option visibility, link Custom-tab tables, and link Visible, Halftone and Underlay values are not available through the supported API path. Create Merged Template copies the Left template, so use Swap to base the merge on the other template.
